Although this is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (go/no-go) reporting group-level whole-brain, multiple-comparison–corrected task-activation maps and adequate participant/task/imaging details, it must be excluded. Primary reasons: (1) The within-participant contrast used is GNG versus fixation (rest), and the study uses fixation as the baseline/control condition rather than an active control task — this meets exclusion criterion E6. (2) The sample includes clinical participants (Tourette disorder) and is not restricted to healthy adults, meeting exclusion criterion E8 for studies not restricted to healthy individuals. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task assessing executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and shown), I9 (task within executive function domain — inhibition), and I10 (reported participant ages, healthy sample info, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (within-participant contrast relative to an active control condition). Full text appears complete and sufficient for screening.

This study reports task-based fMRI of task-switching (an executive function: cognitive flexibility) and includes within-subject contrasts (informatively cued switch > repeat and repeat > switch). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM2 with coordinates and cluster thresholds reported (tables/figures). The paper reports control (healthy) participant demographics, task paradigm, and imaging modality. Although the study also includes a schizophrenia patient group, within-group whole-brain results for the healthy control group are explicitly reported, making the study eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, only between-group contrasts, resting-state baseline only, non-empirical paper, or missing healthy adult within-group maps) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 18–27) using a task-switching paradigm (cognitive flexibility) with within-subject contrasts (switch vs repeat; high vs low reward) and additional contrasts (reward anticipation vs receipt). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed with cluster-level correction and region coordinates/figures reported. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not patient vs control only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials referenced but not required. All inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of the Wisconsin Card Sorting Task (WCST), a canonical executive function (cognitive flexibility/set-shifting) paradigm, conducted in healthy adult participants (N=11; mean age 24, range 18–31). The paper reports within-subject contrasts between WCST event periods and active control trials, performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical analyses (thresholding, random-effects), and provides tables/figures of activation peaks. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function (verbal n-back working memory) in healthy adult controls and includes within-subject contrasts (1/2/3-back vs 0-back active control). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted and reported with coordinates and thresholding; within-group activation maps for the healthy control sample are presented. Participant ages (18–45 for patients, 18–42 for controls), healthy sample status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm details are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines working memory using an audiospatial n-back task (1-, 2-, 3-back) in healthy adults (ages 20–30). It uses within-subject contrasts of memory load (3-back vs 1-back; 2-back vs 1-back), employs voxelwise, group-level whole-brain statistical analyses (voxelwise t-tests, Talairach coordinates reported, figures/tables), and reports participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details. Working memory is an established executive-function domain. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain results are reported; not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; not between-group only; active control used; empirical study with healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines planning (Tower of London) in healthy adults and reports voxelwise activation maps, but it lacks an active control task contrast: baseline is fixation/rest and analyses compare task difficulty levels to fixation and across conditions. This violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline without an active control) and fails inclusion criterion I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control). Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/planning), I7 (group-level voxelwise/statistical maps presented), I8 (whole-brain results described in figures/tables), I9 (task is planning). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no active-control contrast), I10 (participant ages not explicitly reported; only described as undergraduates). Full text is complete for screening.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=45, ages 18–45) using established executive function paradigms (Go/No-Go inhibition; Reward/No-Reward; Loss/No-Loss). It reports within-subject contrasts (No-Go>Go, Reward>No-Reward, Loss>No-Loss) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM2 analyses with voxelwise thresholds and cluster reports; results are presented in figures and tables (coordinates). Participant health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly reported. Thus all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly tests response inhibition (Go/No-go) and a working-memory-loaded variant. It reports within-subject contrasts (No-go vs Go and task vs baseline), uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with correction for multiple comparisons (P≤0.05), and provides tables/figures with coordinates. Participant age, healthy status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, not rest-only baseline, empirical human data, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an event-related fMRI study of cognitive control (task-switching Stroop) in healthy adults (N=12, ages 18–30). It reports within-subject contrasts (instruction: color naming > word reading; response: incongruent > congruent), group-level voxelwise spatial F maps pooled across subjects, and reports coordinates for activations. Imaging modality, participant age/health, and task paradigm are clearly described. Results include whole-brain analyses (spatial F maps) and coordinate reporting. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses active task contrasts, empirical with original human data, participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion E3 met: authors report analyses restricted to preselected regions of interest (motor cortex and preSMA) rather than a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function/inhibition go/no-go task), I6 (within-participant contrast of go vs no-go), I9 (inhibition is an established executive function domain), I10 (participant ages and healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise map), I8 (not applicable because no qualifying whole-brain results reported). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 25.5) using a cued task-switching paradigm (cognitive flexibility/executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., switch vs. repeat, cues vs. targets, targets vs. baseline) including group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with activation foci reported in tables and figures, and small-volume-corrected ROI follow-ups. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, not patient or out-of-range ages, and uses active task contrasts beyond rest). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included.

Full text not provided (only metadata/redirect). The study used fMRI with the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test, so I5 (task-based fMRI) and I9 (task = cognitive flexibility/executive domain) are satisfied. However, I cannot confirm a within-participant contrast against an active control (I6), whether group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported (I7/I8), or whether sufficient participant details (age, healthy-only status) are reported (I10) from the available content. Importantly, the sample includes both healthy volunteers and schizophrenic patients (metadata), meaning the study is not restricted to healthy individuals and therefore meets exclusion criterion E8. Because E8 is met and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded. If a complete full text shows within-group healthy whole-brain maps and results restricted to healthy adults, this decision should be revisited.

This is an fMRI Stroop study of inhibition with within-subject contrasts (Incongruent vs Congruent/Neutral), whole-brain voxelwise group SPM analyses reported (tables/figures), and full reporting of participants (healthy screening), modality, and paradigm. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample includes older adults recruited from a retirement association (participants clearly outside the 18–60 age range). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E8 (includes participants outside 18–60). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite satisfying the inclusion criteria above. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of inhibition (executive function) in healthy adults, reporting within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with coordinates and figures. Participant demographics (n=20, age range 21–37), healthy status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms (Stroop manual and imitation-inhibition) are reported. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References, so the text appears complete for screening purposes.

This study is excluded because it violates two exclusion criteria: E3 and E8. E3: The reported neuroimaging results in the provided full text focus on activity within a scene-selective ROI (left parahippocampal/lingual gyrus) and ROI-based comparisons; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinate results are described in the main text, so it appears to report only ROI analyses. E8: The participant sample includes older adults aged 60–77 years, which falls outside the review’s eligible age range of 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory/executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts: remember vs ignore vs passive), I9 (task within executive function domain: working memory/inhibition), and I10 (participant ages reported, healthy sample, imaging modality and task paradigm described). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no evidence of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study uses task-based fMRI of an inhibition (go/no-go) executive function paradigm with within-subject no-go>go contrasts and reports whole-brain group-level results (tables/coordinates and figures). However, the participant sample consists of boys aged 8–20 years and includes clinical (ADHD) participants and unaffected siblings, i.e., participants are not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E8 (participants outside 18–60 and not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive function task), I6 (within-participant contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (results reported in tables/figures), I9 (task falls within inhibition domain), I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 are satisfied), but exclusion E8 applies, so the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis of healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of executive control (stop-signal task) in healthy adults (ages 22–42). It reports within-subject contrasts (stop vs go; post-stop stop-success vs post-go stop-success), uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM with reported coordinates and thresholding, and provides participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-baseline only, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of inhibition tasks in healthy participants that meets multiple inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) but must be excluded because participants are children/adolescents (mean age ~14.7 years), violating the review’s age restriction (Exclusion E8). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/inhibition), I6 (within-participant contrasts: incongruent vs congruent, on vs off), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps and thresholded Z-stat images), I8 (results reported in text/tables/figures), I9 (tasks in inhibition domain), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable inclusions are satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: E8 (participants outside 18–60 years). Therefore EXCLUDED on grounds of E8.

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (n-back), an executive function domain, in adult participants. It includes within-participant contrasts (1-back vs 0-back, 2-back vs 0-back), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2, provides coordinates/tables and figures, and reports participant demographics and healthy control status. Importantly, the paper presents within-group activation results for the healthy control sample, which satisfies the meta-analysis requirement for healthy adult task activations. Although the study also includes cocaine-dependent participants, the healthy control whole-brain activation maps and relevant methodological details are reported, so inclusion is appropriate. Full text content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Inclusion criteria met: I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10. No exclusion criteria met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task) in healthy adults (N=20, ages 19–43). It reports within-subject contrasts isolating successful vs. unsuccessful inhibition (both contrasted to active go trials) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise mapping (generic brain activation maps with permutation testing and cluster-level inference). Results are reported as coordinates, figures, and time-series plots. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm/methods are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses active task baseline rather than rest, is empirical with original data, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included.

Full text appears incomplete: provided content is largely references and metadata without core article sections (methods, results, group-level analyses). From available information, I5 (fMRI study assessing executive function task-based paradigm) and I9 (task = working memory, an executive function) are satisfied by title/metadata. However I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map), I8 (clear reporting of whole-brain results), and I10 (reported participant age, healthy sample confirmation, imaging modality details, and task paradigm) cannot be confirmed. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly met based on available text. Because essential methodological/results details are missing (fulltext_incomplete=true), I cannot verify all required inclusion criteria, so the study is excluded pending full text. Inclusion met: I5, I9. Inclusion not met/unclear: I6, I7, I8, I10. Exclusion applied: []

This is a task-based fMRI study using the Stroop color-word task (an established executive function/inhibition paradigm) with within-subject contrasts (e.g., incongruent − NI, congruent − NC, blocked contrasts C−N, etc.). Analyses were whole-brain, group-level voxelwise GLMs using FLAME with cluster-wise correction and reported coordinates/tables and figures. Relevant participant information (young adult, college-enrolled controls, age matching, confirmation of healthy control group), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. Although the study includes a clinical ADHD group, within-group task activation maps and contrasts for the healthy control subjects are reported, allowing extraction of healthy adult activations. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria were met.

Although the study meets all methodological inclusion criteria (fMRI task assessing executive functions; within-subject contrasts for N-Back and AX-CPT; group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with coordinates; tasks fall within executive domains; participant/imaging/task details provided), it includes a clinical sample (schizophrenia patients) and is not restricted to healthy adults. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the record must be excluded from a meta-analysis limited to healthy adult task activations.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (2-back) and sustained attention in healthy adults reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 met). However, the contrasts are task versus resting baseline with eyes closed (no active control condition), so it uses rest as the only baseline and therefore violates exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast against an active control) is not met. Full text appears complete.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (age 18–25) using a continuous performance task (CPT‑IP) that targets sustained attention/vigilance — an executive function domain. Analyses include within-participant contrasts (CPT‑IP blocks > active control blocks ‘1 2 3 4’) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses (voxelwise p<0.001, cluster-corrected), with results reported as anatomical loci/coordinates. Participant health status, age range, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (verbal 2-back) in healthy adults (mean age 30). It includes within-subject contrasts comparing the 2-back activation to an active control (0-back/one-letter search), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level ANOVA and conjunction, with tables/coordinates), and provides participant demographics, health-screening, imaging modality, and full methods/results/discussion. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (stop-signal paradigm) in healthy adults (ages 20–33). It reports within-participant contrasts (SST vs NST, UST vs NST, SST vs UST) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99; thresholds and extent reported), with coordinates/tables provided. The task falls under executive function (inhibition). Participant health status, ages, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and violates no exclusion criteria. The full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study using an n-back working memory task in healthy adults (age 21–29) with within-subject contrasts (0-, 1-, 2-back) including a linear memory-load contrast and memory load × stimulus interactions. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed using SPM99 and results (including MNI coordinates and thresholding information) are reported. The task (working memory) is an established executive-function domain. Participant health status, age range, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, baseline includes an active 0-back control, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of task switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility) in healthy adults (n=16, age 21–29). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (task switch vs task repetition—an active control), a group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis with thresholded z-maps and reported coordinates/figures, and provides participant, imaging (3T fMRI), and task-paradigm details. All required inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Exclusion criterion E8 met: the study includes participants outside the 18–60 age range (healthy controls aged 49–70, with some controls up to 70) and the overall sample is not restricted to healthy individuals (Parkinson's disease patients are also included). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study of executive function — Tower of London planning), I6 (within-participant contrasts via parametric analyses across task difficulty and task-level comparisons), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates and figures), I9 (planning is an established executive function), I10 (participant ages, health status of controls, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 were satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of the Stroop task (inhibition), an established executive function. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent > congruent and incongruent > control) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates and cluster significance thresholds. Participant information (healthy native Japanese adults, ages reported, mean age 36, right-handed) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly described. The control condition uses color-neutral words (an active control), and the analyses are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only nor to between-group contrasts. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is incomplete: only references and metadata provided. Cannot verify methods or results. Exclusion decision because core inclusion criteria cannot be confirmed. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none (insufficient information). Inclusion IDs not met / cannot be verified: I5 (cannot confirm PET task-based paradigm assessing executive function despite title suggesting sustained attention), I6 (no information on within-participant contrasts with active control), I7 (no evidence of group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (no coordinate tables/figures described), I9 (task domain not fully verifiable as established executive function despite 'sustained attention' in title), I10 (no participant age/health/sample or task paradigm details reported). fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (go/no-go) in healthy adults (N=6, ages 22–30). It reports within-participant contrasts including go/no-go vs go (an active task control) and go/no-go vs visual control, using group-level voxelwise SPM99 analyses with thresholded whole-brain maps and tables/figures of significant clusters/coordinates. Participant health, age range, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and the task paradigm are described. Although the group analysis used fixed-effects (limiting generalizability), the study nevertheless provides whole-brain, group-level activation maps and coordinate tables suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function (inhibition) activations. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references and appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back) in healthy adults (ages 18–39). It includes within-subject contrasts against an active control (no-back) and rest, and reports a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis (SPM96 group map) with coordinates, figures, and tables describing load-sensitive activations. Task falls within executive function (working memory). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy activation contrasts, and uses an active control). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly probes cognitive flexibility (task switching/Stroop and reverse-Stroop). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs. neutral) and random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and thresholding described. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-state-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy sample). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study using a parametric n-back working memory task (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (0B–1B–2B) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted in SPM (maps, coordinates, and thresholding are described). Healthy adult control participants are included and demographic/task/imaging details are reported. The 0-back serves as an active control baseline. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, event-related fMRI study of executive control tasks (Go/No-go, oddball, response selection) in healthy adults (mean age 22.9, range 18–27). It reports within-participant contrasts and group-level voxelwise random-effects ANOVAs across the whole brain, with tables/figures and coordinate reporting for activation loci. Tasks map to established executive domains (inhibition, selection/monitoring), imaging modality is fMRI, and participant health/age information is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included.

The study meets multiple inclusion criteria for the task-based neuroimaging meta-analysis (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10): it is an fMRI study (I5) using n-back working-memory tasks (I9) with within-participant contrasts (Simple subtraction of active control; I6), reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps/tables/figures for control adults (I7,I8), and provides participant ages, imaging modality, and task details (I10). However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample is not restricted to healthy adults — the study includes children (ages 7–12) and clinical participants with FASD in addition to controls, and thus includes participants outside the 18–60 healthy-adult target and is not restricted to healthy individuals. Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/summary provided). Based on available content: no clear evidence that the task is an established executive function paradigm (I9 not met); no clear within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control is described (I6 not met); no explicit statement of group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps or coordinates is provided (I7 not met); participant age/healthy-sample details and full task paradigm details are not reported here (I10 not met). Exclusion IDs met: none ([]) . Because several required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I9) are not satisfied, the study is excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an executive function domain. Participant sample is healthy adults (n=17, mean age 25.7), imaging modality and paradigm are fully described, and full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses an active control 0-back, empirical human neuroimaging data, healthy participants within 18–60). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

This is an fMRI task-based study of cognitive flexibility (an executive function) in healthy adults (N=20 analyzed; ages 18–32). It reports within-subject contrasts (switch vs repeat) including voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (t maps, cluster correction) and presents coordinates (Table 1, figures). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting-state only, empirical with original human data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and the study should be included.

Meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function meta-analysis: a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults including an executive inhibition paradigm (Go/No-go). Contains a within-participant contrast (No-go vs Go), group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with thresholding and tables/figures of activations, and provides participant age, health screening, imaging modality, and task details. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 25, range 20–31) that directly probes executive functions (task switching, dual-task/divided attention). It reports within-participant contrasts (dual-task vs task-switching; each condition vs baseline) using a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analysis with corrected thresholds and stereotactic coordinates reported in tables and figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are provided. The tasks map onto established executive domains (cognitive flexibility, divided attention). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, active control baseline used, empirical human neuroimaging data, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures). Based on these points the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This fMRI study reports task-based executive function paradigms (Hayling: inhibition/restraint; N-back: 2-back working memory) with within-participant contrasts (inhibition vs initiation; 2-back vs 0-back). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed and thresholded (FDR p<0.05), with coordinates and activation tables/figures reported. Healthy control participants (age 21–47, mean 33.9) are described separately and within-group activation maps for controls are presented, satisfying reporting of participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, supplementary tables) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI executive-task within-participant whole-brain results and reporting requirements for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain) in healthy adults (ages 20–34, plus additional behavioral sample 18–29). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of WM versus an active control condition, uses group-level whole-brain (random-effects, voxelwise) analyses with cluster correction, and provides coordinates/figures describing activations. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete for screening purposes. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although the paper provides a task-based fMRI study of working-memory (an executive function) with within-subject 2-back>0-back contrasts and reports group-level whole-brain maps for healthy controls, it also (a) includes a patient group (not restricted to healthy individuals) and (b) includes participants older than 60 years (controls range up to 63). Therefore it violates E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study of executive function), I6 (within-participant 2-back>0-back contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (results reported as tables/figures of coordinates), I9 (working memory task), I10 (participant ages, healthy-control status, imaging modality, and paradigm described). Inclusion criteria not met: []. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of planning (Tower of London) in healthy adults (n=18, ages 27–43). It reports within-subject contrasts (easy and difficult TOL vs yoked control zero-move condition), and performs group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholded SPM results and coordinate tables/figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI, 1.0T), and task paradigm are reported. The study thus meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses an active control condition, is empirical and limited to healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=10, ages 18–31) investigating planning and set-shifting — an executive function (cognitive flexibility/planning). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and thresholded (reports of coordinate peaks and figures), with within-subject contrasts (e.g., retrieval with shift vs control; retrieval with shift vs retrieval without shift; continuous shift vs control). Imaging modality, participant demographics/health status, and detailed task paradigm are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling assessment against inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=30 males, ages 22–45) using the stop-signal task (inhibition domain of executive function). It reports within-subject contrasts (stop success vs stop error; stop vs go) that isolate inhibitory processes, and performs random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures (with small-volume ROI correction for subcortical regions). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported in detail. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met.

This is an fMRI task-based study of working memory (N-back) in healthy adults (female, 18–25) that reports within-participant contrasts (2-back vs 0-back) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and reported coordinates. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study of the Stroop color-word task in healthy adults (ages 20–45). It assesses an executive function (inhibition/cognitive control) using a task-based paradigm and reports within-participant contrasts (infrequent incongruent vs congruent trials; also an inverse Stroop contrast). Group-level, whole-brain composite statistical maps (voxelwise analyses, thresholded maps and ROI coordinate reporting) are presented and compared across subjects. Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses an active control, empirical human imaging, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly manipulates executive resources (working memory and on-line planning/decision-making) during sentence disambiguation. Analyses are within-subject contrasts (e.g., less-consistent vs more-consistent; with WM phrase vs without WM phrase) and use group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise SPM2 analyses with reported cluster coordinates and tables/figures. The study reports participant age range and healthy status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm. The baseline/control used for contrasts (initial unbiased phrase) is an active task baseline rather than rest. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task) in healthy adult participants (ages 22–42). It uses task-based executive function paradigms (inhibition) and reports within-subject contrasts (successful vs failed stop trials). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected maps, coordinates, and figures/tables). Participant demographics, health status (healthy), imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task methods are provided. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation maps in healthy adults within age range). Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a non-empirical commentary/review article summarizing fMRI/PET work (e.g., Furey et al.) rather than an original empirical human neuroimaging study. It does not present methods, participant data, task-based within-subject contrasts, or group-level whole-brain activation maps. Therefore it fails to meet the required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criterion E7 (non-empirical paper without original human neuroimaging data). Full text appears complete (commentary content present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of cognitive control (modified Stroop) in healthy adults (N=12, ages 19–29). The design includes within-participant contrasts isolating perceptual and response conflict (congruent vs incongruent conditions) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (thresholded p<0.05 FDR), with coordinates/tables reported. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are described. The task fits established executive-function domains (inhibition/attentional control). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), analyses are task-evoked contrasts within healthy participants, and an active task contrast (incongruent vs congruent) is used rather than resting baseline only. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study uses a task-based stop-signal paradigm probing response inhibition (an executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (StopInhibit vs Go) and other Go/Stop contrasts, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (thresholded and cluster-corrected) and reported activation coordinates. Participant demographic information (healthy, age 18–39), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. The task falls within the inhibition domain of executive function. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts in healthy adults aged 18–60, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study uses task-based fMRI with a Stroop inhibitory-control paradigm and reports within-subject contrasts and voxelwise group maps in healthy comparison subjects, satisfying inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (includes pathological gamblers) and the reported age range spans 18–65 years (exceeding the 18–60 range). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E8 (participants outside 18–60 or not restricted to healthy individuals). Although within-group healthy activation maps are reported, E8 requires restriction to healthy adults and/or age within 18–60, so the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI, task-based study of response inhibition (Go/No-Go) in healthy adults that reports within-subject contrasts (No-Go vs Oddball/Go) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy right-handed men aged 20–42 (within 18–60). Imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant information are reported. An active control (Oddball) was used rather than rest/fixation. Results are reported as whole-brain maps and peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, empirical human neuroimaging data in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of inhibition (numerical Stroop) with within-subject contrasts (maximal vs minimal interference) and group-level whole-brain analyses, it should be excluded because participant samples fall outside the meta-analysis’ required age range and are not restricted to healthy adults. Specifically, the study tests elderly participants (mean ages ~68–70) including a clinical MCI group and age-matched controls, violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/inhibition), I6 (within-participant contrasts of interference effects), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I9 (task maps to executive/inhibition domain), I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality, and paradigm described). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDE due to E8 (participants outside 18–60 and not restricted to healthy adults).

This is a methods/protocol paper describing the counting Stroop fMRI task and summarizing validation work. It meets inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI task probing cognitive control), I6 (within-subject interference vs neutral contrast), I9 (task falls within executive function/inhibition domain), and I10 (states healthy adult sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm). However, the full text does not present original group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps or coordinate tables/maps attributable to this specific article; instead it is largely procedural/anticipatory and cites prior validation studies. Therefore it does not satisfy I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map) and falls under exclusion E7 (non-empirical/methods-only paper without original human neuroimaging data). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an fMRI study of an established executive function task (n-back working memory) that reports within-subject contrasts of 1-/2-/3-back versus an active baseline (0-back), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and cluster coordinates/tables and figures, and reports participant/sample details including healthy control group and demographic matching. This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 18–36). It reports within-participant contrasts (successful stop vs. go) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2), with coordinates, tables, and figures describing whole-brain results. This is an fMRI study using the Stroop task (an established inhibition/cognitive control executive function task) with task-based within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs congruent). Although the sample includes first-degree relatives (one relative had schizotypal personality disorder), the study provides within-group whole-brain activation maps for healthy control participants, which satisfy the requirement for healthy adult task activations. Full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not violate exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive function (N-back working memory, WCST, CPT) in healthy adults. It reports within-subject 2-back > 0-back contrasts using SPM2, with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (coordinates and FWE-corrected results, plus figures and tables). Participant ages, healthy status screening, imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigms are explicitly reported. The 0-back condition is an active control. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=18, ages 18–40) using a Stroop task (inhibition/cognitive control). It reports within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs congruent, congruent+incongruent > neutral) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with thresholding and reported coordinates/tables/figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are all described. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function activations and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function (n-back working memory) paradigm, with within-participant contrasts using an active control (1- and 2-back > 0-back). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps are reported for healthy subjects (thresholds, cluster-correction, and peak coordinates provided). Healthy control sample characteristics (male, right-handed, age 18–55) and imaging modality and paradigm are described. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only results, connectivity-only analyses, absence of within-group healthy activations, or use of rest-only baseline) are met. This is an fMRI task-based study of cognitive control/executive processes (thought/image suppression, erasing/updating, imagining) in healthy adults (mean age 25.7). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not rest-only baseline, empirical human fMRI data, healthy adult sample). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an original, event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=10, mean age ~26) using Stroop and Simon tasks that index inhibition/cognitive control. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of incongruent vs. congruent trials (active control), voxelwise/pixel-wise group-level whole-brain statistical maps (t-maps, concordance analyses), and detailed methods, results, and time-course analyses. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are all clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus the study meets all meta-analysis inclusion criteria for task-based executive function whole-brain fMRI in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (N-back working memory) in adult participants. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (2-back vs 0-back), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM random-effects analyses with reported coordinates/figures/tables, and provides participant demographic and health-screening information (cognitively intact, clinically unaffected siblings and matched healthy controls; ages reported in the 30s). The imaging modality (BOLD fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are described. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, figures, references).

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive flexibility (set switching) in healthy adults (N=20, ages 20–43). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (switch vs repeat trials), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis (permutation-based GBAM, cluster-level inference), and presents results in text, table, and figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described. The task falls under executive function (cognitive flexibility). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, empirical healthy-sample study with active control). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and conclusions. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: the participant sample is not restricted to healthy individuals (it includes a clinical group of adults with high-functioning autism). Included criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported), I9 (task falls within executive function domain — working memory), and I10 (participant age, healthy control details, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion I6 is not clearly satisfied: although the design included 0-/1-/2-back conditions, the paper reports voxelwise group maps primarily versus fixation and ROI-based ANOVAs rather than a clearly reported whole-brain within-participant contrast of the executive condition relative to an active control (e.g., 2-back > 0-back). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded for the meta-analysis focused on healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive functions (SART) in healthy adults (ages 19–37). It includes within-participant contrasts (Random vs Fixed SART) isolating inhibition/conflict, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction) and provides coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details are reported in the methods. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (nogo vs saccade), an executive function domain. It reports within-participant contrasts (nogo vs saccade; instruction and response contrasts), and group-level whole-brain mixed-effects voxelwise statistical maps with cluster coordinates and tables. Participant sample is healthy adults (n=11, ages 21–35) and imaging modality and task paradigm are fully described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task study of planning vs memory that uses within-subject contrasts against an active control and reports group-level whole-brain analyses; tasks fall squarely into executive domains (planning/inhibition). However, the full text provided does not report participant ages or age range, which is required by inclusion criterion I10. All other inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I10 (participant age information). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion) so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study (n-back auditory WM) investigates working memory load, an established executive function, in healthy adult participants using a task-based within-subject design. The paper reports group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (second-level SPM2), whole-brain exploratory results (reported at pFDR < .05) and ROI small-volume corrected analyses, with activation coordinates and tables/figures provided. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study tested healthy young adult volunteers on established executive tasks (two-back working memory and the WCST for cognitive flexibility) using within-subject, task vs active-control contrasts. The authors computed group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (normalized, smoothed, thresholded) and report coordinates and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participant health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are described in the full text. The full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Minor uncertainty arises from the lack of exact ages (reported only as 'young'), but the sample is clearly healthy adult volunteers. Therefore inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the participant sample comprises nicotine-dependent cigarette smokers (not a healthy, non-clinical adult sample), violating exclusion criterion E8. Additionally, the reported neuroimaging results are based on small-volume (a priori ROI) masked voxelwise analyses rather than an unmasked group-level whole-brain task activation map, which meets exclusion criterion E3 and fails inclusion criterion I7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — Stroop), I6 (within-participant contrast: incongruent>congruent), I9 (task falls within executive function domain), and I10 (participant ages, health status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task-evoked map reported). Full text appears complete for screening.

Exclusion criterion E8 is met: the sample includes participants outside the 18–60 age range (ages 22–75, with group mean 57.1 and included participants up to 75 years). Although the study otherwise satisfies the review inclusion criteria — I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive/inhibition task), I6 (within-participant incongruent vs neutral contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (coordinates and figures reported), I9 (Stroop = inhibition/cognitive control), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy status screening, imaging modality and task paradigm) — the age inclusion boundary is violated. Therefore the study must be excluded. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion IDs not met: none. Exclusion IDs met: E8. Exclusion(s) met: E8 — participants are aged 50–70 years, which falls outside the review age range of 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function: working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts: manipulation/retrieval vs maintenance and vs motor control), I7 (group-level whole-brain random-effects analysis reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and illustrated), I9 (task falls within executive domain: working memory), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: None (all required inclusion criteria were reported/satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because E8 is violated (age outside 18–60), the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

Exclusion based on E3: the study does not provide a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Although fMRI contrasts (Difficult vs. Control; Easy vs. Control) and individual subject SPM t-maps were computed, group analyses were performed on manually defined VOI spatial-extent measures (percent suprathreshold voxels) using t-tests rather than a voxelwise whole-brain group map. Additionally, image acquisition covered only eight axial slices of the superior brain (not whole-brain coverage). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — planning/Tower of London), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs an active control condition), I9 (task falls in executive domain — planning), I10 (participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore the study is excluded under E3.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts (one- and two-back vs zero-back active control), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps using permutation-based cluster inference. Participant details (healthy adults aged 21–29), imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI), and task paradigm are all clearly reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract available). Based on the abstract: meets I5 (fMRI study of cognitive interference/executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast: interference vs. neutral), and I9 (task maps to inhibition/cognitive interference). However, I cannot confirm I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map) because the abstract only reports group activity without specifying whole-brain voxelwise results or tables/coordinates/figures. I10 is not fully satisfied because participant ages are not numerically reported (only described as "adult volunteers"). No exclusion criteria (E3-E8) are clearly met. Because not all inclusion criteria can be verified from the provided content, I exclude the study pending full-text review.

This is a review/methods paper (non-empirical) that summarizes and illustrates covariance-based analyses using prior PET/fMRI studies but does not report original empirical, within-participant task vs active-control contrasts or group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps for a healthy sample. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E7 (non-empirical paper). Inclusion criteria not met include: I5 (not an original fMRI/PET study assessing executive function), I6 (no within-participant contrasts reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps provided), I8 (no qualifying whole-brain results presented), I9 (although working-memory/executive topics are discussed, no original task data are reported), and I10 (no participant/sample imaging details for an original empirical study). No inclusion criteria are satisfied by this article as the study itself is a review/methods paper.

This study is a PET task-based neuroimaging experiment using a working-memory (N-back) paradigm (executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (2-back minus 0-back active control), provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and thresholded activation maps with stereotactic coordinates and figures, and gives participant demographics (ages, healthy control status), imaging modality (H2(15)O PET), and full methods/results/discussion. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes within-group healthy control activations (so E5 not met), reports whole-brain task activations (E3/E4 not met), uses an active control (not rest-only; E6 not met), is empirical human imaging data (E7 not met), and the healthy control subgroup falls within the adult age range (E8 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Full text appears incomplete (only redirect/metadata shown). Based on title/metadata, study involves patients with schizophrenia and olanzapine modulation of the default mode network, not healthy adults performing executive function tasks. Exclusion IDs met: E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (no evidence of task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive task vs active control), I7 (no confirmed group-level whole-brain task-evoked map), I8 (no reported whole-brain task results), I9 (task not in executive-function domains), I10 (does not report a healthy sample). Full text incomplete=true; cannot confirm methods/results. Decision: EXCLUDE due to E8 and failure to meet required inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (stop-signal task), an executive function domain (inhibition). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., StopSuccess vs StopFailure; StopSuccess vs Go with 0% stop probability) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with cluster-level inference and reported coordinates/figures. Participant information (n=24, ages 19–26, healthy) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, baseline includes active Go trials, and sample is healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This study is an fMRI Stroop (inhibition) task and reports group-level whole-brain activation maps for healthy controls and TBI patients, with participant ages, modality, and task described. However, it does not include a within-participant contrast against an active control condition—task activation is contrasted against rest/fixation only. Additionally, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (it explicitly includes TBI patients), which conflicts with the review’s focus on healthy adults. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E6 (rest/fixation as only baseline) and E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) with simultaneous EEG. It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., Load 7 vs Load 3; comparisons across loads and to Load 0 baseline), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses in SPM5 with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level correction, and provides participant demographics (20 healthy right-handed adults, age 18–28), imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or non-healthy/out-of-range participants) are met. Thus all required inclusion criteria are satisfied and the study is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain. It reports within-participant contrasts (2-back vs 1-back for Category and Location), uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction, and presents results in figures/tables. Participant age, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported (healthy adults, 18–30). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (visual target switching/working memory) in healthy adults (N=9, ages 19–42). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., target switching vs. non-switching) and group-level voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses with voxel-wise FDR correction and tables/figures of coordinates and maps. Imaging modality, participant health/ages, and task paradigm are clearly described. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Although this is an event-related whole-brain fMRI study of executive function (interference suppression and response inhibition) with within-subject contrasts (incongruent>neutral, no-go>neutral), clear group-level whole-brain voxelwise results, coordinate reporting, and full reporting of participant demographics and healthy status, the sample includes children (ages 8–12) in addition to adults. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the 18–60 years range or not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I-criteria were reported), but exclusion E8 is met because participants fall outside the 18–60 age range.

The study is an fMRI investigation of an executive function task (n-back working memory) in healthy adults (mean age 36.3, range 25–51). It reports within-subject contrast analyses (parametric modulation of BOLD by n-back difficulty) and group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level random-effects maps (SPM2) with FDR correction; results are presented as maps, tables, and coordinates. Task falls within working memory (an established executive domain). Participant/sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), this is task-evoked fMRI (not resting-state or connectivity-only), within-group contrasts in healthy participants are provided, and participants are within the 18–60 age range. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (stop-signal task) in healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age 20). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (GO/STOP vs GO ONLY; correct vs incorrect STOP trials; parametric modulation of STOP likelihood) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (thresholding, coordinates, figures, and tables). Participant health status, age, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-state-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical sample). Full text is complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This is an empirical fMRI Stroop study of cognitive control in healthy adults with within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and full reporting of participants, ages, modality, and paradigm (meets I5, I6, I9, I10). However, all task activation statistical inference was carried out within an a priori ROI mask (BAs 24/32, 8/9/46, 7/40) using SPM2 and significance was reported within these ROIs; no whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task-evoked activation map is reported. Because the paper reports only ROI-constrained task results (and not whole-brain voxelwise activation maps), it violates exclusion criterion E3 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (N=43, age 18–30) using the Stop-signal task (inhibition), an established executive function domain. It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., StopInhibit–Go, StopInhibit–Fixation, Go–Fixation) comparing task conditions (active control Go), and reports group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (second-level contrasts for the entire group; search region = 137,514 voxels). Although primary statistical inference is reported within anatomically defined ROIs with small-volume correction, the methods describe whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis and results include MNI coordinates and statistical maps/figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state-only, empirical with human data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study examines inhibitory control (go/no-go), reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (PLS) with tables/figures and coordinates, and provides participant demographics and healthy screening. However, it includes older participants aged 60–80 years, i.e., participants outside the eligible 18–60 age range for this review, violating exclusion criterion E8. Therefore, despite meeting all inclusion criteria (I5–I10), the study must be excluded because it includes participants older than 60. (a) Exclusion met: E8. (b) Inclusion met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. (c) Inclusion not met: none.)

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory in healthy adults (N=14) using a Sternberg paradigm, which falls under executive function. The study reports within-subject contrasts of the experimental (working memory) condition versus an active control task, and group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses (one-sample t-tests) were performed and thresholded, with results reported in tables/figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and full task/method details are provided. Although reporting emphasized ROIs (foci reported only within predefined ROIs), a whole-brain voxelwise group analysis was conducted, satisfying the whole-brain map requirement. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present.

This fMRI study reports task-based whole-brain activation during an established executive-function task (Chinese-character Stroop; inhibition/action-monitoring). It includes within-participant task-vs-control contrasts and presents group-level, voxelwise whole-brain results for the normal control group (one-sample t-test; fixed-effects maps and tables/figures), with between-group random-effects analyses also reported. Participant demographics and screening for healthy controls are described; imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are fully detailed. Age range reported for patients is 18–60 and groups did not differ in age; healthy control status is confirmed. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met, and no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related fMRI study of planning (Tower of London) in healthy adult participants (n=17, ages 21–39) that reports within-participant contrasts of the executive/planning task versus two active control conditions. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (random-effects, p<0.05 FWE-corrected) with activation coordinates in tables and figures. The study clearly reports participant demographics, imaging modality and task paradigm. The task falls within an established executive-function domain (planning). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not using rest/fixation as the only baseline, and this is original empirical human neuroimaging data with participants in the 18–60 range. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (female, age 19–33) using a Stroop paradigm that targets executive function (inhibition/conflict). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent trials; ATD vs BAL) and behavioral measures. Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (cluster-corrected; results reported in tables/figures and coordinates), and ROI analyses are supplementary — satisfying whole-brain reporting. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text content including introduction, methods, results, and discussion is provided. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

This fMRI paper investigates amygdala responses to anticipation of pain while subjects perform a Continuous Performance Task (CPT) as an active coping manipulation. Although imaging, healthy adult sample, ages, and task details are reported (I10), the study does not meet the meta-analysis requirements: (1) the primary focus is emotional/pain anticipation rather than an executive-function/cognitive-control task contrast (fails I5 and I9); (2) it does not provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation map for an executive-function contrast — results are reported as ROI-based amygdala analyses (meets exclusion E3 and fails I7/I8); and (3) there is no within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control condition as required (fails I6). Therefore the study should be excluded from a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This study reports task-based BOLD fMRI in healthy adults performing an N-Back working memory task (executive function). It includes within-subject contrasts (2-Back vs 0-Back active control), group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with voxelwise results and reported coordinates (with correction and small-volume results), and provides participant demographics and imaging/task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not patient-group-only, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

Although this fMRI study assesses an executive-domain task (sustained attention/CPT-IP) and reports whole-brain, group-level, within-subject activation maps for healthy participants, it also includes a clinical sample (unmedicated bipolar patients) and is not restricted to healthy individuals. Exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the age range 18–60 years or not restricted to healthy individuals) therefore applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive/cognitive control task), I6 (within-participant contrast of task vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), I9 (task falls in executive domain: vigilance/sustained attention), I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore exclude per E8.
