It reports within-subject contrasts (anti vs pro, anti vs nogo, pro vs nogo) and mixed-effects group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with thresholding and cluster correction; results are provided in figures and tables (coordinates). Participants are healthy adults (ages 22–33, mean 26). Imaging modality (fMRI) and full task paradigm are described. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a PET study of a continuous performance (vigilance) task and includes healthy control participants, but it does not provide the required within-participant task vs active-control contrast nor whole-brain, voxelwise group-level task activation maps. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (analyses are ROI-based using 60 rectangular ROIs with no whole-brain voxelwise results reported) and E5 (the paper focuses on patient vs control comparisons and predictors of treatment response without presenting a within-group task activation contrast for healthy participants). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study assessing an executive function task), I9 (task falls under vigilance), I10 (participant ages, healthy-control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of task relative to an active control condition), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of a 2-back working memory (executive) task with within-subject contrasts (digits vs letters/faces) and random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses reported. However, the sample includes 8-year-old children in addition to adults (study reports child and adult groups), i.e. participants outside the 18–60 year age range. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (includes participants outside 18–60). Although adult within-group results are reported, the study population is not restricted to healthy adults 18–60, so it does not meet the review's age restriction. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a visuospatial n-back working memory task (an executive function). The paper reports within-subject task contrasts (memory-load-dependent/linear n-back contrasts using 0-,1-,2-,3-back blocks), group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99, p_corrected<0.05) with coordinates and figures, and provides participant demographics and health status. The task falls within the working memory domain. Full methods, results, and discussion are presented, so the full text appears complete. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 23–47) directly probes initiation and inhibition — executive function domains (initiation, inhibition). It includes within-subject contrasts between task conditions (e.g., ballistic vs smooth for initiation; stepwise vs ballistic or smooth for inhibition), where smooth movement served as an active control. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster-thresholded maps and stereotactic coordinates), and results are described in the text and figures/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not patient-only contrasts, and participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for this review.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory in healthy adults with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps and reported coordinates, it does not present at least one within-participant contrast of the executive function task relative to an active control condition. The study includes visually guided saccade (VGS) trials but states these were not considered in the main statistical analyses; main analyses contrast task time courses against fixation/ baseline and compare short vs long delay conditions, so no clear task vs active-control within-subject contrast is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI working memory task), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (coordinates/tables reported), I9 (working memory/executive function domain), I10 (participant age/healthy sample/imaging modality/task described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of task vs an active control condition reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are clearly violated based on the provided full text. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10: it is an fMRI task study of executive function (working memory manipulation) (I5); contains within-participant contrasts including manipulation > maintenance (I6); reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses and an exploratory whole-brain Age×Task interaction analysis with coordinates/tables/figures (I7, I8); the task falls within an executive function domain (working memory) (I9); and participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported (I10). However, exclusion criterion E8 applies: the sample includes older adults aged 65–82, i.e., participants outside the 18–60 age range specified by the review. Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded. No other exclusion criteria were met. Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study used rest/fixation baseline (task conditions were modeled against baseline/rest) and did not include an active control condition for the reported whole-brain group contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (rest/fixation used as only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function: verbal working memory), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps reported and cluster-thresholded), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described/reported), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive function task relative to an active control condition; primary contrasts are versus rest/baseline). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study examines working memory (an executive function) using a delayed recognition task for faces and voices with an active scrambled sensorimotor control. It reports within-subject contrasts (face vs control, voice vs control, direct face vs voice) and group-level voxelwise statistical maps (Z-maps, whole-brain analyses with multiple-comparison correction), and provides participant demographics (ages 18–34), healthy sample screening, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigms. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical paper, or non-healthy/out-of-range participants).

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (working memory load and distractor interference). It reports within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; load × congruency interactions) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with thresholds and cluster results. Tasks fall within executive domains (working memory, inhibition/response control). Participant demographics (healthy adults aged 18–35), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (not truncated). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-state baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

Full text is incomplete (only page redirect/landing content available). Cannot verify methods or results. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met/confirmed: I5 (unable to confirm fMRI/PET task details), I6 (cannot confirm within-participant contrasts vs active control), I7/I8 (cannot confirm presence of group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps or coordinate tables/figures), I9 (task classified as working memory likely but not verifiable), I10 (participant ages, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm not fully reported in the available content). Because core article content (methods, results) is missing, the study cannot be assessed against all inclusion criteria and is therefore excluded pending full text. Full text incomplete: true.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function) in healthy adults (n=12, ages 19–34). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (update > cued maintenance; memory blocks > category discrimination control), and performs group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction; results and coordinates are described and referenced (including supplementary tables). Participant health status, ages, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not a between-group patient study, uses active control conditions, is empirical with original human neuroimaging data, and participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of working memory/attentional control (three-back task with lure vs non-lure trials), sampling healthy adults (age 18–37). Analyses include within-participant contrasts between task conditions (lure vs non-lure; event-related trial-type effects) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported cluster coordinates (Table 1 and figures). Task is an established executive-function paradigm (working memory/interference control). Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria relevant to the meta-analysis (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10).

Although this is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants using a working memory (MOPT) paradigm and reports within-subject contrasts and group-level whole-brain analyses, it fails to meet all inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive/cognitive control domain), I6 (within-participant contrasts: MT-MC and ST-SC), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results described and tabulated), I9 (task falls within working memory/executive function domain). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 — the full text does not report participant ages or an explicit age range; while health status and imaging modality and task paradigm are described, age information required by I10 is missing. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because not all inclusion criteria are satisfied (specifically I10).

This randomized, double-blind study used task-based fMRI in healthy adults (ages 40–60) to examine cognitive tasks that map onto executive function domains (spatial working memory and verbal memory). The imaging analyses include within-participant contrasts that serve as active-control contrasts (5-dot minus 3-dot spatial working memory; verbal old vs new), and group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps are reported with stereotaxic coordinates (Table 3 and figures). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task contrasts, healthy adults within age range). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E8 applies: the study includes participants outside the target age range (participants aged 33–75, i.e. up to 75 years) and is not restricted to healthy individuals (contains premutation carriers with FXTAS and unaffected premutation carriers as well as healthy controls). The study otherwise meets multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function — verbal working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast: Encoding vs Rehearsal+Retrieval), I7 (group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses and cross-group maps), I8 (whole-brain results reported/described and tables/figures), I9 (working memory is an established executive domain), and I10 (participant ages, healthy/control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Due to violation of E8, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60.

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive function (task-switching cognitive control) in healthy adults (N=19). It includes within-subject contrasts (shift vs repeat; high vs low response and stimulus conflict), conducted as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses with reported thresholds and coordinates (whole-brain results and ROI follow-ups; supplemental data referenced). Participant age/health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm and methods are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an event-related fMRI study of executive function (proactive interference/inhibition within a modified WCST) in healthy adults. It meets inclusion criteria: (I5) imaging modality fMRI and task-based executive control (inhibition/cognitive flexibility); (I6) within-subject contrast of interest (control vs. release trials; control minus release) isolating inhibition; (I7) group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM2 with reported thresholding and FDR correction and coordinate tables/figures; (I8) whole-brain results are reported as figures and coordinate tables and described in text; (I9) task falls within cognitive flexibility/inhibition executive domains; (I10) participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported (N=78, age 20–28, healthy). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical paper, or out-of-range/clinical sample). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion and references (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Full text is complete and reports a task-based fMRI group, whole-brain analysis of healthy adults performing a category learning/matching task. However, the task is a perceptual category-learning paradigm rather than a canonical executive function task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning), and therefore does not meet the review’s domain inclusion (I5, I9). Critically, the main within-subject contrasts compare the task to central fixation (rest/fixation baseline), which violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as only baseline). The paper does satisfy I7 (group-level whole-brain maps reported), I8 (results clearly described), and I10 (participant age/health/imaging and paradigm reported), but fails I5, I6, and I9. Thus it must be excluded.

This fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive control/executive processes (working memory updating and visual search) (I5); includes a within-subject contrast of an executive task (modified Digit Symbol Test) versus an active control task (drawing a single symbol) (I6); reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects and fixed-effect parametric analysis) with coordinates and thresholding described (I7,I8); the task maps onto established executive domains (working memory/updating, attentional control) (I9); and reports participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm details (I10). No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain results reported, not ROI-only; active control included; healthy adult sample aged ~21.6). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore I include this study in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that includes a canonical executive-function task (2-back working memory) and reports within-subject task contrasts. The paper presents group-level, whole-brain analyses and group fMRI maps (figures and text) for the 2-back task, and reports participant ages (mean 27, range 22–52), healthy sample status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm details. The 2-back design uses alternating task and active-control epochs (including a TAP response instruction during control epochs), supporting a within-participant contrast against an active control condition. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study of working memory and visuospatial tasks in healthy adults (I5, I6, I9, I10 satisfied). However, the functional imaging for the main 1.5T experiment was restricted to the cerebellum (limited field-of-view) and the reported voxelwise group analyses focus on cerebellar ROIs/subregions rather than whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps. The supplementary 7T data also report cerebellar coverage only. Therefore criterion I7 (at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map) is not met, so the study cannot be included in a whole-brain meta-analysis. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I9, I10. Inclusion IDs not met: I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (age 18–37) that examines executive function domains including working memory and associative memory. The paper reports within-participant task contrasts with active control conditions (STERN: novel vs practiced/RT control; PMT: associative learning vs simple classification). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) statistical maps were generated and reported (thresholded whole-brain maps, ROIs derived from these contrasts; results presented in figures/tables), and coordinates/ROIs are described. Participant demographics, healthy-sample screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation contrasts, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

Study used fMRI and reported group-level whole-brain results and healthy adult participants; however the key executive contrast (blink inhibition) was analyzed versus a closed-eye baseline (rest) rather than an active control, and no within-participant contrast of the inhibition task against an active control condition is reported. This violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline) and inclusion criterion I6 is not met. Other inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI with inhibition component), I7 (group-level whole-brain analysis), I8 (coordinates/figures reported), I9 (task maps onto inhibition domain), I10 (participant and imaging details reported). Therefore EXCLUDED.

While this is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) with group-level whole-brain maps and within-subject contrasts across difficulty levels, the full text as provided does not report ages for the healthy volunteer sample. The inclusion criteria require relevant information about participant age in addition to healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm. Age information for the nine healthy participants is absent in the provided text, so inclusion criterion I10 is not satisfied. All other inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9) are met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This full-text fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults. It uses a task-based fMRI paradigm (2-back working memory) (I5), includes a within-participant 2-back versus 0-back contrast (active control) (I6), and reports group-level voxelwise SPM analyses with whole-brain, random-effects results (voxel-based analyses with small-volume correction) presented as coordinates and figures (I7,I8). The task is an established executive function (working memory) task (I9). Participant age, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported (I10). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext complete). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only reporting, connectivity/rest-only analyses, between-group-only contrasts, passive baseline only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/non-healthy-only samples) are met. Therefore the study is suitable for inclusion.

This is an empirical PET and fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 21–41) using the Tower of London planning task (an executive function). It includes within-participant contrasts (active problems vs zero-move baseline) and parametric (difficulty) regression analyses. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported using SPM99 with statistical parametric maps and coordinate tables/figures. Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modalities, and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports original task-based fMRI data in healthy young adults (median age 22, range 18–25) using an n-back working memory task (executive function). The authors performed within-subject contrasts (two-back vs active ‘x-target’ baseline) and second-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported cluster coordinates and thresholds. Task paradigm, participant health status, age range, and imaging modality are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task activations, uses an active baseline, empirical fMRI data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of visual working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 22–36). It includes within-subject contrasts (WM vs fixation-control and correct vs incorrect trials), reports group-level whole-brain voxel-wise maps (fixed-effects group Z maps) supplemented by random-effects ROI analyses, and presents results in figures/tables. Imaging modality, participant health status/ages, and task paradigm are all reported. The fixation-control condition included active button-press responses (an active control), so it does not meet the exclusion for using only rest/fixation as baseline. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study does not meet the review population and task-domain requirements. Exclusion criteria met: E8 — the sample includes older adults with MCI and AD (not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps and voxelwise analyses are reported using GLM and Talairach transformations), I8 (whole-brain results are described and illustrated in figures/tables), I10 (participant age/education, healthy control status for the control group, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the fMRI task assesses semantic memory/naming, not an executive function/cognitive control task), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control condition is provided), I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, or cognitive flexibility). Because E8 is violated (participants are not a healthy adult sample within 18–60 only), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite some whole-brain reporting.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–32) that uses a task requiring memory for a target location and go/no-go saccade execution (involving both spatial working memory and response inhibition). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., go vs. no-go; left vs. right) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses (voxelwise results reported, with tables/figures). Participant demographics, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are provided. The task domains cover established executive functions (working memory and inhibition). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses active task contrasts, empirical, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets multiple inclusion criteria for the review (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: within-participant contrast deceased vs control words; I7: group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported; I8: whole-brain results reported with coordinates; I9: task falls within an executive-function domain—Emotional Stroop indexing inhibitory/cognitive control processes; I10: participant age, healthy screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes an age outside the allowed 18–60 range (reported age range 22–62 years). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite satisfying all listed inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy young adults (mean age ~27) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation contrasts. The experiment uses active task contrasts (calculation conditions vs a number-matching active control) and within-subject contrasts (trained vs untrained; untrained/trained vs number-matching). Whole-brain results are reported with coordinate tables and corrected cluster-level thresholds. The tasks engage executive processes (working memory and executive control) as discussed by the authors and evidenced by activations in inferior frontal and parietal control regions. Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are all reported. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study uses blank/rest trials as the baseline and reports load-related effects rather than a within-participant contrast against an active control condition. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline without an active control). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function—working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), I9 (task falls within working memory executive domain), I10 (reports participant health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (at least one analysis involving a within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult bilinguals (mean age 25.4) that explicitly investigates language control — a form of cognitive control involving inhibition/switching. It includes within-subject contrasts comparing selection contexts (e.g., LSc vs SNc, LSc vs TSc, L2 vs L1) against active naming/control conditions. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM2 results reported in figures and coordinate tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI, 1.5T), and detailed task paradigms are reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or resting-baseline-only design; participants are healthy and age within 18–60).

This study is excluded because it includes participants outside the target adult age range (adolescents; exclusion E8). Although it is a task-based fMRI study that examines cognitive control over emotion and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps (satisfying I5, I6, I7, I8, I10), the task paradigms (directed vs incidental facial emotion and age judgments) do not fall within the specified executive function domains required by I9 (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore inclusion criterion I9 is not met and exclusion criterion E8 is met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 19–26) using a Stroop-like task assessing attentional control/inhibition (an executive function). It reports within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent targets) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded at p<.05 FDR; coordinates and tables provided). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active task baselines, empirical human neuroimaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Only the reference list and bibliographic metadata are provided; the core article content (introduction, methods, participants, results, discussion) is missing. From the title it is plausible the task involves working memory (I9 met), but I cannot verify imaging modality (fMRI/PET), the presence of within-participant contrasts against an active control (I5, I6), group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps or coordinate-based whole-brain results (I7/I8), or reporting of participant age and health status (I10). No exclusion criteria from the list (E3–E8) can be confirmed from the available text. Because the full text is incomplete and key inclusion criteria cannot be verified, the study must be excluded pending access to the complete article.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive control (Stroop) in healthy adults (n=14, ages 19–28). It reports within-participant contrasts (SI vs CO; RI vs SI; RI vs CO) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with thresholds and Talairach coordinates (tables/figures). Methods, results, and discussion are present; participant demographics, healthy sample status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active control conditions). Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of sustained attention (vigilance), an executive function domain. It includes within-participant contrasts (RVIP vs Control) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and cluster results (tables/figures/coordinates). Participant demographics (mean age 29.6), health-screening procedures, imaging modality (4T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. Although participants are current smokers with moderate nicotine dependence, they were screened for serious health/psychiatric conditions and the sample is described in sufficient detail to meet the ‘healthy sample’ reporting requirement. Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers (mean age 32) that directly investigates task switching (cognitive flexibility), an executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts (switching vs non-switching; semantic-category vs overlearned sequences) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with corrected thresholds and tabulated stereotactic coordinates and figures. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy sample) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This 3T event-related fMRI study investigates working memory (an established executive function domain) using task-based paradigms in healthy adults (N=13; mean age 24.9). It reports within-participant contrasts of working memory tasks versus an active control (letter case judgment), and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (reported at P<0.001 uncorrected) with coordinates and figures. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigms are described. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back and Sternberg), which falls within executive function domains. The study reports within-participant contrasts (parametric load contrasts and encoding/responding contrasts) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM99 with corrected and uncorrected thresholds; results are presented in tables and figures. Participants are healthy adults (n=21, mean age 22.7 ± 3.6) and imaging modality/methods and task paradigms are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state baseline only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10.

Full text unavailable (fulltext_incomplete=true). Title indicates an fMRI verbal working memory study, so it likely assesses executive function, but without the full text I cannot confirm key required elements: within-participant contrasts vs active control (I6), group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (I7/I8), and reporting of participant age/healthy status and task details (I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) can be confirmed from the available metadata. Therefore I must exclude due to incomplete/full-text not available preventing verification of inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study directly comparing visual search and memory search within the same healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 19–27). It includes within-participant contrasts (visual search vs active control; memory search vs active control) using an active control task rather than rest, and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM99) with tables/figures of coordinates and conjunction/ROI analyses. The tasks recruit executive processes (monitoring/manipulating multiple items, cognitive planning, attention shifts) that map onto established executive domains (working memory/monitoring and planning). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, empirical with healthy adult sample). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=17, ages 18–30) examining working memory (an executive function) and controlled semantic processing. It reports within-participant contrasts (primed vs unprimed; WM load comparisons and interactions) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (third-level random-effects maps, corrected cluster thresholds) with coordinates/tables. Participant demographics, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are described. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include within-group task activation maps, use active within-task contrasts (primed vs unprimed / WM load) beyond rest, and sample is healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria listed (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (study includes a lesion case participant aged 77, i.e., includes participants outside 18–60 and is not restricted to healthy individuals) and E6 (task contrasts are reported relative to rest/fixation only; no active control condition). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps reported), I8 (results presented in figures/tables), I9 (working memory is an established executive function), I10 (participant ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition). Therefore the paper must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study using the N-back working memory task (executive function). It reports within-participant 2-back > 0-back contrasts, processed with SPM5 and second-level random-effects voxelwise analyses. Whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (reporting results within a priori DLPFC via small-volume correction) and figures/coordinates are provided for significant loci. Participants are healthy adult volunteers (sample sizes and screening described; imaging sample demographics and age were reported/controlled and referenced in Supplementary Table 5), imaging modality (BOLD fMRI) and task paradigm (N-back working memory) are clearly described. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI with within-subject active-control contrast and group-level voxelwise maps. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete.

Full text is complete. The study is excluded because its imaging analyses were conducted within a predefined ROI framework and between-group comparisons were limited to those ROIs; the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. This meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only results). The study does meet multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based BOLD fMRI of an executive function — verbal working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast: mPASAT versus auditory monitoring active control), I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within executive function — working memory), and I10 (participant age range, healthy controls, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). However I7 (requirement for at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise map) is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study examining phonological control/working memory during syllable judgment tasks in healthy adults (ages 18–33). The task probes verbal working memory/phonological control (an executive function domain). The paper reports within-subject contrasts between active task conditions (pseudo-English vs English; novel vs familiar words), performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99; tables of coordinates and figures), and provides participant, imaging modality, and task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting-state only, empirical fMRI data in healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete with introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of an executive (working memory) task (spatial n-back) with reward manipulations in healthy adults (mean age 21.7). It includes within-subject contrasts (3-back vs 1-back; reward vs no-reward and interactions), uses group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with reported thresholds and tables of coordinates, and provides participant, task, and imaging details. An active control (0-back) was used. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=13, age 19–42) using a visual three-stimulus oddball paradigm that probes attentional control, target detection, and working-memory-related processes (executive domains: vigilance/attention and working memory). The study reports within-subject contrasts (target and distractor vs. standard) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (corrected thresholds) and coordinate/ROI tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are reported. Thus all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 29–41) using a task that engages executive processes (guessing/gambling with working-memory and decision-making demands). It includes a within-subject contrast of an executive task (guessing) versus an active control (reporting) with matched perceptual/motor demands. Analyses are whole-brain voxelwise SPM group-level maps with reported activation foci/coordinates and figures/tables. Sufficient participant, imaging modality, and paradigm details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text is incomplete/unavailable (content only shows a redirect/placeholder). Cannot verify core methods or results against inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable: I5 (fMRI/PET task assessing executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), I8 (clear reporting of whole-brain results), I9 (task falls within executive function domains), I10 (participant age/healthy status/imaging modality/task reported). Exclusion criteria applied: none can be confidently applied from the provided content (e.g., E3–E8 cannot be assessed without full methods/results). Because the full text is incomplete, this study must be excluded from the meta-analysis until the complete article is obtained and re-screened.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that manipulates working-memory demands during sentence processing. It reports within-participant contrasts comparing grammatical features with differing WM demands (e.g., transitivity vs inflectional morphology and dual-task vs single-task manipulations), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (SPM analyses) with coordinate tables. Participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active task contrasts, empirical, healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables).

This is an fMRI task-based study examining the imagery analogue of the verbal transformation effect that explicitly engages verbal working memory and related decision processes (an executive function domain). It reports a within-subject contrast (verbal-transformation vs baseline mental repetition), and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM results with peak coordinates, tables, and figures. Participants are healthy adults (n=10; mean age 24 ± 7), imaging modality and paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study uses task-based within-subject contrasts (Melody Discrimination and Harmony Discrimination vs an active button-press control) and reports group-level whole-brain results (z-maps and stereotaxic coordinates) in healthy adult participants (age range 19–46). The discrimination tasks require holding and comparing auditory stimuli online and the authors explicitly report involvement of working-memory and cognitive-control regions (dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, anterior cingulate), consistent with executive-function processes. Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and therefore appears complete. Based on these points the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working-memory/central executive function (reading span test) in healthy adults (ages 20–27). It reports within-subject contrasts (RST vs read control) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures (SPM99 results, corrected thresholds). Participant health status, age range, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task activations, uses an active control condition, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This is an original task-based fMRI study of executive function (branching integrating working memory and attentional allocation). It reports within-participant contrasts (branching vs control, delay, dual-task) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and statistical thresholds (tables/figures). Participants were healthy right-handed adults aged 20–28. Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigms (working memory, dual-task, planning/branching), and participant/sample details are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active control condition, empirical data, participants within 18–60 and healthy).

This study is excluded because it includes non-healthy participants (MTBI patients) and is not restricted to a healthy adult sample (Exclusion E8). Met inclusion criteria: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported in SPM and figures), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), and I10 (participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Not met inclusion criteria: I5 (the fMRI task is a spatial navigation/spatial memory paradigm, not a clear executive function/cognitive control task), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control condition was reported), and I9 (task does not clearly fall within established executive function domains such as working memory/inhibition/cognitive flexibility). Full text appears complete (includes intro, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded for failing to meet the executive-function-specific inclusion criteria and because the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (E8).

Full text appears to describe a resting-state fMRI study of mild cognitive impairment and mild Alzheimer’s disease rather than a task-based executive function study in healthy adults. Exclusion IDs met: E4 (resting-state/connectivity analyses without a whole-brain task activation map) and E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals; includes patient groups). Inclusion IDs met: none []. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (not a task-based executive function fMRI/PET study), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control contrast reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map), I9 (tasks are not within executive function domains), I10 (insufficient/irrelevant reporting for healthy adult task paradigm). Full text provided appears incomplete (only metadata/redirect page), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–27) examining working memory manipulation (an executive function). It reports within-subject contrasts comparing manipulation versus maintenance (active control) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds and activation coordinates/figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

Although this study meets general methodological inclusion requirements (fMRI, a working-memory executive task with within-subject contrasts versus an active baseline, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses, and adequate reporting of age, modality and paradigm), it is not restricted to healthy adults and does not provide a healthy-subject-only whole-brain task activation map. The experiments were performed in a mixed sample of childhood-onset GH-deficient patients and matched controls; group results are reported across subjects (patients+controls) and as patient>control interactions, but a standalone within-group whole-brain activation map for healthy controls is not presented. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E8 (participants not restricted to healthy individuals) and E5 (no accompanying within-group task activation contrast in healthy participants). Because the meta-analysis objective is executive-function activations in healthy adults, the absence of a healthy-only whole-brain activation map prevents inclusion.

The study reports fMRI task-based data including a verbal working memory (letters) task that is an established executive function domain (I9). It includes within-subject contrasts (experimental > control blocks for the letters task and other tasks) satisfying I6. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM (individual and mixed-effects group analyses producing SPM{t} maps/Z scores), meeting I7 and I8. The paper reports participant ages (19–42), confirms healthy volunteers, describes the imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigms in detail, meeting I10 and I5. No exclusion criteria are violated: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), not limited to connectivity/rest, include within-group contrasts in healthy adults, and participants are within 18–60. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=14, age 18–36) using a number Stroop executive task with emotional priming. It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; aversive vs neutral primes; stars control), uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME) with multiple-comparison correction (FDR), and provides participant demographics, imaging parameters, and task details. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (n-back) with whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses and within-participant task contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 0-back). It meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample includes both patients with schizophrenia and healthy comparison subjects (i.e., the study is not restricted to healthy adults), which violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adult executive-function activations. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Exclusion criteria met: E8.

This is an ASL perfusion fMRI study of sustained attention/vigilance (PVT) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps and participant/sample details (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the study contrasts the task against resting baselines (pre/post rest) rather than an active control task; there is no within-participant contrast against an active control condition (I6 not met). Because the study uses rest/fixation as the primary baseline, it violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest-only baseline without an active control). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=10, mean age 29±10) that directly contrasts executive-function-related conditions against active control conditions. The spatial attention and memory paradigm (SAMP) involves working memory/attentional demands (an established executive domain). The paper reports within-participant (task vs control) contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with voxelwise and cluster-level thresholds; peak coordinates and activation tables are provided. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the report is complete for screening purposes.

This is an fMRI study of verbal working memory in healthy adults that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps and provides participant/sample details. However, the analyses primarily contrast task epochs (encoding/retrieval) against a fixation baseline and do not present a within-participant, group-level voxelwise contrast of the executive (working memory) task versus an active control condition. Although the authors ran conjunctions and ROI timecourse ANOVAs comparing DSR and simple speech/tapping, they did not provide the required whole-brain DSR > active-control contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (use of rest/fixation as the primary baseline without an appropriate active-control whole-brain contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of healthy adults using working memory tasks (delayed recognition) with event-related, whole-brain group analyses; participant ages and health status are reported. However, the paper does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive task versus an active control task condition. The reported analyses focus on task-period activity (cue, delay, probe) using main-effect-of-task maps (conjunctions) and comparisons to baseline, rather than an active control task. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 is not met, and exclusion criterion E6 applies (use of rest/fixation or baseline-only contrasts without an active control). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of a NoGo (inhibition) task, which is an established executive function domain. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (NoGo vs Go) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses for healthy control subjects (contrast images, β images, and tables/figures with coordinates). Participant information (healthy control group described, demographics referenced in Table 1), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, allowing verification of criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-group healthy contrasts, resting-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range participants) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14, age 26–42) using a covert orienting task to probe inhibition of return (IOR). The study reports within-subject contrasts (long SOA vs short SOA) to isolate IOR-related effects, and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with corrected thresholds and reports peak coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, health-status screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are all reported. IOR indexes an inhibitory attentional process and maps onto the ‘inhibition’ domain within executive function constructs. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, active task control, healthy adults within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

Exclusion: The study does not investigate an established executive function task domain (it examines auditory spatial attention reorienting in a passive listening paradigm) and does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control. Additionally, the primary task contrasts are reported versus a REST (silent) baseline (i.e., rest/fixation), fitting exclusion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported), I8 (whole-brain results and coordinates are reported in tables/figures), and I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an fMRI/PET study of executive function/cognitive control task), I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition), and I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, or cognitive flexibility). Full text appears complete for screening.

This study is excluded because it reports primarily EEG-derived connectivity analyses (PDC and graph-theoretic measures) and does not provide a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map from fMRI or PET. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (reports only connectivity analyses without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrast: congruent vs. incongruent Stroop conditions), I9 (task is Stroop — an executive/inhibition paradigm), I10 (reports participant age, healthy status, imaging modalities, and task details). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-activation fMRI/PET study reporting task-evoked activations), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map presented), I8 (no whole-brain activation coordinates/voxelwise maps described). Full text appears complete for screening. Therefore the paper does not satisfy required whole-brain fMRI/PET activation evidence and must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study with whole-brain group-level activation maps in healthy adults (meets I7, I8, I10). However, the task is autobiographical emotion induction (irritability/happiness) rather than a canonical executive-function/cognitive-control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 (task assessing executive function/cognitive control) nor I9 (task within established executive function domains). Although within-subject contrasts are reported, they are contrasts of emotional states rather than an executive task contrast, so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

Exclusion E8 applies: participants are healthy elders (mean age 68.3), i.e. outside the 18–60 age range required by the review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of executive function - N-back working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast 2-back > 0-back with active 0-back control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with SPM2), I8 (whole-brain results reported via tables/coordinates), I9 (task falls within executive function - working memory), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 satisfied). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore exclude due to E8 (age outside target range).

This is an empirical fMRI study of an executive-function task (colour Stroop; inhibition) in healthy adults (N=28, mean age 20.2). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (parametric linear trend across blocks varying proportion of incongruent trials and supplementary contrasts of each incongruity level vs 0% baseline), and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures (P<0.001 uncorrected). Participant details, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The 0% incongruent blocks provide an active baseline/control condition. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state-only, participants are healthy and adult). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is a task-based fMRI study using a modified Stroop color-naming paradigm (an inhibition/cognitive-control task), with within-subject contrasts comparing death-related and negative-valence words to neutral-valence words (active control). Group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholds and coordinates, figures/tables). Participants are healthy adults (female, ages 18–25). Imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are fully described. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations in healthy adults and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/NoGo), an established executive function (inhibition), in healthy adult participants (male, 18–50). It reports within-subject NoGo vs Go contrasts, uses random-effects group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses, and provides coordinates and figures of activation. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. The Go condition serves as an active control rather than rest. No exclusion criteria are met and the full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an fMRI study of working memory (delayed item recognition for letters) in healthy adults (n=40, mean age 25.1) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level GLM and MLM) and presents coordinates/figures of activation. The paper includes within-participant contrasts across task conditions (set-size/load comparisons and delay-period effects) that serve as active cognitive-control contrasts (low vs. intermediate vs. high WM load). Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, and participants are healthy adults within the 18–60 range. The full article (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Although this is an fMRI study of an executive/working-memory task (modified PASAT) with group-level, whole-brain task activation maps and adequate reporting, the paper does not present a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition. Analyses appear to be task versus off-period (rest) activation maps rather than PASAT versus an active control (e.g., auditory monitoring) contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation used as the baseline without an active-control contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Exclusion criteria met: E6.

This is a prospective task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–35) that includes executive-function paradigms (working memory STERN; also attention), reports within-participant contrasts versus active control conditions (e.g., NT vs CT for working memory; AL vs SC and RE vs SC for associative memory), and conducts group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (group contrast maps, voxel-by-voxel SPM2 analyses with FWE correction; ROIs derived from whole-brain contrasts with MNI coordinates). Participant health status, age range, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly reported. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activations, includes active control contrasts, empirical fMRI data in healthy adults).

This is an fMRI, task-based experiment in healthy adults examining spatial negative priming (inhibition/selection), which falls under executive function (inhibition). It reports a within-subject contrast (spatial inhibition vs control) and presents group-level whole-brain task activation maps (task vs rest) and attempted whole-brain paired t tests; ROI follow-up is reported but whole-brain analyses are present. Participant age, health status, modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups only, includes active control trials, healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical within-subject fMRI study using an emotional go/no-go task (response inhibition) — an established executive function (inhibition). Group-level whole-brain random effects analyses are reported (voxelwise maps, cluster thresholds, tables/figures/coordinates) and within-participant contrasts compare inhibitory (distracter) vs non-inhibitory (target) conditions. Participant age, healthy sample screening, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, includes active task contrasts, empirical, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Thus all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=16, ages 19–35) directly investigating cognitive control/executive function (contextual and episodic control, task switching/conflict). The paper reports within-participant, group-level voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and factorial analyses (SPM2; voxelwise and cluster thresholds; FDR correction) and presents coordinates/figures of activations. Detailed methods, participant health/age, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=40, ages 22–42) using a stop-signal task (inhibition/vigilance). It reports within-participant contrasts (pre-stop-error vs pre-stop-success) and second-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected results and coordinate tables/figures. Participant inclusion/health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, and participants are within 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be included.

Exclusion: E8 applies because the study sample is not restricted to healthy adults (includes antipsychotic-naïve first-episode schizophrenia patients and healthy controls) and the recruitment age range included participants as young as 15 years (outside the 18–60 range). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive function task — ODR vs visually guided saccade active control), I7 (group-level voxelwise/whole-brain voxel-wise analyses reported), I8 (results reported in figures/tables and described in text), I9 (ODR is spatial working memory — an executive function), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality and paradigms are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Because E8 is violated (mixed clinical sample and ages outside 18–60), the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory control/integration (an executive function domain). It reports within-subject contrasts among task conditions (IN vs SG, MO, RO) and voxelwise group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses with coordinates and brain maps. Participant information (healthy adults, ages reported), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described in detail. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI empirical study of working memory (n-back phonological and spatial tasks) in healthy adults. It reports within-subject contrasts between executive task conditions (PWM>SWM and SWM>PWM) and task>baseline contrasts, uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with coordinates and thresholding described, and provides participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not rest-only baseline without active contrasts, not non-empirical, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10.

This is an fMRI study of verbal working memory that includes a healthy control group and reports participant details (meets I5, I9, I10). However, the paper’s task activation analyses are performed at the individual/native-space ROI level and subsequent ROI-based group comparisons; there is no clear report of a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the working-memory task (I7 not met). The analyses emphasize ROI/regional measures and stage-specific functional connectivity rather than whole-brain task activation maps, so it effectively reports only ROI-based task results and connectivity findings (meets exclusion E3: only ROI analyses with no whole-brain task results). Additionally, a within-participant contrast against an active control baseline is not clearly presented as required (I6 not met). Therefore the study fails required inclusion criteria for whole-brain task maps and within-participant active-control contrasts and is excluded.

This is an fMRI task-based study investigating cognitive control/response inhibition during intentional false responding. It includes within-subject contrasts (FALSE vs TRUE; FALSE_AUTO vs TRUE_AUTO), uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 random-effects with FDR correction) reported with coordinates/tables/figures, reports participant ages (20–34), confirms healthy sample status, and details imaging modality and task paradigm. The task falls squarely within executive function domains (inhibition/cognitive control). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, includes active within-subject contrasts rather than rest-only baseline, empirical human neuroimaging data, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criteria E6 and E8. E6: the fMRI analyses contrast the 2-back working memory task against fixation (rest) without an active control condition (no 0-back/1-back or other active baseline), so it lacks a within-participant contrast against an active control as required (I6 not met). E8: the sample includes participants outside the healthy adult range and not restricted to healthy individuals (participants include schizophrenia patients and siblings aged 14–25, i.e., under 18), violating the healthy adult/age-range requirement. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), I9 (working memory is an executive function), I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control). Given E6 and E8 are met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 20–27). The study reports within-subject contrasts (LST vs Listen and Remember) and group-level random-effects analyses using whole-brain voxelwise methods (SPM99). Whole-brain results are reported as coordinate tables and glass-brain figures. Participant health, age range, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unspecified participants) are met. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of auditory 2-back working memory in healthy adults and meets multiple inclusion criteria (I5: task-based fMRI assessing executive function; I7: group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM maps were generated; I8: whole-brain results presented in figures/tables; I9: working memory is an established executive function domain; I10: participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). However, the task contrast uses rest epochs as the baseline (rest vs. 2-back) with no active control condition (e.g., 0-back or another active control). Therefore it does not meet I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control) and it violates exclusion criterion E6 (studies using rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control). Because failing I6 and meeting E6 are sufficient to exclude the study, the decision is to EXCLUDE.

EXCLUDED because participants include older adults outside the 18–60 range (E8). While the study reports whole-brain, group-level fMRI results (I7) and describes whole-brain results in text/tables (I8), and provides participant age/health, imaging modality, and task details (I10), it does not examine an executive function task per inclusion definitions (task is long-term recognition/encoding of unfamiliar faces, not working memory/inhibition/cognitive flexibility etc.; I5 and I9 not met). Also there is no within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control as required (I6 not met). Therefore the study must be excluded. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages reported) using task-based paradigms that probe movement planning and cognitive control (planning/inhibitory aspects). The paper reports within-participant contrasts isolating the rotated (RJM/RHM) versus non-rotated (JM/HM) conditions (active control conditions), and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with figures and coordinate tables. Imaging modality, participant health status, ages, and task paradigms are described. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and participants are within the 18–60 range. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive control (retrieval/maintenance of task sets, conflict detection/inhibition). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent cues) and voxelwise, group-level whole-brain analyses (random-effects t-tests with voxelwise thresholds) as well as ROI analyses. Participant details (N=18 after exclusion; ages 18–30; healthy) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) and full task paradigm are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of Stroop/attentional control in healthy volunteers with within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses; however the paper does not report participants' ages or age range, so I10 (reporting participant age) is not satisfied. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study is excluded. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this study reports group-level whole-brain fMRI analyses and provides full participant and task details, it does not assess canonical executive function domains required by the review. The main tasks are object categorization and recognition (perceptual/memory tasks), and the mental-rotation localizer probes visuo-spatial transformation rather than an established executive domain (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility). The report does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control that would meet I6/I9. Therefore it fails I5, I6, and I9 despite meeting I7, I8, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete.

While the study is an fMRI study of inhibition (modified RPS) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, it does not include a within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control condition. The fMRI analyses reported are task versus rest within groups and a between-group (lose vs win) comparison; subjects were assigned to win or lose groups rather than performing both conditions within-subject. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control) is not met. Exclusion criterion E6 applies because the within-subject baseline contrasts use rest/fixation without an active control task. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (8 participants, ages 20–25). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of executive tasks versus matched active control conditions (REP/REP CONT, MAT/MAT CONT, REP/MAT).
