Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM) are reported, with thresholding corrected for multiple comparisons and cluster extent criteria; results are presented as statistical maps and described in the text/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are all reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly investigates cognitive control/conflict monitoring (ACC–PFC) during semantic retrieval (the TOT state). It contains within-participant contrasts comparing TOT versus Know and Don’t Know conditions (active task conditions), reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected statistics (SPM, p<0.05 cluster-corrected), and provides participant demographics (14 healthy adults, ages 19–27), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm details. Thus it meets I5 (fMRI study of cognitive control), I6 (within-subject contrasts against active conditions), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures), I9 (examines cognitive control/monitoring processes within executive function domain), and I10 (reports participant age, healthy status, modality, and paradigm). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a within-subject task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=23, mean age 21.3) probing selective/object-based attention and top-down cognitive control. It reports within-participant contrasts (attend vs ignore/observe) using active control conditions, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions and state contrasts) with thresholding described. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The selective attention task targets cognitive control/top-down biasing processes and thus falls within executive/cognitive-control domains relevant to the review. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active control conditions, healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of a sustained attention (CPT) task in healthy adults (ages 18–28) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (SPM) comparing task blocks to baseline. CPT falls within the review’s executive-function domain (vigilance). Methods report a within-subject contrast of active CPT versus a baseline of meaningless images (visual control), which serves as an active control condition rather than simple fixation. Relevant participant information (age, health status), imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are provided. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports a task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (n-back), an established executive function domain, in healthy adult volunteers (mean age ~33.8) and schizophrenia patients. It includes within-subject contrasts of executive task versus active control (2-back vs 0-back) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE/FDR-corrected clusters and MNI coordinates). Required participant, imaging modality, and task details are provided. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults.

Although this is a group-level, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults with voxelwise statistical maps reported (meets I7, I8, I10), the experimental tasks target language processing (attention to semantic vs. phonological relations) rather than established executive function domains (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not satisfy I5 (study of executive function/cognitive control) nor I9 (task within established executive function domains). I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control) is not met because the within-participant contrasts are between two language tasks rather than executive-control tasks with an active control designed to isolate executive processes. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered, and the full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Consequently the study is excluded for failing to meet key inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I9.

This is an fMRI study that uses task-based contrasts probing verbal working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-subject task contrasts against active control conditions (nonword reading vs consonant strings; picture naming vs scrambled images). The paper describes voxelwise statistical mapping and provides group-level coordinates/figures (e.g., average MNI coordinates for pSTG and MTG; stimulation locations transformed to atlas space), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked results. Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met.

This paper reports an fMRI study in healthy adults using an n-back working-memory paradigm (an executive function task) with within-subject contrasts (n-back levels vs 0-back control and parametric complexity contrasts). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses are reported and thresholded; coordinates and cluster tables are provided. Participant characteristics (healthy right-handed volunteers, sample size, matching to controls) and imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and task details are described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Inclusion criteria applied: I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

This is an empirical fMRI study of inhibitory control (GO/NOGO), an executive function, with healthy adult participants (N=15, age 23–40). It reports within-subject contrasts of task events (successful Stops/NOGO) relative to baseline/Go conditions and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Talairach normalization, voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction). Results are presented as whole-brain activation maps and described in text/tables/figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so full text is complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study includes a working-memory (n-back) manipulation (executive function domain) with within-subject contrasts (high > low WM load) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (random-effects SPM results with voxel coordinates and thresholding). Participants are healthy adults (16 males, age 22–30). Imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant details are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: n=12, mean age 25±3.3; Experiment 2: n=12, mean age 22±4.1) investigating top-down attentional control (zooming in/out), which the authors frame as executive/cognitive control processes. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., zooming in/out vs high-level baseline [HLB]; zooming out > zooming in; zooming in > zooming out) and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; cluster- and voxel-level thresholds reported) with coordinates/tables. Task paradigm and imaging modality (fMRI) are fully described. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-only baseline, non-empirical paper, or out-of-range/clinical sample). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

The study is excluded because its control condition is a passive fixation/rest baseline (subjects in total darkness maintaining fixation), which meets exclusion criterion E6 (studies using rest or fixation as the only baseline without an active control). Although the paper uses fMRI and an antisaccade inhibition task (I5), reports within-participant contrasts versus the fixation control (but not versus an active control; I6 not met), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and figures (I7, I8), uses an executive inhibition task (I9), and reports participant age/healthy sample/imaging modality/task details (I10), the lack of an active control task violates E6. Therefore it does not meet all inclusion criteria required for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 20–37) that examines a rule-guided go/nogo (inhibition) task — an executive function domain. The paper reports within-subject contrasts comparing ocular baseball decided-go/decided-nogo conditions to matched active controls (always-go, always-nogo). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM99; thresholds reported) and results are presented in figures/tables. Imaging modality, participant health/ages, and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes active controls).

The study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: the participant sample is not restricted to healthy adults (it includes individuals with Prader–Willi syndrome as well as matched typically developing controls). Although the paper reports whole-brain fMRI task contrasts of task-switching (switching vs non-switching) and provides group-level, voxelwise maps and tables for both groups, the meta-analysis objective is restricted to healthy adults and E8 therefore applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast: switching vs non-switching blocks), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/text), I9 (task switching = cognitive flexibility/executive domain), I10 (participant ages, health status of control group, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: [] (all applicable I-criteria were reported). Full text appears complete: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study investigates nonspatial attention shifting (feature-based set-shifting) in healthy adults using within-subject contrasts (shifting attention vs sustained attention) and reports voxelwise group results with Talairach coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive control), I6 (within-participant contrast of executive-like task vs active control), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures), I9 (task maps to cognitive flexibility/set-shifting), I10 (participants’ ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). However, the study does NOT meet I7: although voxelwise group analyses were performed, imaging coverage was limited to posterior brain and cerebellum (coronal slices covering occipital/parietal/part temporal and cerebellum) and did not provide whole-brain coverage (frontal regions were not imaged), so there is no qualifying whole-brain group-level activation map. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore exclude because I7 is not satisfied.

Exclusion rationale: This study is excluded because (1) participant age is outside the review age range (subjects aged 60–69; E8) and (2) the task contrast uses fixation as the baseline (ENCOD vs FIX), i.e., rest/fixation only rather than an active control (E6). Inclusion coverage: the study provides group-level whole-brain, voxelwise fMRI results (I7) and reports participant age/healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm (I10). Inclusion criteria not met: it does not test an executive function/cognitive-control task (face encoding is episodic/visuospatial memory rather than working memory/inhibition/cognitive flexibility; I5 and I9 not met) and it lacks a within-participant contrast of an executive control task against an active control condition (I6 not met). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study includes participants outside the target population for the meta-analysis: it includes a patient group (Turner syndrome) rather than being restricted to healthy adults, and includes participants younger than 18 (age range for Turner group includes 14-year-old), thus violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — working memory tasks), I6 (within-participant contrasts across task conditions/domains and distracter vs no-distracter), I9 (tasks fall within executive function domain — working memory), I10 (participant ages, health status of control group, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no clear report of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map in the main text; results are primarily ROI-based with group-average activation maps reported in supplementary figures but no clearly described voxelwise group-level statistical maps for inclusion). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60.

This fMRI study investigates voluntary suppression of thermally induced pain, reporting whole-brain group voxelwise activations and healthy adult sample details. However, the suppression condition is contrasted against rest (a passive baseline) rather than an active control task; there is no within-participant contrast of the executive/suppression task relative to an active control. Therefore it fails exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task engages cognitive control/inhibition), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (results reported with figures/tables/coodinates), I9 (task taps an executive domain: inhibition), I10 (participant age/health, imaging modality, paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast vs an active control). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears to be limited to abstract-level information (methods/results summary) and is therefore incomplete. Based on available content: I5 (fMRI study of working memory/executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast: Order vs Item task), and I9 (working memory = executive domain) are satisfied. However, critical inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the provided text: I7 (presence of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map) is not explicitly confirmed, and I10 (reported participant age range, confirmation of healthy sample status, and full task/imaging details) is missing. No exclusion criteria are explicitly met from the available information. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be verifiable and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article that can confirm I7 and I10. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I9. Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I7, I10.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (N=16 after exclusion; mean age 25 ± 3). It uses within-subject contrasts of memory-load conditions (e.g., load 6 vs load 2), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses using SPM with thresholded maps and coordinate tables. The manuscript provides participant details, imaging modality, and task paradigm. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata available) so critical methodological details cannot be verified. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (study includes Alzheimer’s patients and is not restricted to healthy participants). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory — an executive function) and I9 (working memory task). Inclusion criteria not met / not verifiable from available text: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast vs an active control reported in the abstract), I7 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise statistical maps cannot be confirmed from the abstract), I10 (participant ages not reported in available text and healthy-sample details insufficient). Therefore the study cannot be included for the meta-analysis based on available information and because it includes non-healthy participants. Full text incomplete: true.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 23.9) that directly examines cognitive control using a forced-attention dichotic listening paradigm (an executive-function conflict/inhibition task). The design includes within-participant contrasts (FL, FR, NF conditions; paired t-tests comparing drug-naïve vs. memantine sessions) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM5 with tables of MNI coordinates and figures; small-volume corrections are also described. Participant demographic and health information, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-groups-only, participants are healthy adults 18–60). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function) in healthy adults (n=10, mean age ~25). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., first vs. last maintenance–retrieval sections, parametric/exponential modulation across retrieval blocks) that test practice-related changes in executive processing. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported with tables of Talairach coordinates and figures (voxelwise results at P<0.001), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting baseline only, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study uses PASAT (working memory/executive task) and reports within-group, whole-brain, random-effects analyses in healthy controls (one-sample t-test) contrasted against an active control task (number repetition). Group-level voxelwise results are reported and coordinates/figures/tables are provided. Participant sample includes an explicitly described healthy control group, imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text includes methods, results, and discussion, so core article content appears complete. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults.

Full text provided consists only of references and metadata (authors, journal, DOI) - core article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is missing, so fulltext_incomplete is true. From the available information the title and snippets indicate an fMRI study of hippocampal activity during a virtual radial arm maze (spatial navigation/memory). This does not appear to target established executive function domains (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning), so it likely fails I9. Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map), I8 (clear whole-brain results reporting), or I10 (reporting of participant age and healthy-sample status). Therefore the study is excluded. Exclusion criteria met: none clearly met from available content ([]). Inclusion criteria met: none ([]). Inclusion criteria not met (or not verifiable): I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Fulltext_incomplete=true.

This fMRI study examines planning, monitoring, and rule-related cognition during driving — processes that map onto executive functions (planning, rule retrieval/maintenance). It uses within-subject contrasts (e.g., Action planning > Coasting; Monitoring traffic > Coasting; Traffic rules > Coasting) against an active baseline (coasting). Analyses were conducted with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM models and peak coordinates/tables are reported. Participant demographic and health information, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported (20 healthy right-handed licensed taxi drivers, ages 27–59). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/rest-only; not between-group-only; participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function activations.

This study reports an fMRI emotional linguistic go/nogo task targeting response inhibition (an executive function). It includes within-participant contrasts (nogo vs. go within emotional contexts) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with coordinate tables and figures. Healthy control group details (n=18; ages 21–40) and imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are provided. Although the study also includes a clinical patient group, it presents within-group results for healthy controls, satisfying the meta-analysis requirement to extract healthy adult executive-function activations. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures described) is present and appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults that examines encoding and decision stages of a time-discrimination task and explicitly assesses working memory and decision-making (executive) processes. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of decision difficulty (hard vs easy discriminations), which are active task-vs-task comparisons indexing executive/working-memory demand. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (tables of coordinates and figures). Participant age range, health status, imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are described in detail. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline without active contrasts, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy samples) are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

This fMRI study investigates sensorimotor selection-for-action (reach-to-grasp) rather than an established executive function/cognitive control task. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and clearly described), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess executive function or cognitive control per se using an executive task), I9 (task does not fall within specified executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation), and therefore I6 (contrast is not an executive-function vs active-control contrast). No exclusion criteria from E3–E8 are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Consequently the study is excluded because it does not meet the core requirement that the task probes executive function domains relevant to the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=12; ages 20–45) that directly contrasts a category-discrimination task (CAT) with an active auditory-discrimination control (AUD) using within-subject contrasts. The CAT task involves processes linked to working memory/executive function (authors explicitly interpret categorization as engaging working memory). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM results, figures, and coordinate tables). Imaging modality, participant health/age, and task paradigms are all described. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-only baseline, or non-healthy/age-out-of-range issues). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core article content appears complete.

Exclusion E3 met: the fMRI results are presented as individual subject activation images and ROI-based summary statistics (McNemar test across regions of interest) rather than a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical map or reported coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function — auditory digital working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast of working memory vs an active non-working-memory control), I9 (task is working memory, an established executive domain), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported), and therefore I8 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results via coordinates/figures) is not satisfied at the group/voxelwise level. Full text appears complete for decision-making. Given the lack of requisite whole-brain group-level voxelwise results, this study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age reported) that investigates mental calculation tasks engaging working memory and manipulation (executive function). It reports within-subject contrasts of calculation versus active control conditions (result-matching, letter pseudo-calculation, substitution tasks). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM and results are reported in figures/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigms are described. Although the final analyzed sample is small (n=5) and a fixed-effects group model was used, these aspects do not violate the stated inclusion/exclusion criteria. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study of cognitive set-shifting (a cognitive flexibility/executive function task) in healthy adults (n=18, ages 19–25). It reports within-subject task contrasts (e.g., negative vs positive feedback; shift/generate/update/maintenance contrasts), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR correction, tables/figures of activations, and Granger-causality connectivity analyses. Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, not between-group-only, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures described). Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion.

(a) Exclusion criterion met: E8 — participants are elderly (age range 62–76, mean 68.9), which lies outside the meta-analysis age range of 18–60. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing working memory/executive function), I6 (within-participant task vs active baseline contrasts), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results/coordinates clearly described), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory), I10 (reports participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: none (all other inclusion criteria satisfied). Given E8, the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria. Full text is complete.

This PNAS study uses task-based fMRI of working memory in healthy volunteers with within-subject contrasts against active control tasks, reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses (coordinates/figures), and addresses an executive function domain (working memory). However, the provided full text does not report participant ages, so I10 (relevant information regarding participant age) cannot be confirmed. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I10 is not satisfied from the provided content, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered by the available information.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult volunteers that includes an established executive function task (Go No-Go response inhibition) with a within-subject design and within-participant contrasts (No-Go minus Oddball). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (cluster-based XBAM analysis; coordinates provided in Table 2 and figures), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting of results. The paper reports healthy sample status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms; demographic data are referenced (Table 1) supporting participant information. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I9 and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. Full text appears complete with methods, results, and discussion available.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly examines inhibitory executive control using task-based paradigms (Stroop and flanker) and a sentence plausibility manipulation. Within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent for Stroop and flanker; implausible vs. plausible for sentences) are reported, and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented (tables and figures, with voxelwise thresholds). Participant demographics (age range 19–23), healthy status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are all reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete for screening purposes.

The study is excluded because it includes participants older than the 18–60 age range (E8). Although it is a task-based fMRI study of executive processes (working memory/attention) with whole-brain voxelwise results and reports coordinates (I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 are satisfied), the sample includes older adults up to 84 years, violating the age restriction (E8). Additionally, the primary reported task contrasts are task vs fixation (rest) and multivariate task patterns rather than a clear within-participant contrast of an executive task versus an active control condition; thus E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control contrast) also applies. Therefore the paper does not meet all inclusion criteria (notably I6) and meets exclusion criteria E8 (and E6). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study does not provide a group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (I7). Functional EPI acquisition had limited slice coverage (“six axial images were obtained covering from the parietal region to the inferior frontal gyrus”), so the functional results are not whole-brain. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of cognitive/phonological processes), I6 (within-participant contrasts including task vs an active control CONT), I8 (results reported in figures/tables/text), I9 (PHONO engages phonological working memory), and I10 (healthy adult sample, ages reported, imaging modality and paradigm described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Therefore it must be excluded because NOT ALL inclusion criteria are satisfied (specifically I7). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical PET study that assesses executive function (counting Stroop) in healthy adult volunteers. It includes within-subject contrasts of incongruent vs. neutral (active control) Stroop conditions, reported at the group level using voxelwise whole-brain SPM analyses (results presented in tables/figures). Participant ages and healthy status, imaging modality (H2(15)O PET), and task paradigm are clearly described. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met.

Excluded because analyses were performed exclusively using region-of-interest (ROI) approaches with no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map reported, thereby violating exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function — working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts of task conditions), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory), and I10 (participant ages reported, healthy sample, imaging modality and task paradigm described). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results provided). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory (operation span) versus an active control (arithmetic), reporting within-subject contrasts (OSPAN > Arithmetic and task > baseline) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded maps, tables/figures). Participants are healthy adults (mean age 24.8). Imaging modality, paradigm, methods, and results (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are fully reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–24) using a task that probes cognitive flexibility/set-shifting (an established executive function domain). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., negative > positive feedback; ED vs ID shifts), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures, ROI analyses, and full methodological and participant information (modality, paradigm, ages, health screening). Whole-brain group contrasts are explicitly reported (tables/figures) meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, not resting-state-only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy and within 18–60 years). Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study does not evaluate an executive function/cognitive-control task contrast required by the review. Although it is an fMRI, task-based, group-level whole-brain study (I7) with clearly reported results (I8) and reports participant/sample/task details (I10), the primary reported analyses focus on a monetary incentive delay reward task (not an executive function task) and the manuscript does not present a within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control (I5, I6, I9 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation of working memory (n-back) reporting within-subject 2-back > 0-back contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results; demographics and imaging/task details for healthy controls are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample includes schizophrenia patients and healthy controls (i.e., it is not restricted to healthy individuals). Per exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals), the study must be excluded despite meeting the other inclusion requirements. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is a task-based fMRI study of inhibition (inhibition of return), an executive function domain (inhibition). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., Long_SOA vs Short_SOA; cued vs uncued) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-corrected thresholds and coordinate tables. Participant demographics (ages 21–25), healthy status, imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes active task contrasts, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided; fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded because the study uses rest/visual fixation as the baseline and does not include an active control task contrast (exclusion E6). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps reported for epoch-related WM contrasts), I8 (results reported in figures/tables and described), I9 (working memory is an established executive function), I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I6 — there is no within-participant contrast of the executive task versus an active control condition; the epoch contrasts use visual fixation/rest as baseline and the primary analyses focus on intrinsic/connectivity measures rather than an active-control task. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED under E6.

This study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function—numerical Stroop tapping interference/inhibition), I6 (within-participant contrasts: maximally vs minimally incongruent), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps reported), I8 (coordinates and figures reported), I9 (task falls within inhibition/executive control), and I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm are reported). However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes participants outside the 18–60 age range (children aged 8–12 and elderly participants up to 81 years). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite satisfying the inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI task-switching study of cognitive control/cognitive flexibility in healthy adults (mean age 22, range 19–29). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., task switch vs. repetition; interaction of feedback type) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables/figures describing activated clusters (Tables 1–2, Figures). The task falls squarely within executive function (cognitive flexibility/task switching). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task/paradigm and analysis methods are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses active task contrasts, empirical human neuroimaging, healthy adult sample). Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Full text is incomplete (HTML contains only metadata), and the article title explicitly states the sample are patients with schizophrenia. Meta-analysis requires healthy adult samples. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (study includes non-healthy participants / not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met (based on available metadata): I5 (task-based fMRI study) and I9 (task concerns context processing/cognitive control, an executive function domain). Inclusion criteria not met / could not be verified due to incomplete full text: I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map), I8 (reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures), I10 (reported participant age and confirmation of healthy sample status). Given E8 and the incomplete full text, the study must be excluded for this meta-analysis of healthy adult executive-function activations.

This is an fMRI (task-based) study of executive control (cued task switching) in healthy adults (ages 21–33). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent/congruent vs neutral ‘critical’ trials) and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported activation foci (tables/figures) and cluster-level correction. Participant demographics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting baseline only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy sample) apply. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met.

This is an event-related fMRI study of interference resolution/inhibitory control (executive function: working memory/inhibition) using task-based paradigms (recent negative probe). It reports within-participant contrasts (interference vs control) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with thresholding and Talairach coordinates (tables/figures). Participant details (healthy adults, mean age 23, range 21–26) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigm are fully reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies I5–I10 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study using the Stop Signal Task (inhibition) in healthy adults (N=14, age 22–35), reporting group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses with whole-brain correction and coordinates. The design includes within-participant contrasts/deconvolution separating response, error detection, and post-error slowing (i.e., task vs active control trial types). The paper reports participant demographics, imaging modality, and task paradigm. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of an executive function (spatial working memory using an n-back task) that includes healthy adult participants. It reports within-participant contrasts (2-back vs 0-back), performs group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) second-level SPM analyses, and presents whole-brain results with coordinates, ROI and cluster statistics. Participant ages and healthy/control status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. The paper provides separate within-group results for healthy controls (and for MS patients), satisfying the meta-analysis requirement to derive healthy adult task activations. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study reports task-based, within-subject contrasts between motor sequence conditions that manipulate internal modulation/initiation (e.g., TATA vs 1 Hz), which maps onto the executive domain of initiation/planning. Group-level, whole-brain (RFX) voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM maps, thresholds, coordinates), and results are presented in figures/tables. Participants are healthy adults (n=10, ages 23–42), imaging modality and task paradigm are fully described. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study uses a task that elicits cognitive interference (semantic–prosodic conflict) analogous to Stroop-like executive control tasks, and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses contrasting incongruent (CONF) vs congruent (NOCONF) conditions. Participants are healthy adults (ages 24–38). Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigm, behavioral results, and whole-brain statistical results are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function activations and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This article reports task-based fMRI of working memory (an executive function) with healthy control participants and patients. It includes within-participant contrasts of working memory tasks versus active control tasks (letter-case and form-judgment control conditions). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (cluster- and FWE-corrected results, with coordinates/tables and figures). Participant demographics and healthy sample matching are described; imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigms are fully detailed. Although the sample includes patients, the paper provides within-group healthy control activation maps suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function in healthy adults. Full text content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this is an fMRI study of a stop-signal (inhibition) task in healthy adults and reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., STOP vs GO, STOP-success vs STOP-fail) with participant ages and task details (meets I5, I6, I9, I10), the analyses are ROI-focused and the report does not provide a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map. The authors explicitly restricted analyses to anatomically defined ROIs and did not perform or report whole-brain group-level voxelwise results. Therefore this study violates exclusion criterion E3 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) and fails inclusion criterion I7 (no group-level whole-brain map). Full text appears complete. Exclusion based on E3; included criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10; inclusion criterion not met: I7.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory and selective attention (executive domains) in healthy adult participants. It includes within-participant contrasts of executive tasks vs an active control (STERN: NT vs CT) and attention conditions (TO vs DO), and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group maps, z-thresholds, cluster correction). Participant health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are described; demographic matching and exclusion criteria are reported (see Table 1). The paper therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not violate exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation maps, and uses active control contrasts). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria met.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest analyses (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps are presented in this paper) and primarily uses task vs. fixation (rest) contrasts rather than an active control condition; additionally, the sample includes clinical participants (schizophrenia) and is not restricted to healthy adults. (a) Exclusion IDs met: E3 (ROI-only, no whole-brain results), E6 (rest/fixation used as the primary baseline for key contrasts), E8 (sample not restricted to healthy individuals). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI including working memory), I9 (task within executive function domain — working memory), I10 (reported participant demographics, healthy sample status for control group, imaging modality, and task paradigm). (c) Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition for the executive-task contrasts), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map presented in this full text). Thus the study does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and is excluded.

This fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI to probe the central executive component of working memory (I5,I9), reports within-participant contrasts of task conditions (high-demand vs. low-demand subtraction) that serve as active task comparisons (I6), and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM second-level t-tests with reported coordinates and figures (I7,I8). Relevant participant information is provided (healthy native Chinese adults, ages 21–26), imaging modality and detailed task paradigm are described (I10). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-age-range/clinical samples) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive control/dual-task processing in healthy adults (ages 19–32). It reports within-subject task contrasts (DM>SM, SM>SP) and pre/post training comparisons (Time × Group, Time × Group × Condition). The manuscript includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-thresholded Z-stat maps) and tables/figures describing whole-head results as well as coordinate tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigms are reported. Although hypothesis-driven ROI analyses are used, whole-brain results are also provided (including DLPFC increases and Time × Group whole-head maps), so the study is not ROI-only. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI, task-based, whole-brain group study in healthy adults reporting within-subject contrasts (fixed vs random sequence; task vs visual control). However, the paradigm is an implicit motor sequence learning (Double Serial Reaction Time) task aimed at procedural learning; it is not a canonical executive-function task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility) despite authors’ discussion of working-memory/monitoring contributions. Therefore it fails the requirement that tasks fall within established executive function domains (I9) and does not clearly meet I5 (assessment of executive function/cognitive control). Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I6, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I9. No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: n=4, ages 20–30), with clearly described task paradigm (cue–target learned irrelevance task) and participant details. It includes within-subject contrasts (cued vs non-cued; pre-exposed vs non-pre-exposed) using an active control condition, and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation mapping (FPQ maps transformed to standard space, tables and figures with stereotaxic coordinates). The task probes attentional/associative learning processes closely related to vigilance/attentional control, which fits within the executive function domains listed. Imaging modality, methods, and results are reported in full. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy within-group contrast, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/no healthy sample) are violated. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study using a 2-back working memory task (an executive function domain). It reports within-participant contrasts among task conditions (Word, Cross, Within), including direct comparisons (e.g., Cross vs Within) and percent signal changes across conditions. Group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses were performed with FDR correction and reported activations with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults (ages 20–28), imaging modality and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, active task contrasts beyond rest are reported, healthy adult sample within range). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is an fMRI task-based investigation with whole-brain group analyses in healthy adults (12 males, age 18–30). However, the paradigm primarily investigates imitation/perception–action matching and social-cognitive processes rather than a canonical executive function task. Although the authors discuss working memory and error-detection, the task does not clearly fall within established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation) as required by I9. Therefore it fails I5 (assessment of executive function/cognitive control) and I9 (task within established executive domains). Consequently I6 is not met because the within-participant contrasts are not contrasts of an identified executive function task vs an active control. The paper does meet I7, I8, and I10 (whole-brain group analyses, coordinates/tables reported, and participant/sample/imaging details provided). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive control (color–word Stroop) in healthy adults (age 24–40). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; one-word vs four-word blocks) and group-level mixed-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME) with peak coordinates in tables and ROI follow-ups. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Although the study meets multiple inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI (I5: counting Stroop task; I6: within-participant interference–neutral contrast; I7: group-level whole-brain random-effects statistical maps; I8: coordinates/figures reported; I9: task maps to inhibition executive domain; I10: reports ages, healthy-control status, imaging modality, and paradigm), it includes clinical (multiple sclerosis) patients alongside healthy controls and is not restricted to healthy adults, thus violating exclusion criterion E8. The presence of a mixed clinical sample (and one control aged 61 slightly exceeding the 18–60 range) prevents inclusion in a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adult activations. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study probing cognitive control/monitoring (representational conflict resolution) during language perception. It includes within-subject contrasts of task vs active control (misspelled vs correctly spelled; syntactically incorrect vs correct), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded and cluster-corrected; tables/figures provided), and provides participant demographics confirming a healthy adult sample (ages 18–26), imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigms. The task probes executive function domain of cognitive control/conflict resolution (analogous to inhibition/cognitive flexibility). No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain results are reported, it is not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, empirical, healthy adult sample). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 18–28). It reports within-subject contrasts between binding conditions and an active single-item non-binding baseline, conducts group-level, whole-brain (second-level voxelwise) analyses (with FDR correction), and presents whole-brain results in figures/tables. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Exclusion met: E6 — the study uses an OFF (black screen) baseline as the control condition (block ON vs OFF) and does not include an active control task, so it meets the exclusion criterion for using rest/fixation as the only baseline without an active control. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — 3-back working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables/coordinates), I9 (working memory is an established executive domain), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 — there is no within-participant contrast against an active control condition (task contrasts are relative to OFF/fixation). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to meet I6 and for meeting exclusion E6.

This study is excluded because it violates the review age- and baseline-related exclusion criteria. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (sample includes participants aged 7–15 in addition to adults, i.e., not restricted to healthy 18–60-year-olds) and E6 (task contrasts use rest/fixation as baseline blocks rather than an active control condition). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported statistical maps/coordinates), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and described), I9 (working memory is an executive function domain), and I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast versus an active control condition; contrasts are WM vs rest). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it includes participants outside the eligible age range (subjects aged 18–80), thereby meeting exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET study of cognitive tasks), I6 (within-participant contrasts: task minus active sensorimotor control), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM and voxel-wise maps), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and illustrated), I9 (includes executive function task: WCST; RPM contains a working-memory/abstract reasoning component), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample screening, imaging modality and task paradigms). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because inclusion criteria are otherwise satisfied but participant age range violates the review’s 18–60 restriction, the study must be excluded per E8.

Meets all inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI study of working memory (executive function) with a within-subject contrast (2-back vs 0-back) and a second-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analysis reported with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults (ages 25–47), modality and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are violated (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes active control 0-back, not between-group patient comparison, participants within 18–60). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore this study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is a within-subject, task-based fMRI study in healthy young adults reporting whole-brain group-level (random-effects SPM) voxelwise contrasts. Tasks include spatial working memory and sustained spatial attention (established executive domains). The authors report within-participant contrasts of each executive task delay period versus an active control delay, as well as laterality contrasts, with whole-brain statistics and peak coordinates. Participant demographics (n=18, mean age 23.4, healthy, non-smokers), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are described in detail. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, active control used, empirical fMRI in healthy adults within 18–60).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory updating (an executive function) in healthy adults (N=16, ages 19–34). The design includes within-subject contrasts (update vs. hold; rule vs. number updates) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction; whole-brain results and coordinates are reported (supplemental tables). Participant health, age range, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are described. The task falls squarely within the working memory/executive function domain. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (operation span), an executive function task. It reports within-participant contrasts (Concrete vs Abstract OST and comparisons vs an active baseline), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds and reported coordinates/figures. Participant sample is healthy adults (N=13 initial, 12 analyzed), ages 20–30, imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are fully described. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control/executive function (context representation and maintenance, selection) in healthy adults (N=16, ages 21–34) using the missing-letter task. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (context vs neutral; context-appropriate vs context-inappropriate; high vs low selection demand) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported activations and coordinates. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults explicitly comparing deceptive (lie) vs truthful responses and false vs true recognition. Deception contrasts (Lie vs Truth) constitute within-subject executive/cognitive-control task contrasts, analyzed at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise random-effects statistics and reported coordinates/thresholds. Participants are healthy adults (n=20, age range 19–28). Imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant health/age are all reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study includes a within-subject executive function contrast (Reverse vs Go) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses for both healthy controls and patients, with coordinates and t-maps. The task is an inhibition/cognitive-control paradigm (response reversal), modality is fMRI, participant ages and healthy control status are reported, and methods/results/discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, or absence of within-group healthy contrasts) are met. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

Excluded because the study uses fixation (rest) as the baseline for its primary task analyses and does not present a within-participant contrast of the executive (working memory) task against an active control task; thus it violates exclusion criterion E6. The paper does meet multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (fMRI study of working memory/executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps are reported), I8 (whole-brain results presented in figures/tables/text), I9 (task falls within executive function domain — working memory), and I10 (reports participant/sample, imaging modality, and task details). Inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast of executive task vs an active control) is not met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore study is not eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of cognitive control during selective retrieval (memory suppression and selection) in healthy adults. It reports within-participant task contrasts (e.g., successful vs unsuccessful retrieval; first vs third successful retrieval) indexing executive control demands, uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported coordinates and figures/supplementary tables, and provides participant demographics (ages 18–32), health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. The task maps onto executive domains (inhibition/selection/conflict monitoring). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain task activation maps; not connectivity-only; includes active null-event baseline; healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 25.5) that reports within-participant contrasts comparing executive-like task conditions (Timing, Sequencing, Simple). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with corrected thresholds and condition contrasts (e.g., Timing–Simple, Sequencing–Simple) and reports activation loci and tables/figures. The task manipulations target initiation/timing and sequencing—executive domains that include initiation and cognitive control—and the manuscript reports participant demographics, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigms. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active task contrasts beyond rest, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an fMRI study of an executive-function task (visual N-back working memory) in adults, with within-subject contrasts (N-back vs 0-back active control) and parametric load contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (paired t-tests, corrected maps; activation images and tables provided). Participant information (age range/mean, health status—‘healthy smokers’ with exclusion of neurological/psychiatric disorders except nicotine dependence), imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient vs control only, resting-state only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical sample) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study directly assesses executive-control processes (inhibition/conflict monitoring) in healthy young adults using task-based paradigms (Piaget-like interference task vs control). It reports within-subject contrasts comparing the executive (INT) condition to an active control (COV) and uses reference control tasks (REFINT/REFCOV), computing group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g. [(INT−REFINT)−(COV−REFCOV)]), with tables/figures and coordinate reporting. Participant demographics (n=9, mean age 23.2, healthy, right-handed), imaging modality (fMRI) and detailed task methods are provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (n=19, mean age 24.9) using task-based antisaccade paradigms that probe response inhibition and volitional saccade generation (executive control domain: inhibition). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., main effect of inhibition: Conditions 1 & 3 > 2 & 4; main effect of generation; interactions) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted with SPM5 (FDR-corrected results and exploratory uncorrected maps). Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures with coordinates. Participant demographics, healthy status screening, imaging modality (fMRI 1.5T), and full task methods/results/discussion are provided. Thus inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

Exclusion E3 met: the study reports region-of-interest (small-volume) corrected analyses within a priori ROIs rather than a reported group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function - Go/NoGo inhibition), I6 (within-participant contrasts reported, e.g., No Go vs Go within healthy controls and patients), I8 (results reported with coordinates/tables and figures), I9 (task falls under inhibition executive domain), I10 (participant details, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no clear whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical map was reported; analyses were restricted to ROI/small-volume searches). Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to provide whole-brain activation maps required by the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 22–25) using a delayed matching-to-sample paradigm that probes mismatch/conflict processing (working memory/executive function). The study reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent) and group-level whole-brain analyses (Talairach normalization, group composite maps, cluster-filtered voxelwise contrasts with thresholding and figures), and provides participant demographics, imaging modality, and task details. All required information for inclusion is present and no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses active control conditions, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/NoGo), an executive function (inhibition). It reports within-participant contrasts of successful inhibitions (STOPS) relative to baseline/ongoing Go trials (an active control), and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (AFNI; cluster and voxel thresholds reported) with coordinates/tables/figures. Participant information (n=71, ages 18–46, healthy status), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activations, healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 28.6). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (high vs low load) for the working memory task and for motoric rehearsal and uses conjunctions (WM AND NOT MR) to identify regions unique to working memory, effectively comparing the executive task to an active control. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported, with coordinates and figures provided. Imaging modality, participant health/age, and task paradigm are clearly described. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although this is an event-related fMRI study of spatial working memory in healthy adults with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported (coordinates/tables) and full participant/task information, it does not present a within-participant contrast of the executive task against an active control condition as required. The reported contrasts are lateralization comparisons (e.g., left vs. right memory field) and delay-period activity often compared to fixation/ITI baseline or to filled vs. unfilled delay variants; the primary contrasts of interest use fixation as baseline or compare memory-field laterality rather than an active control task. Thus Inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied, and Exclusion criterion E6 (use of rest/fixation as only baseline without an active control) applies. Other inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Full text is complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (15 right-handed women, age 18–31) using a delayed-response working memory task with emotional, neutral, and scrambled distracters (working memory = executive function). The study reports within-subject contrasts (emotional vs neutral vs scrambled distracters; correct vs incorrect trials) and trial-based analyses. Group-level, random-effects voxelwise analyses are described and peak coordinates and t-values are reported (whole-brain maps/coordinates reported), and conjunction analyses identify inferior frontal cortex regions; results are reported as coordinates and figures. Necessary participant, modality, and paradigm details are provided. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, not only connectivity/rest, not between-group only, not non-empirical, and participants are within the 18–60 healthy range. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusion).

Exclusion E8 met: the study’s relevant task (counting Stroop) data for healthy controls include participants aged 10–22 (mean 15.43), i.e., minors <18 and thus the sample is not restricted to healthy adults 18–60 required by this meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function/cognitive control), I6 (within-subject interference vs neutral contrast/active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported, SPM2, FWER-corrected), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: inhibition/cognitive control), I10 (participant age, healthy control status, imaging modality and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none of I5–I10 are absent; however the study violates exclusion E8 (age range/participant restriction). Full text appears complete: fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study includes a task-based fMRI Stroop color-word interference experiment (an inhibition executive function task) with within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs. neutral). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (activation maps at corrected P < 0.001), and results are described in the text and figures. Participants were healthy adults aged 23–29. Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigm, and participant details are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations in healthy adults and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (executive function domain) with healthy adult participants (ages 18–33). The design includes within-subject contrasts (Remember Face/Remember Scene vs Remember Both) and other within-participant contrasts; group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (one-sample t tests, conjunctions, ANOVAs) with peak coordinates and figures. The paper reports participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm in detail. No exclusion criteria are violated. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so it is complete for screening purposes.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function domain) in healthy adults that reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and coordinates. The paper includes within-subject contrasts that isolate task components (e.g., D4 vs D0 delay contrast, 12 vs 8 s probe contrast) in addition to task vs fixation contrasts, meeting the requirement for within-participant contrasts against active task conditions. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI), and task paradigm (Sternberg Item Recognition Paradigm adapted for event-related fMRI) are all reported. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Therefore this study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). It includes within-subject contrasts (high vs low memory load; and an active nonmemory control), reports group-level analyses and provides whole-brain exploratory activation maps and coordinate tables for controls and alcoholics (Tables 2–5, including controls alone), and reports participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details. Although the primary inferential analysis used ROIs, the paper includes group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) results reported in tables/figures as described in the text, satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement. Healthy control within-group activations are available, allowing inclusion in a meta-analysis of healthy adult executive function activations. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered based on the full text provided. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy young adults reporting group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) contrasts (mental rotation Rotation>Control; object-decision Intact>Scrambled) with SPMs and coordinate tables. The mental rotation task involves manipulation of visuospatial representations (a form of working memory/mental transformation) and the paper explicitly discusses recruitment of VLPFC areas implicated in working memory, attention, and cognitive control. Active within-subject control conditions are used (no-rotation control; scrambled images). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of proactive interference resolution, a form of executive control/inhibition.
