It reports within-subject contrasts among task conditions (I-PI vs N-PI; C-PI vs N-PI; I-PI vs C-PI), uses group-level voxelwise SPM99 random-effects analyses with whole-brain multiple-comparison thresholds (and reports activation maps and a table of coordinates), and provides participant age range, healthy status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

While this is an event-related fMRI study with group-level whole-brain voxelwise results and clearly reported coordinates/figures and participant/imaging details, it does not target an executive function/cognitive-control task as required. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures and described in text), I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study investigates episodic associative memory encoding, not an executive-function or cognitive-control task), I6 (contrasts are subsequent-memory effects, not within-participant contrasts of an executive task vs an active control), I9 (tasks fall under episodic associative memory rather than an established executive-function domain such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis focused on executive function task activations.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants using an n-back working memory task (executive function) with within-subject contrasts (2-back vs 1-back). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (tables/figures; corrections for multiple comparisons), and the paper explicitly reports the fMRI methods, participant ages and health status, and task paradigm. The 1-back condition serves as an active control, satisfying the within-participant active-control contrast requirement. The study also reports whole-brain interaction effects (visibility × load) localized to LOC. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply.

This study must be excluded because it includes participant ages 60–74 (older adult sample), i.e. participants outside the meta-analysis age window 18–60, violating exclusion criterion E8. The paper is an fMRI study reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps for a working memory (N-back) task (an executive function) and provides coordinates and detailed methods. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI assessing executive function — N-back), I6 (within-participant contrast of task vs control blocks), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), I8 (results reported with maps and coordinates), I9 (task is working memory within executive domains), and I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Exclusion criteria applied: E8 (participants outside 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Because E8 is met, the study is excluded despite meeting the inclusion criteria.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all inclusion criteria: it is an fMRI task-based study of executive function (PVSAT; working memory/executive processes) (I5), includes within-subject contrasts of the calculation condition versus an active control condition (button-press control) (I6), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (one-sample and two-sample SPM2 analyses with voxelwise and cluster thresholds) (I7) with coordinates/figures described (I8), employs a task within executive function domains (working memory/executive control) (I9), and provides relevant participant, imaging, and task details (healthy control group, imaging modality, task paradigm) (I10). Full text contains Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and analysis), Results (within-group and between-group whole-brain results), and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting baseline only, or non-empirical study). Therefore the paper is suitable for inclusion for extracting whole-brain activation coordinates for healthy adult executive-function task activation.

This study reports task-based fMRI (Switch and Simon) with within-participant contrasts (switch>repeat; incongruent>congruent), whole-brain voxelwise group analyses and provides participant age, healthy-sample status, imaging modality, and task details. However, the sample includes adolescents (age range 13–38), i.e. participants under 18, which violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside 18–60 years). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of working memory (operation span/dual-task) assessing executive function (attention shifting), using task-based paradigms. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (Arithmetic+Memory vs Arithmetic and Memory single-task conditions), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with corrected thresholds and reported coordinates/figures. Participant details (age 22–27, healthy, right-handed), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active control tasks, empirical with healthy adult sample).

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (n=5, mean age 23.8). Tasks were task-based working memory paradigms (phonological and visual) with an active, matched control (letter case judgement), and analyses use within-participant contrasts of memory vs matched control. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain statistics are reported (SPM99, voxelwise P<0.05 corrected; additional results at P<0.001 uncorrected) and activations are presented in tables/figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, resting baseline only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Although the group analysis used a fixed-effects model (limiting generalizability), it still constitutes a group-level whole-brain task activation map satisfying I7. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

This is a task-based fMRI study of semantic event sequencing—a planning/executive function task—reporting within-subject PS>CON contrasts and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses. The paper provides within-group whole-brain maps for healthy Control participants (figures/tables and corrected maps), details participant ages (27–54), confirms healthy control status, and fully describes the fMRI paradigm and methods. The control group activations (PS>CON) meet the meta-analysis requirement for healthy adult task activations. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without within-group healthy maps, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy young adults. It uses within-subject, within-participant contrasts comparing a face working-memory condition to an active sensorimotor control, and contrasts for encoding vs retrieval and memory delay vs control delay. Analyses are voxelwise/whole-brain with reported statistical thresholds, Talairach coordinates, regional volumes, and group-level effects; results are described in text/tables/figures. Participant status (healthy), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described; age is described as “young” (n=7). Full article content (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting baseline only, non-empirical, or non-healthy/out-of-range participants) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI, task-based, working memory (executive function) study with within-subject contrasts (maintenance > no-maintenance active baseline), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses, coordinate reporting, and full participant/task details. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the sample includes children (ages 7–12) in addition to adults (20–29), so the study includes participants outside the eligible 18–60 age range for the meta-analysis. This violates exclusion criterion E8, so the study must be excluded despite meeting the other inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=18, ages 21–38) using a numerical Stroop paradigm that probes cognitive control/inhibition. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (conflict/incongruent vs nonconflict/congruent/neutral, error vs correct) and second-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2, with coordinates/tables of activations. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting-state only, empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete for screening purposes. Inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied; exclusion_criteria none applied.

This fMRI study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses task-based fMRI (I5) with a letter-fluency task that is an established executive function paradigm (I9). The design includes within-participant contrasts of experimental versus active baseline conditions (letter fluency: word generation vs repeating the word ‘rest’; confrontation naming: naming vs fragmented picture/repeat ‘rest’) satisfying I6. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (median activation maps, non-parametric permutation testing, cluster-level statistics), and results are presented as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables (I7, I8). Relevant participant information is reported: healthy control group characteristics, age-matching, confirmation of healthy status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and task paradigms (I10). Although the study includes a patient group, within-group median activation maps across subjects were computed and thresholded, providing healthy-adult task activation data suitable for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 24–33) using a counting Stroop (inhibition) paradigm. The paper reports within-subject I–N (interference vs neutral) contrasts and between-condition contrasts (Trp vs placebo). Group-level mixed-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (Z thresholds, cluster significance) and results are reported with tables/figures and peak coordinates. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are fully described. The neutral condition serves as an active control. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 30.5) that examined complex mental multiplication, a task the authors explicitly characterize as relying on working memory, strategy planning and executive control. It includes within-subject contrasts of task conditions against an active control (number matching) and direct task contrasts (untrained vs trained). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses were performed (SPM; voxelwise p<0.001) with results reported in tables/figures. Participant, imaging modality (fMRI), and paradigm details are provided. No exclusion criteria are met: not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the study used rest/fixation as the only baseline (exclusion E6). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function — modified Stroop), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported as tables/figures), I9 (task within executive domains — inhibition/selective attention), I10 (participant age/sample details, imaging modality, and task described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition; the contrast was task vs rest). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study with within-subject contrasts versus an active control and reports group-level whole-brain results (satisfies I6, I7, I8) and provides participant demographics and imaging details (I10). However, the experimental paradigm primarily probes episodic/semantic memory retrieval (temporal-order and spatial-location judgments), not established executive function domains (e.g., standard working memory, inhibition, task-switching, planning). Therefore it does not meet the requirement that tasks fall within established executive function domains (I5/I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) that uses a within-subject contrast (structured vs. unstructured sequences) constituting an active control condition. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FDR correction and tabulated/figure coordinate results. Participant details (ages 19–37, healthy, right-handed, sample sizes), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are all clearly described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–35) that used within-subject contrasts (object change vs no change; arrangement change vs no change) against an active control condition and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected). The paradigm involves immediate visual comparison and is discussed by the authors as engaging short-term visual working memory/visual discrimination (i.e., an executive function domain: working memory/maintenance). Participant demographics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task details are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy participants) apply. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the record is complete.

The study uses task-based fMRI of inhibition (eye-blink suppression) with within-subject contrasts and reports whole-brain voxelwise activation maps, and provides participant/ task/ imaging details. However, the sample includes both children and clinical participants with Tourette syndrome (not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60), which violates exclusion criterion E8 for a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults. Therefore it must be excluded despite meeting the methodological inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study that used a Stroop color–word interference task (an established executive function/inhibition paradigm) in healthy adult participants (N=7, mean age 26±3). The paper reports within-participant task analyses (task conditions: neutral, congruent, incongruent) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (GLM, Talairach-space group activations, tables/figures of activation clusters). Imaging modality, participant characteristics (healthy adults, age reported), and task paradigm are all described. The design includes active control conditions (neutral/congruent) in addition to baseline, satisfying the requirement for an active control contrast, and whole-brain results are presented. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and does not violate listed exclusions.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults explicitly examining planning (an executive function domain). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing Final Goal vs Immediate Goal during the planning stage, and presents group-level whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise results with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates/tables/figures. Participant age and health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (Sternberg task) in healthy adults (mean age 24.8). It includes within-subject contrasts (e.g., ss5>ss2), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses (SPM5) with coordinate tables and figures, and provides participant, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task details. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly assesses executive control (color-word Stroop; emotion-word Stroop) and reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral; negative vs neutral). Group-level, voxelwise paired t-test maps were generated and thresholded (whole-brain analysis described, with cluster correction via AlphaSim), and results are presented in figures and ROI/coordinate-based analyses. Participants are healthy, ages reported (mean 18.57 years), imaging modality and task paradigms are described in detail. All required information for inclusion (I5–I10) is present. The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met: the study does not report only ROI or connectivity analyses, includes whole-brain task activation maps, uses active control (neutral word blocks) rather than fixation-only baseline, and samples healthy adults within the 18–60 range. Inclusion criteria applied: [I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10]. Exclusion criteria applied: [].

Full text is incomplete (page redirect only). Based on available metadata: title indicates a visuo-spatial working memory task, which meets I9 (task falls within executive function: working memory). However, the provided content does not include methods or results to confirm imaging modality (I5), presence of a within-participant contrast vs an active control (I6), group-level whole-brain voxelwise task maps (I7/I8), or reporting of participant age/healthy sample and task details (I10). Therefore I cannot verify all required inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3-E8) can be confidently applied from the available information. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I9. Inclusion IDs not met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I10. Decision: EXCLUDED due to incomplete/full-text unavailability preventing verification of inclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive control task (counting Stroop) with a within-participant contrast (incongruent > congruent) computed per individual and analyzed with group-level, whole-brain random effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with reported coordinates and figures. The task is a canonical inhibition executive function paradigm. Relevant participant information (ages, healthy control inclusion/exclusion criteria), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a PET study in healthy adult participants that directly manipulates working memory updating (an executive function domain) using a within-subject contrast (variable target > fixed target). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed using SPM95 with correction and results reported in figures/tables and Talairach coordinates. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cued task-switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., task switch vs task repeat) and other condition contrasts (CTI100 vs CTI2000). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests of contrast maps, z-score maps) are described; ROIs were derived from these whole-brain contrasts. Participant details (N=22 measured, 18 analyzed after exclusions; ages 21–35; healthy) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigm are reported. Thus all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group contrasts; active task contrasts beyond rest; empirical data; healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion summary: E8 applied. The study is excluded because participants are outside the target age range and the sample is not restricted to healthy adults: mean age ~66–67 years (older than 60) and the sample includes Parkinson’s disease patients as well as controls (not a healthy-only sample). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI investigating inhibition—a form of executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/tables), I9 (task falls within executive domain: inhibition), I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive condition relative to an active control task was reported—main contrasts are Go vs baseline and NoGo vs baseline; NoGo>Go or similar active-control contrast is not presented). Therefore study fails E8 (and also does not satisfy I6), so it must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on healthy adults aged 18–60.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (executive function) using a complex working memory span (CWMS) paradigm. The paper reports within-subject contrasts of CWMS versus processing-only and storage-only conditions, conducted as whole-brain, voxelwise, random-effects tests (FDR q<.05) with coordinates and tables. Participant details (N=12, ages 19–24, healthy adults), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are clearly described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-active-baseline-only designs; participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references present).

This is an fMRI empirical study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). It includes within-subject contrasts (MEMORY [EAR/EYE] vs NO-MEMORY active control), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (surface-projected group t-statistic maps, thresholds and cluster criteria reported), and reports coordinates/results in the text/figures. Participant information is provided (16 healthy adults, ages 20–42), imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm. Thus it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not limited to ROIs, not only connectivity, not between-group patient contrasts, include an active control (NO-MEMORY), are empirical with healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI, task-based working memory study with within-participant contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (see reported Talairach coordinates and voxelwise thresholds). It therefore meets I5 (fMRI executive-function task), I6 (within-participant contrasts against active distracter baseline/control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (coordinates/voxel reporting), and I9 (working memory task within executive domains). However, the full text as provided does not report participant ages (it states only “six right-handed normal participants”), and Inclusion criterion I10 requires relevant information about participant age in addition to healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm. Because participant ages are not provided, I10 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded due to failure to meet I10 (participant age reporting).

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) that includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., switch vs. stay cues and cue-related contrasts), group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with FDR correction, and reports whole-brain results in tables/figures. The task falls squarely within executive-function domain (working memory). Participant demographics (ages within 18–60), healthy sample status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, resting-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy samples) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of selection (response selection/free choice) in healthy adults (n=12, age 23–38). It reports within-subject, group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., free selection vs externally specified; action vs colour) with SPM results and coordinate tables/figures, and provides full methods, results, and discussion. Tasks target executive selection/cognitive control processes. Participant health, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly probes inhibitory control during semantic ambiguity resolution (a form of cognitive control/inhibition). It reports within-subject contrasts (ambiguous vs unambiguous; incongruent vs congruent) and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM5 with statistical thresholds and peak coordinates. Participant age range (20–52), healthy status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study should be excluded because it does not meet the review’s task-domain inclusion requirement. Although it is an event-related fMRI study with within-subject contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and reports necessary participant and imaging details, the task is a sensorimotor/arbitrary visuomotor conditional-association paradigm rather than a canonical executive-function task. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrasts: DS-DR/DS-SR/SS-SR), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and corrected thresholds), I8 (results reported as maps/tables/coordinates described in text), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (study does not clearly assess an executive function or cognitive control task as defined by the review), I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria from E3–E8 are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This study is an fMRI, whole-brain, task-based investigation of spoken-word processing in noise in younger and older adults. Exclusion criterion met: E8 — the sample includes participants aged 63–75 (older group), which falls outside the review’s 18–60 age range. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps are reported), I8 (whole-brain results are reported/illustrated in text, tables, and figures), I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the study does not primarily assess executive function/cognitive control; its primary focus is auditory/speech perception), I6 (no within-participant contrast of a defined executive function task vs an active control condition), I9 (the task is not an established executive-function paradigm despite incidental working-memory/attention involvement). Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Consequently, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis due to E8 and failure to meet the EF-specific inclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 19–34) that tests interactions between episodic retrieval and cognitive control. It reports within-subject contrasts (Strong vs Weak associative retrieval; Weak>Strong) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and thresholds (SPM99), and includes ROI and regression analyses. The task explicitly probes executive processes (conflict detection and familiarity monitoring) engaging ACC and DLPFC, which fall within executive function domains (monitoring/selection). Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI task study of working memory with emotional distraction in healthy adults (female, 18–33). It uses a within-subject task contrast (emotional vs. neutral vs. scrambled distracters), reports group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (conjunctions, maps, figures, and ROI follow-ups), and provides participant demographics and imaging protocol. The working memory task falls within executive function. Thus all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is not available in the provided content (only a redirect/placeholder page). Unable to verify key methodological details required for inclusion. Therefore I cannot confirm any inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria not met / unknown: I5 (fMRI/PET task-based study), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise map), I8 (results reported as whole-brain coordinates/figures), I9 (task within established executive function domains), I10 (participant age/healthy sample/imaging modality/task details). No exclusion criteria are positively identified from the available metadata. Because core article content (methods/results/discussion) is missing, I exclude the study due to incomplete full text. fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age 22.6) that includes a sustained visual attention (vigilance) task and directly compares it within-subjects to episodic retrieval. It reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses using SPM99 and provides coordinate tables and activation maps/figures. Within-participant contrasts (VA vs ER and ER vs VA, and each condition vs implicit baseline) are reported. The VA task fits an executive function domain (vigilance), and participant/sample, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, includes active task contrasts beyond fixation, empirical fMRI data in healthy 18–60-year-olds). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI event-related study of pro- and anti-saccades (anti-saccades are an inhibition/cognitive-control task), but the primary analyses are ROI/time-course based using single-subject localizer maps and extracted FEF/SEF/IPS time courses rather than a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation map. Inclusion met: I5 (fMRI task involving cognitive control—anti-saccades), I6 (within-participant contrasts and analyses comparing pro- vs anti-saccades and SRT quartiles), and I9 (task falls within executive domain: response inhibition). Inclusion not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical map for the main executive contrasts reported; the localizer/ROIs were single-subject and main results are ROI-based), I10 (participant age information is not clearly reported). Exclusion applied: E3 (results rely on ROI/extracted time-course analyses with no qualifying whole-brain group map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

The study reports fMRI of a verbal working-memory (delay) task in healthy adults and provides group-level whole-brain activation results and participant/task details, but it does not present a within-participant contrast of the executive task against an active control condition. The reported maps appear to reflect task-evoked activations relative to fixation/baseline (or simple task epochs) rather than an active control condition, which violates exclusion criterion E6. Therefore I cannot include it for the meta-analysis.

The study is an empirical fMRI investigation of a visuo-motor tracking task (sensorimotor/motor control), not an established executive function domain. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain GLM used to define ROIs) and I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (task is not an executive function/cognitive control paradigm) and I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains). I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control) is also not satisfied for an executive-function contrast. No exclusion criteria from the provided list are triggered (e.g., the paper is not non-empirical, participants are healthy adults within the age range, and whole-brain analysis was performed). Therefore the article does not meet all required inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function activations and must be excluded.

The study uses task-based fMRI of mental rotation framed as visuo-spatial working memory (an executive function domain). It reports within-participant contrasts (mental rotation vs. passive viewing active control), and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates/figures. Participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group activations, uses an active control, empirical fMRI data, healthy adults aged within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an fMRI study with group-level whole-brain analyses and reports participant/sample and imaging details (I7, I8, I10 satisfied). However, the task is a smooth pursuit oculomotor paradigm (target tracking with blanking) and not an established executive function or cognitive control task (does not meet I5 or I9). Although there is a within-subject contrast (target blanking vs continuous), that contrast does not assess an executive function relative to an active control (I6 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are directly triggered by the study. Therefore it must be excluded because it fails to meet the required inclusion criteria for executive function task relevance (I5 and I9).

This is an fMRI study of working memory (n-back) and attention tasks (executive domains). It reports within-subject contrasts between task levels (1-back,2-back,3-back) and intertask contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 1-back, 3-back vs 2-back), providing active control comparisons. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps and thresholding procedures are described, and within-group main effect maps for healthy controls are reported. Participant ages (controls: 23–50; patients: 22–49) are within 18–60, healthy control status is confirmed, imaging modality and task paradigms are detailed. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, within-group healthy participant activations are present, and an active task control (lower-load n-back) is used. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus the study meets all specified inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations in healthy adults and can be included.

This fMRI study used a task-based emotional Stroop paradigm requiring selective attention/inhibitory control (an executive function). It reports within-subject contrasts (negative vs. neutral; positive vs. neutral) using an active control (neutral words) and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-thresholding and coordinates. Participants are healthy adults (college sample, mean age 18.7), imaging modality is fMRI, and task details are fully described. Thus it satisfies I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This fMRI study assesses working memory (2-Back) in healthy middle-aged adults and reports group differences in task activation, but analyses were conducted using a priori ROI-based measures rather than reporting group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast: 2-Back vs 0-Back active control), I9 (working memory is an executive function), I10 (detailed participant age/health, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no evidence of a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map; results are ROI-based). Exclusion criterion triggered: E3 (study reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis that requires whole-brain group-level maps.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (N=17, age 20–40) that investigates antisaccade performance (inhibition and volitional generation), which clearly falls within executive function (inhibition) domains. The study reports within-subject contrasts (antisaccade vs prosaccade; phase-wise inhibition vs generation) using group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses in SPM2 and presents voxelwise results (figures and Table 2 coordinates) with cluster-corrected thresholds. Relevant participant, modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60 years. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

Exclusion E8 applies: the study includes both schizophrenia patient groups and healthy controls and is not restricted to healthy adults, whereas the meta-analysis requires studies restricted to healthy individuals aged 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study of executive function — CPT; vigilance), I6 (within-participant contrasts: task vs baseline, degraded vs non-degraded), I7 (group-level voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within executive domain: vigilance), I10 (reports imaging modality, task paradigm and participant information). Inclusion criteria not met: []. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs). Therefore exclude because E8 is violated despite satisfying the other inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that explicitly tests cognitive control/conflict (ACC, DLPFC) during moral dilemmas. It includes within-subject contrasts isolating control demands (high-RT vs low-RT personal dilemmas; utilitarian vs nonutilitarian trials with RT matched), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with thresholds and cluster correction), and provides participant demographics (41 healthy adult undergraduates), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm details. The tasks probe inhibition/cognitive control processes, which fall within executive function domains. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses task contrasts beyond fixation, empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion E8 applies: the sample includes children and adolescents (age range 8–30 with participants 8–17), so the study is not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60. The study otherwise meets executive-function fMRI criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts—e.g., long vs short delay trials), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported maps/coordinates), I8 (results clearly described with coordinates/figures), I9 (working memory is an established executive function), and I10 (participant ages, health status, modality, and paradigm reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present), so fulltext_incomplete=false. Because exclusion criterion E8 is met, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults 18–60.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 23–36) investigating a cognitive control (reappraisal/"reality checking") strategy during anticipation of emotional stimuli. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (expectation negative vs neutral; unknown vs neutral) and group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and thresholds. Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are reported. The cognitive control manipulation maps onto executive/cognitive control domains. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only analyses, connectivity-only, patient-only samples, resting baseline only) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of healthy adults (ages 23–37) that includes an executive-function task (n-back working memory). It reports a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition (‘look for X’), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (t-maps thresholded and cluster-corrected), and supplies participant, imaging modality, and task details. Full methods, results, and discussion are present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines sustained attention (psychomotor vigilance task), an accepted executive-function domain (vigilance). It reports within-participant contrasts (fastest vs intermediate RTs and task-related effects) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (tables/SOM referenced). Participants are described as young healthy adults, imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, does not use rest-only baseline as the sole contrast, is empirical, and samples healthy adults). Full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is a task-based fMRI study using a verbal fluency paradigm (an established executive/frontal task) with within-subject contrasts of correct task performance versus an active control (‘rest’ word aloud). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (activation maps, cluster coordinates, and figures). Healthy control within-group activation maps are provided, and participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group healthy activations). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Although the study meets the methodological inclusion criteria (fMRI task-based executive paradigms, within-participant task vs active control contrasts, whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with coordinates reported, tasks within executive-function domains, and adequate participant/age/imaging/task information), it includes a clinical sample (participants with Autism Spectrum Disorder) alongside healthy controls. This means the study sample is not restricted to healthy individuals, which violates exclusion criterion E8. Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis limited to healthy adults. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion IDs not met: none. Exclusion IDs met: E8 (study includes non-healthy participants).

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–36) that includes the emotional counting Stroop, a task assessing cognitive control/interference (inhibition), satisfying the executive-function domain. The Stroop analyses use within-participant contrasts (positive vs. neutral; threatening vs. neutral) and are reported as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with cluster thresholds and peak MNI coordinates. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigms are fully reported. The facial expression task is non-executive but unnecessary since the Stroop fulfills the executive-function requirement. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; whole-brain results are presented; not connectivity/rest-only; includes within-group task contrasts; sample restricted to healthy 18–36-year-olds). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=18, ages 21–29) that explicitly investigates cognitive control/inhibition using a primed dichotic listening paradigm. It includes within-participant contrasts of executive-function conditions (matching-prime vs non-matching-prime; select primed vs unprimed) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with coordinates and figures (voxelwise maps; p<.001 uncorrected, cluster extent threshold). Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion (appears complete).

This is an event-related fMRI study of saccadic inhibition (antisaccade task), an executive-function (inhibition) paradigm. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (ANT and FIX vs PRO) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (with Bonferroni correction), including figures and Talairach coordinates for activation peaks. A healthy control group is reported (n=17, mean age 25.9 ±4.1) with within-group activation information described; imaging modality, task paradigm, and participant ages/health status are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or age/healthy-sample violations) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and is appropriate for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI task-based study of executive function (attention switching within verbal working memory) in healthy adults (N=11; ages 19–41). The authors performed within-subject contrasts parametrically manipulating switching frequency (High/Medium/Low) and report group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (voxelwise repeated-measures ANOVA) with tables/figures of significant clusters (Tables 2–3, Fig.3) and Talairach coordinates. Task falls within established executive domains (working memory/attentional control). Participant characteristics, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, includes active within-task contrasts beyond rest, empirical human neuroimaging, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is a task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory in healthy adults (ages 19–35) that fits the meta-analysis objective. It includes within-subject contrasts manipulating working memory load (high vs low) and visual-search load (i.e., active task control conditions), reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using FLAME with cluster correction, and provides necessary participant, modality, and task details. The study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and does not rely solely on resting/fixation baselines (load contrasts provide active controls). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study that parametrically manipulates working memory load (number of intervening NPs) during a grammaticality judgment task and reports within-subject contrasts (parametric WM effects and Movement vs Binding contrasts). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and coordinates are reported. The task maps onto an established executive function domain (working memory). Participant details (healthy, right-handed adults, mean age reported), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group task contrasts; uses task baselines rather than rest-only; empirical study with healthy adults 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of spatial working memory in healthy adults that reports within-subject task contrasts (Match vs Non-Match) and provides group-level, voxelwise coherence (functional connectivity) maps. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (within-participant contrast between task conditions), I9 (working memory task within executive function domain), I10 (participant age and healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). However, the paper reports only connectivity/coherence analyses (condition-specific coherence maps and group t-tests on coherence differences) rather than a group-level, whole-brain, task-evoked activation map (univariate activation contrast). The univariate activation results are referenced from Curtis et al. (2004) but are not presented here as a whole-brain task activation map in this paper. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-only study without a whole-brain task activation map) and does not satisfy I7. Consequently the study is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (n=17, ages 18–24). The study reports within-subject contrasts (verbal vs object WM; high vs low load) and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and time-course figures. Participant demographics, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is not ROI-only (includes whole-brain voxelwise maps), not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, includes an active task contrast rather than rest-only baseline, is empirical with original data, and includes healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adult participants. It reports within-subject contrasts (selection vs. neutral cue) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2 one-sample t-tests and regression), with results described and peak coordinates/thresholding provided in tables and figures. Participant age and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses an active control cue rather than only rest/fixation, is empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of working memory/interference resolution in healthy adults with within-participant task contrasts (meets I5, I6, I9, I10). However, the paper reports ROI-based analyses derived from individual subject task-effect contrasts and reports percent signal change within ROIs rather than presenting a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinates/tables of whole-brain results. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of an executive function task (working memory recency-probes) with within-subject contrasts of interference vs noninterference. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise GLM results are reported (tables of coordinates, cluster thresholds, and conjunction analyses), and the paper provides participant characteristics (n=27, adults 18+), confirms healthy participants, specifies imaging modality (3T fMRI), and details the task paradigm. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) using a task-based Sternberg paradigm. It reports within-subject contrasts (novel task NT versus control task CT and practiced task PT versus CT) and describes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group t-maps, voxelwise thresholding, and reported MNI coordinates for active clusters). Healthy control participants were recruited and screened (MINI), imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are fully described, and demographic details (age/gender matching) are reported in the methods/table. Whole-brain results are reported in figures and tables of coordinates. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so appears complete for screening. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (age range 25–42) that investigates interference/conflict (number-size Stroop) and reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., incongruent > congruent; distance 1 > distance 4). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses are presented with voxelwise thresholding and tables of activation coordinates. Participant/sample details, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. These elements satisfy all inclusion criteria for task-based executive function activations. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text is complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult subjects performing an N-Back working memory task (an executive function). It includes within-participant contrasts (2-Back > 0-Back), group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses, and reports task-evoked activations with coordinates/figures and supplementary tables. Participant selection, healthy sample status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described (demographics in SI). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts in healthy participants, uses an active control 0-Back). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied.

This study reports a task-based fMRI emotional Stroop paradigm that probes cognitive control/inhibition (executive function). It includes within-participant contrasts (emotional incongruence vs congruence) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses for the healthy control group (voxel-wise one-sample t-tests; results in tables/figures). Participant age, healthy control status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described. Although the paper also includes a schizophrenia patient group, the healthy control within-group whole-brain contrasts are present and extractable for meta-analysis of executive function in healthy adults. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided here.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 25.6) that investigates cognitive control/executive processes (go/no-go inhibition, response compatibility/interference). It includes within-subject contrasts relevant to executive function (e.g., incompatible vs. neutral, incompatible vs. compatible, effect tones vs. neutral), and reports group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures (thresholds and cluster criteria provided). Imaging modality, participant health/handedness, ages, and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy sample). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory in human participants. The study reports within-participant contrasts comparing memory trials to matched control trials (active control with similar stimuli and motor responses), uses a voxelwise GLM and reports whole-brain activations in figures and coordinate tables, and the task falls squarely within the executive function domain (working memory). Imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly described. While participant demographics (exact ages and explicit statement of healthy status) are not shown in the provided excerpt, the full text includes methods, results, and discussion, and refers to human participants; therefore inclusion is judged appropriate with moderate confidence.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (n=17, mean age 25.7). It reports within-subject two-back WM versus 0-back reference contrasts (active control), group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses using SPM99 with thresholded maps and tables/figures (conjunction and cognitive-subtraction results). Participant health, age, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that includes within-subject contrasts of an executive/ cognitive-control task (the distraction condition involving holding a six-letter string; a working-memory manipulation) versus an active attend/look condition. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM2, AlphaSim correction) with coordinates/tables and figures. Participants’ age (mean 24.4), healthy-sample screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. The task (distraction) falls within the working memory/executive function domain. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses an active baseline (look), is empirical with original human neuroimaging data, and includes healthy participants aged 18–60. Full text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

Although this fMRI study reports group-level, whole-brain task activation maps and provides full methodological detail, it does not test an established executive function task domain. Met criteria I7, I8 and I10 are satisfied (whole-brain voxelwise analyses, clearly reported maps/coordinates, and adequate participant/imaging/task details). However, it fails to meet key inclusion requirements: I5 (the study’s primary aim is to characterize synesthetic perception, not to assess an executive-function task or cognitive-control paradigm per se), I6 (there is no within-participant contrast that isolates a predefined executive-function task versus an active control designed to probe EF), and I9 (the tasks do not fall within standard EF domains such as working memory, inhibition, set-shifting, planning, vigilance, or initiation; the DLPFC activation reflects incidental conflict in a perceptual task rather than an a priori EF manipulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI Stroop (inhibition) task in OCD patients and healthy controls, with task vs active control contrasts and voxelwise random-effects group analyses. However, for the meta-analysis target (healthy adult executive-function activations), the paper reports primarily between-group contrasts (patients vs controls) and pre/post patient maps; it does not present a standalone group-level, whole-brain task-activation map for the healthy control group in the text/tables provided. Therefore it fails the requirement that healthy-participant within-group whole-brain activation maps be available (exclusion E5). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (within-participant task vs active-control contrasts were computed), I8 (results reported via tables/figures/coordinates), I9 (task falls within executive domain: inhibition), I10 (participant demographics, healthy-control status, imaging modality and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met (for the purposes of this review): I7 as applied to healthy participants (no reported group-level whole-brain within-group activation map for controls). Full text appears complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI (N-back working memory) in healthy adult participants using a within-participant 2-back vs 0-back contrast, with group-level voxelwise analyses in SPM99 and coordinates/vouchered loci reported for prefrontal activation. Participant characteristics (adults 18–60, healthy controls/subgroup matched for age, handedness, IQ) and imaging modality/task paradigm are described. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (fMRI executive function task), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (group-level voxelwise whole-brain analysis), I8 (coordinates/figures reported), I9 (working memory = executive domain), and I10 (participant age/healthy status/imaging modality/task reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group healthy activation contrast, uses active control). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of cognitive control/executive processes (letter vs visuospatial decision tasks) in healthy adult volunteers. It reports within-subject contrasts (letter vs visuospatial; tasks vs baseline) using an active control baseline (simple reaction-time task), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and corrected statistics. Tasks probe executive functions (response selection, inhibition, conflict monitoring). Participant sample is described as healthy right-handed volunteers (n=16); imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigms are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of executive function with within-participant contrasts and whole-brain maps.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI (I5) to examine working-memory processes (an executive function domain, I9); includes within-participant contrasts between active task conditions (l/r vs b/n and l/r vs d/n; I6); reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM99 with random-effects inference and reports coordinate tables and activation figures (I7, I8); and provides participant age range, healthy status, modality, and task paradigm details (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E3), not connectivity- or resting-state-only (E4), not between-group-only (E5), and an active control task contrast is present so baseline-only exclusion (E6) does not apply; participants are healthy adults within 18–60 so E8 is not violated. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion so is sufficiently complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical fMRI study (I5) using task-based paradigms targeting working memory/attention (executive function domain; I9). The analyses include within-participant contrasts across task conditions/set sizes (e.g., ns < nm, nm > nl) at the group level (I6). Whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses are reported with cluster-level correction and tables/figures/coordinates (I7, I8). Participant characteristics (age range, mean ages), confirmation of healthy sample, imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigms/methods are provided (I10). No exclusion criteria are met: the paper includes whole-brain activation results (not ROI-only), is not a connectivity-only or between-group-only study, uses active task contrasts (not just rest/fixation baseline), is empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults within 18–60, and is not a review/simulation. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling extraction of required data. Therefore this study should be INCLUDED.

The full text reports a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age 24.6) that directly probes working memory and recognition processes (an executive function domain). The within-subject contrasts include game > dot (a working-memory vs. perceptual-motor active control), game > scene, and game > random. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses (fixed-effects) were performed and significant clusters are reported (tables/figures and coordinates), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps. Participant, imaging modality, and task details are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to this meta-analysis are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (contains introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study must be excluded because it includes both healthy controls and schizophrenia patients and therefore is not restricted to healthy individuals (exclusion E8). The paper is an empirical, task-based fMRI study that reports within-subject GLM contrast images (Sternberg working memory probe/encode, auditory oddball, sensorimotor), performs whole-brain group-level analyses and reports spatial maps and coordinates. Thus it satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function—working memory), I6 (within-participant GLM contrasts/contrast images), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (whole-brain results reported as figures/tables/coordinates), I9 (includes working memory task), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample status for controls, imaging modality and task paradigms). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task-based study of verbal working memory (an executive function). It uses within-subject contrasts of maintenance versus an active case-judgment control, reports group-level whole-brain analyses (random-effects t maps and coordinates) and functional connectivity, and provides participant demographics (11 healthy adults, mean age 21.4). Thus it satisfies I5–I10. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses an active control, empirical fMRI study with healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of executive working memory (dual-task WM span) in healthy adults. It reports within-subject contrasts of the executive dual-task (Read+Remember) versus active component tasks (Read, Remember), with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM and coordinates/tables/figures of activations. Participant ages and healthy status are provided (18–31 yrs, right-handed volunteers). Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigms, methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adults that includes within-subject, whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts that probe cognitive control/executive processes during an empathy/perspective-taking task. Although the primary topic is empathy for pain, the authors explicitly test and interpret contrasts (e.g., No Pain: Dissimilar > Similar) in terms of executive functions such as response inhibition and self–other distinction (rIFC, dmPFC), and perform whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported coordinate tables. Participant age and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active task controls, empirical data in healthy 19–34 year-olds). Therefore it meets the meta-analysis requirements for inclusion of executive-function-related task activations.

This is an empirical, within-subject event-related fMRI study of cued task switching (executive function/cognitive control). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and tables/figures of activation foci (coordinates). It includes within-participant contrasts (advance target vs. advance cue and congruency contrasts) that are task-based contrasts between active conditions. Participant age range, healthy status, imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI), and full task methods are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activations, healthy adults 20–29). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an fMRI, whole-brain, task-based study in healthy adults that reports group-level voxelwise results (meets I7, I8, I10). However, the paradigm investigates smooth pursuit eye movements (sensorimotor/motion processing) rather than a canonical executive function/cognitive control task. Although the authors discuss working memory, attention, and monitoring components, the primary task does not fall clearly within established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it fails I5 and I9. The within-participant contrasts are comparisons of pursuit/blanking conditions rather than an executive-task vs active control contrast per the review definition, so I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (n=19, ages 22–34). It reports within-participant contrasts of load (5 vs 3 items) using a low-load active control, a delayed match-to-sample working memory task. Group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses were performed (SPM2) with cluster-level FWE correction and coordinates/tables/figures reported. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete.

This study must be excluded because it includes participants outside the eligible age range (13-year-old children in addition to adults), meeting exclusion criterion E8. The study otherwise satisfies the inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — visuospatial working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts comparing WM events to control trials), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected results and reported coordinates), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables and text), I9 (task falls within executive function — working memory), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). No other exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded solely due to E8.

This is an fMRI study that includes an executive task (Stroop) and reports group-level ICA maps of the default mode network, but it does not provide a within-participant, whole-brain task activation contrast isolating executive function (e.g., incongruent>congruent Stroop) relative to an active control. The paper’s primary analyses are connectivity/ICA-based and resting/task-modulation of the default mode network rather than standard voxelwise task-evoked activation maps for executive-control contrasts. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E4 (connectivity-focused without an appropriate whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task including an executive paradigm), I8 (coordinates/tables reported), I9 (task falls within executive domain — Stroop), I10 (participant/sample and imaging details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive task vs an active control condition isolating executive demands), I7 (no conventional group-level voxelwise task activation map for an executive-control contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (n=14, ages 19–28) using task-based paradigms addressing executive/cognitive control (Stroop for conflict/inhibition; time-estimation for performance monitoring). The paper reports within-subject GLM contrasts (incongruent>congruent; errors>correct; correct feedback>error feedback) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with stereotactic coordinates, tables, and figures (p<.005, contiguity threshold). Participant health, age range, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are clearly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (N=21, ages 20–26) using modified Wisconsin Card Sorting Test set-shifting paradigms that probe cognitive flexibility/executive control. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., A minus D, A minus B, B minus C) and group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with thresholding and peak coordinates reported (Table 1 and figures). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are described. These elements satisfy the meta-analysis inclusion criteria (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baselines, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy participants). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This fMRI study examines attentional modulation (selective attention/vigilance) during an active task, which falls within executive function domains. It includes a within-participant contrast (attend vs. ignore prepulse), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM maps and coordinate tables), and provides participant/sample details, imaging modality, and task paradigm. The paper contains full methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, between-group-only without within-group contrasts, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of language switching that directly tests cognitive control/executive function (language switching vs single-language naming). It reports within-subject contrasts (mixed/alternating vs blocked single-language) using group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise SPM2 analyses with tables/figures describing activation loci (DLPFC, ACC, parietal, etc.). Participants are healthy adults (mean age 21.4), imaging modality (3T fMRI) and task paradigm (covert picture naming with mixed/blocked conditions) are clearly reported. The switching task falls within established executive domains (cognitive flexibility/inhibitory control). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion and tables/figures. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, within-group contrasts present, active control condition used, healthy adult sample 18–60). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults assessing attention/alertness (vigilance), which falls within executive function domains. It reports within-subject contrasts between two active task conditions (distributed vs focused spatial attention) and performs whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM second-level random effects) with coordinates/tables and figures. Participant age range and health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting-only baseline without active task, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory/reference-frame shifts (executive function domain: working memory). It reports within-subject contrasts (AlloSpace vs EgoSpace; Space vs NonSpace) and uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with FDR correction; results are reported as coordinates and figures.
