Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task study), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported), I9 (task falls within working memory/executive domain), I10 (participant demographics and health, modality, and task are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (contrast against an active control). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of task switching (cognitive flexibility), with healthy adult participants (ages 21–35). It reports within-subject contrasts (switch vs repeat), group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures, and detailed methods/results (behavioral, whole-brain contrasts, ROI time-course analyses). All required participant, modality, and task information are reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

This PET study reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts of metabolic effects of acute ethanol (influx vs placebo, elimination vs placebo, influx vs elimination) and correlates resting metabolic activity with neuropsychological test performance. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (coordinates/tables/figures provided), I9 (neuropsychological tasks include cognitive flexibility/attention), I10 (participant demographics and imaging modality reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (imaging was not a task-based fMRI/PET paradigm assessing executive function during scanning — FDG uptake was measured during rest under infusion rather than during execution of the executive tasks), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control condition — tasks were performed outside the FDG uptake window and no task>control activation contrast is reported). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are directly triggered. Therefore excluded because essential inclusion criteria I5 and I6 are not satisfied.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=10, ages 23–32). It uses a Stroop paradigm (inhibition/cognitive control) with within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral) and additional active tasks, satisfying an executive-function comparison. The authors report group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (group average Z-maps, thresholded; Table 1 provides Talairach coordinates) and describe imaging modality and participant characteristics. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. All inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy young adults that examines dorsolateral PFC engagement and hippocampal suppression during an episodic retrieval task that explicitly involves post-retrieval working-memory/monitoring (i.e., cognitive-control) processes. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (recall–classify vs. classify, and comparisons with an active even/odd baseline), presents group-level voxelwise whole-brain statistical maps and cluster-corrected results (with coordinates/tables/figures), and provides participant age, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigms. These features satisfy inclusion criteria I5–I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task contrasts, uses an active baseline in addition to fixation, is empirical human imaging work, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

Although this is an fMRI task study that investigates inhibitory control (LPFC involvement) and reports within-participant contrasts across motion-coherence conditions, the provided full text does not report participant ages or explicitly confirm a healthy sample, and it is unclear whether group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate tables/figures are reported. Therefore required inclusion criteria for whole-brain evidence and participant/sample reporting are not satisfied based on the provided content.

Exclusion E6 met: the study reports task activation contrasted against fixation/baseline (visual fixation cross) rather than an active control task; thus it uses rest/fixation as the primary baseline for the within-participant contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — visuospatial working memory DMTS), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and cluster-wise inference with tables of coordinates), I9 (task falls within the working memory domain), I10 (participant age/health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion I6 is not met: there is no within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition (contrasts are task vs fixation or baseline). Because E6 is violated, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not assess an established executive function domain targeted by this review. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-subject contrasts: easy/difficult vs active baseline), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with correction), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures), I10 (participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality [fMRI], and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (the study investigates temporal discrimination/timing, not an executive function or cognitive control task per se), I9 (task does not fall within defined executive domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that investigates prediction and frequency-matching and explicitly manipulates working memory (detect 1-back vs detect 3-back). It reports within-participant, within-group contrasts (Predict vs Detect and Predict vs Detect 3-back) using random-effects, whole-brain SPM analyses with coordinates and figures, and provides participant age range, health screening, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigms. No exclusion criteria apply: it is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not a between-group patient study only, not a non-empirical paper, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI task-based study in healthy adults (ages 21–35) that investigates inferential reasoning processes that recruit working memory, rule manipulation, and cognitive flexibility—domains within executive function. The design includes within-subject contrasts of emergent relation (test) versus learned-relation (baseline) blocks (active control), with sham feedback to prevent learning, meeting the requirement for an active control contrast. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (thresholded maps and reported activations; Table 1 and figures), satisfying whole-brain reporting (coordinates/figures). Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria from the review (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, out-of-range participants) apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps reported; however, the analyses focus on delay-period activity contrasted against baseline/ITI rather than an active control condition. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (working memory task within executive domains), I10 (participant/sample and imaging/task details reported). Inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control condition) is not met. Exclusion criterion E6 is therefore triggered: the study uses rest/blank/ITI baseline rather than an active control condition for the primary contrasts. Full text appears complete. Consequently the study is excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (verbal working memory n-back) in healthy adults, includes within-participant contrasts (2-back vs 0-back; negative vs neutral), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and statistical maps (SPM2 results, tables and figures), and provides participant demographics confirming a healthy sample within the 18–60 range. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. There are no exclusion criteria met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group activation contrasts, uses active control 0-back, and is empirical).

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults explicitly probing executive processes (working memory, selective attention, response monitoring) during rule-based versus similarity-based categorization. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with Talairach coordinates (tables/figures), and provides within-participant contrasts (e.g., LOW-DISTORTION vs MEMBER+HIGH-DISTORTION; early vs late learning within each condition) that index increased executive demand. Participant demographics and health status are reported. Thus the paper satisfies the meta-analysis requirements for modality, whole-brain group maps, task-based probing of executive function, within-participant contrasts, and adequate reporting of participants and methods.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory in healthy adults that reports within-participant contrasts using an active control (no-delay) condition, uses an established executive domain (working memory), and provides participant age/health, imaging modality, and task details. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task assessing executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control), I9 (task within executive function domain), I10 (participant demographics, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task described). However, the study does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map: analyses were performed and reported at the single-subject level only. Therefore inclusion criterion I7 (group-level whole-brain map) is not satisfied, which is required. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I7 is not met, the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function) that reports within-subject contrasts of working memory versus an active control (letter-case judgment) and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/tables and corrected statistics. Healthy control within-group activation maps are reported separately, satisfying the requirement for healthy adult task activations. Participant demographics, healthy control status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described. The full text (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is provided. Although the study also includes a clinical bipolar group, it reports the necessary within-group healthy control whole-brain results, so no exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, uses active control).

This is an fMRI study of sentence processing that manipulates working memory (DISTANCE) and structural complexity and reports group-level voxelwise results confined to a left inferior frontal gyrus volume-of-interest (ROI) mask. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (within-participant contrasts isolating working-memory-related distance and structure), I8 (peak coordinates and cluster details reported), I9 (working memory is an executive function domain), I10 (participant age, healthy status, modality, and task described). Inclusion not met: I7 (no whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps reported; analyses were confined to an LIFG VOI). Exclusion met: E3 (reports ROI-restricted analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failing I7 and meeting E3.

The study is an fMRI task-based empirical study in healthy adults (ages 20–29) that reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and coordinates. The paradigm involves visual search with contrasts (Congruent vs Incongruent; fast vs slow RT bins; Present vs Absent singletons) that probe response selection/motor planning (intention) and attentional control. These contrasts are within-participant, compare active task conditions, and map onto executive domains relevant to the review (planning/response selection/decision-making). Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task details are reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (N=30, age 19–35) using a dual-task Sternberg paradigm. It reports within-subject contrasts (high WM load vs low WM load) and other task contrasts (WM maintenance, encoding) with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-thresholded maps and coordinates reported). Imaging modality, participant health/status, ages, and task details are fully described. The paper includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or inappropriate ages/clinical sample) are met.

This study must be excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes participants outside the 18–60 range (subjects aged 16–17 were included) and is not restricted to healthy individuals (it includes recent-onset schizophrenia patients). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function — working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), I9 (task is working memory, an executive domain), I10 (participant ages, healthy control selection, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition is clearly reported; primary contrasts are task vs fixation/baseline and load effects rather than an active control). Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory in adults that reports within-subject task-vs-control contrasts and whole-brain voxelwise analyses. However, the sample includes smokers who meet DSM-IV criteria for nicotine dependence, so the cohort is not restricted to healthy participants. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study of executive function/working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), I9 (task = working memory). Inclusion criterion I10 (confirmation of healthy sample status and participant info) is not met because participants include individuals with nicotine dependence despite reporting other medical/psychiatric screening; thus the sample is not exclusively healthy. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is an empirical fMRI study of an executive function task (n-back working memory) in healthy adult participants (mean ages ~23–24) (I5, I9, I10). It includes within-subject task contrasts (3-back vs 1-back; error vs correct trials) comparing task conditions against an active control condition (1-back) (I6). Analyses are performed at the group level using whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses and report peak coordinates and cluster results in tables and figures (I7, I8). Participant/sample details, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are described (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity/rest, include within-group activation contrasts, and sample is healthy adults within 18–60 (no E3–E8 met). The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 20–44) that manipulates visual working memory load and attentional demand — a task within the executive function domain (working memory/attention). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., load 3 vs load 1; difficult vs easy search; interactions) and presents group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise statistical maps thresholded and reported in tables/figures (FDR-corrected). Imaging modality, participant demographics, health status, and task details are fully reported. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only or connectivity-only analyses; not a between-group patient study; not rest-only baseline; empirical data present; participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion, supplementary analyses).

This fMRI study meets multiple inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI of an executive function (working memory) (I5), includes within-participant contrasts between active tasks (category vs location) (I6), reports group-level voxelwise whole-brain analyses and statistical maps/tables (I7,I8), uses an established executive domain (working memory) (I9), and provides participant age, health screening, imaging modality, and task details (I10). However, it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes older adults (mean age ≈65.8) above the 18–60 age range, so the study includes participants outside the allowable age range. Therefore it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Although this is an event-related fMRI study of a delayed-response task tapping working memory, action selection and planning (executive processes), with within-subject contrasts (specific vs non-specific preparation; reward vs no reward), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM results reported, the full text does not report participants’ ages or age range. Inclusion criterion I10 requires reporting of participant age (or age range) in addition to healthy status, imaging modality and task paradigm. Because participant age is not provided in the provided full text, I cannot verify that participants fall within the 18–60 healthy adult range, so I10 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered by the available content.

This is an empirical fMRI study of an executive function (planning) task (Tower of London) in healthy adults. It reports within-participant contrasts (planning and movement execution vs four-move control conditions), employs group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction, and reports coordinates/figures and detailed methods/results. Participant age and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not resting-state only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present.

The paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults using an executive function paradigm (N Back working memory) with a within-subject Two Back vs Zero Back contrast and group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses. Whole-brain statistical maps and coordinates are reported for genotype group comparisons; imaging modality, paradigm, healthy sample status, and methods (scanner, sequence, preprocessing, statistical approach) are described. Although sample sizes are small in the fMRI subsamples, all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met (task-based fMRI/PET of executive function; within-participant contrast vs active control; whole-brain group-level voxelwise results reported; coordinates/figures provided; tasks fall within executive domains; relevant participant, modality, and task information provided). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion: E8 applies — participants are community-dwelling older adults aged 64–74, which is outside the required 18–60 healthy adult range. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not an fMRI or PET activation study; this is a structural MRI study correlating atrophy with behavior), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control neuroimaging contrast reported), I7 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical activation maps), I8 (no task activation coordinates/whole-brain results to report), I9 (no task-based neuroimaging of executive function domains—only behavioral cognitive tests), I10 (does not report relevant fMRI/PET modality or task-based neuroimaging paradigm). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (mean age 23 ±3) using numerical and physical Stroop tasks (executive function: conflict/inhibition). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; error vs correct) and models trial-by-trial pupil-related regressors. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses were performed using SPM2 with voxelwise results reported and coordinate tables and figures provided. Participant health status, age, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; includes whole-brain activation maps; not resting-state or connectivity-only; within-group task contrasts present; healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (students, N=14) using a size-congruity conflict paradigm tapping cognitive control/inhibition. It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs neutral vs congruent), group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with coordinates and figures, and describes participant sample, imaging modality, and task. Core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of conflict monitoring/resolution (executive control). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs. congruent; high vs. low conflict resolution) and group-level voxelwise analyses. The paper includes whole-brain exploratory analyses with FDR correction and reports activation coordinates and figures, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The task falls squarely within executive function (inhibition/selective attention/conflict resolution). Participant age, healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting baseline only, empirical human data, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This study reports task-based fMRI whole-brain group analyses in healthy adult participants (ages 21–38) performing a semantic categorization task with unpredictable between-trial changes of visible target language, yielding switch vs nonswitch contrasts. The language-switch condition operationalizes cognitive flexibility/task switching (an executive function domain). The paper reports voxelwise random-effects analyses with thresholds and coordinates, describes within-participant contrasts (switch vs nonswitch; priming contrasts), and provides participant demographics and imaging modality. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria for fMRI executive-control task activations and includes whole-brain, group-level results and adequate methodological detail.

The study is an empirical task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive control/executive function in healthy adults (n=16, ages 18–29). It includes within-participant contrasts isolating conflict (incongruent vs. congruent targets) and cue-related effects (cue-only vs cue-plus-target), and reports group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM'99 voxelwise ANOVA and thresholded maps) with coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are described in detail. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, not a non-empirical paper, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the study uses a rest/fixation (total darkness/maintain fixation) baseline as the control condition rather than an active control task, which violates exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive/inhibition task — antisaccade), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), I9 (task within executive domain — inhibition), I10 (participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (within-participant contrast relative to an active control condition) because the control was a rest/fixation baseline. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is a behavioral/neuropsychological study of elderly (60+) depressed patients and healthy controls; it does not include any functional neuroimaging (fMRI or PET) data or task-evoked whole-brain statistical maps. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (participants outside the 18–60 age range and not restricted to healthy adults). Inclusion criteria met: I9 (tasks used—Stroop, Trail Making, verbal fluency, Digit Span—fall within established executive function domains). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no fMRI/PET study), I6 (no within-participant neuroimaging contrast vs active control), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task map), I8 (no reported whole-brain coordinates/figures of neuroimaging results), I10 (required imaging modality information lacking). Full text appears complete and contains methods/results/discussion. Therefore the study is not eligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

EXCLUDED because the paper reports only region-of-interest/multivariate decoding analyses (V1–V4 ROI-based pattern classification) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinate/figure-based whole-brain results. This meets exclusion criterion E3. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI examining working memory, an executive function), I9 (task falls within an executive function domain — working memory), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast of an executive task versus an active control reported as a standard task activation contrast), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked map), and I8 (no acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in coordinates/figures). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study is excluded under E3.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy young adults that directly manipulates executive-control components (working memory, selection, monitoring, stimulus–response mapping) using task-based paradigms. Within-subject contrasts (recency vs ordering, stimulus-number and response-number manipulations, recognition controls) are reported. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with tables of coordinates and figures are provided. Participants’ ages and healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. The study therefore meets all required inclusion criteria for task-based executive-function fMRI and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an original, task-based fMRI study of working memory manipulation (executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 25, n=18). It reports within-participant contrasts (color vs angle; conjunction vs color/angle) using a group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM with voxelwise inference and cluster-size thresholding; coordinates and statistical thresholds are provided. Imaging modality (3T fMRI), participant health/age, and task paradigm details are fully reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults (meets I5, I9) and reports group-level whole-brain multivariate (ST-PLS) results with tables/coordinates (meets I7 and I8), and provides participant demographics and imaging/task details (meets I10), the paper does not include a within-participant contrast of an executive-function task versus an active control in the reported analyses. Control trials were collected but excluded from the primary ST-PLS analyses (and no task-vs-control whole-brain contrasts are reported), so inclusion criterion I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded for failing to meet I6.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults using the antisaccade task, a well-established inhibition/cognitive-control paradigm. It includes within-subject contrasts (antisaccade vs prosaccade; correct vs error) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain GLM analyses with corrected thresholds and stereotaxic coordinates. Participant demographics (mean age, healthy status), imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. All required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Excluded because the sample includes participants aged 37–83, i.e. includes individuals older than 60, violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task-based study of executive/cognitive-control processes using semantic and syllable decision tasks), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs an active control condition — semantic vs syllable), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described/figured), I9 (tasks map onto executive domains: working memory/monitoring/decision-making), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 satisfied). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded solely due to E8 (age range outside 18–60).

Exclusion: E6 (study uses rest as the baseline for task contrasts and does not include an active control condition). Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI study probing cognitive control/working-memory and rule-use demands), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and described in text), I9 (task engages executive-domain processes, notably working memory and rule maintenance), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition — contrasts are versus rest/baseline and the main between-strategy comparisons are between-subject). Full text appears complete.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses for the main neuroimaging results and does not present a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the qualifying contrasts (meets exclusion E3). Additionally, the sample includes clinical participants (first-episode, medication-naive schizophrenia) and is not restricted to healthy adults, which violates exclusion E8 for this review. The study does satisfy several inclusion elements: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts were modeled, e.g., NT/PT/CT), I9 (task falls within executive/working memory domain), and I10 (reports participant/sample characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm). However, it fails I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise activation map is reported for the healthy sample/contrasts), and thus cannot be included in the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (visuospatial working memory and attention shifting). It includes within-participant contrasts (Rotation+Arrow vs. Rotation/Arrow; dual-task vs. single-task conditions) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects activation maps (coordinates, tables, and figures). The paper provides participant demographics (healthy adults aged 22–29), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and a detailed task paradigm. Reporting of whole-brain results and coordinates satisfies acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not exclusively connectivity/rest, includes within-group task contrasts, uses active control conditions, empirical with healthy adult sample). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16, ages 18–27) using task-based contrasts that probe rule maintenance/working memory and attentional control during categorization. Imaging modality and whole-brain, group-level SPM contrasts (CA vs FR, FR vs CA, and rest) are reported with cluster/coordinate data. The tasks engage executive processes (rule maintenance/working memory, target monitoring), and within-participant active-condition contrasts are presented. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. Therefore it meets fMRI/task-based executive-function criteria and provides whole-brain voxelwise results suitable for inclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using n-back working memory tasks (1-back, 2-back), which are established executive function paradigms. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., 2B vs PL, 1B vs 2B) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FLAME mixed-effects, cluster-corrected Z maps) with tables of local maxima and figures. Participant ages (22–31), healthy status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task details are provided. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study reports an event-related fMRI investigation of verbal working memory (an executive function domain). It includes within-subject contrasts sensitive to task phase and memory load (high load vs low load) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures. Participant demographics and healthy status (ages 18–28, n=15) and imaging modality (3T fMRI) are clearly reported. Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (seven males, age 22–44) that directly probes working memory/stimulus discrimination (executive function) using a task-based, sequential two-alternative forced-choice paradigm. The paper reports within-subject contrasts isolating executive processes (P2 vs P1 for discrimination; P1 vs spheres for feature encoding) and models a delay period for short-term storage. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM results with thresholding and tables of Talairach coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting standards. Imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), participant demographics/health status, and detailed task paradigm are provided. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, includes active control contrasts, empirical data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10.

Although this is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults with group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and within-subject contrasts, it does not target established executive function domains. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrasts: introspection vs categorization; rapid vs slow), I7 (group-level whole-brain random-effects maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/figures), I10 (participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not assess executive function or cognitive control per se; focuses on self-related introspection and sensorimotor categorization), I9 (tasks do not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Therefore the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of analogical reasoning that manipulates working memory and abstract relational integration (executive processes). It reports within-subject contrasts (ANA vs CAT, ANA vs SEM, CAT vs SEM) against active control tasks, uses whole-brain voxelwise group analyses (SPM99) with coordinates and figures, and provides participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task details. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., it is not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-groups-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, nor outside the 18–60 healthy range). Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study is an event-related fMRI investigation of spatial working memory and saccade selection in healthy adults, so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I9 (working memory/executive domain), and I10 (reports participant demographics, imaging modality, and task paradigm). However, the reported analyses are ROI-based (FEF and IPS) with parameter estimates and time-series derived from these ROIs; there is no clear group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map reported for inclusion in a whole-brain meta-analysis. The figures/descriptions show subject-level maps and ROI statistics, but the paper’s primary results rely on ROI analyses only, thus violating exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only with no whole-brain results). Additionally, a clear within-participant contrast against an independent active control condition (as required by I6) is not explicitly presented. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a working memory (Sternberg delayed face recognition) task in healthy adults (ages 22–27), meeting the review objective of executive function activations. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (match vs nonmatch) during the response period and reports both ROI and a whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analysis (Talairach-normalized t maps, voxelwise thresholding), with coordinates and anatomical descriptions. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (appears complete). Therefore it satisfies I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, participants are healthy and within age range).

The study is an fMRI task study of infrequent target detection (an oddball task interpreted as engaging working memory/attention) with a within-subject contrast of targets versus standards and reports participant ages and healthy status. However, the imaging coverage was limited to four coronal slices (partial-brain coverage) and the reported group analyses do not constitute a whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map as required by I7. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I7. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI task study of subliminal motor inhibition in healthy adults (age 27–34) addressing inhibition (an EF domain) with within-subject contrasts (compatible vs incompatible). However, although the authors ran whole-brain analyses they report no significant whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked results and present significant findings only from ROI analyses. Because the study effectively reports only ROI results with no whole-brain activation map/peaks to include in a voxelwise meta-analysis, it fails the requirement for usable group-level whole-brain task activation evidence. Therefore exclude under E3. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of auditory/visual rhythm reproduction and motor timing (finger tapping) and does not assess an established executive function/cognitive control task domain (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance). Thus it fails inclusion criteria I5 and I9. The analyses do not present a within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control condition (I6 not met); instead the study uses rest as an implicit baseline for several contrasts and conjunctions, meaning exclusion criterion E6 is met (rest/fixation used without an active control). The paper does satisfy whole-brain group voxelwise reporting and coordinate reporting (I7, I8) and provides participant, health status, age, imaging modality and task details (I10). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not investigate executive function tasks and uses rest as the only baseline for key contrasts (exclusion E6).

This is an event-related fMRI study of cognitive control (Preparing to Overcome a Prepotent Response) in healthy adult participants (first-degree relatives and matched controls). It reports within-subject contrasts (RED vs GREEN conditions) reflecting executive control, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise F-maps with thresholding and tables of activation coordinates (Tables 2–4) and figures. Participant demographics, screening to confirm healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are described. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal (task-based) in healthy adults (mean age 21.1), reporting within-subject contrasts (Reappraise > Negative and Negative > Reappraise) against active control conditions (Attend/View). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (FDR-corrected whole-brain results) and coordinates/figures/tables are provided. The task involves top-down cognitive control processes (reappraisal entails inhibition/reinterpretation and cognitive flexibility), satisfying the review’s executive function/cognitive control scope. Relevant participant, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is suitable for inclusion. Confidence is moderate-high due to interpretive boundary of whether emotion reappraisal is classified as an executive function task; rationale for inclusion is provided.

This fMRI study examines working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain voxelwise results, but its control condition is passive visual fixation (subjects instructed to fixate a crosshair). Inclusion criterion I6 requires a within-participant contrast versus an active control, and exclusion criterion E6 bars studies using rest/fixation as the only baseline. Therefore the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function/working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported via SPM and thresholding), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within executive function domains—working memory), I10 (participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no active control; only fixation baseline). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This fMRI study investigates working memory (an established executive function domain) using task-based delayed-recognition paradigms in healthy young adults. It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., SKf > SUf, SKf > (PVf + SUf)) comparing predictive vs neutral/active control conditions, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise univariate maps and statistical analyses. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details are clearly reported. Therefore all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines decision uncertainty and cognitive control during a prototype distortion categorization task. It reports within-participant contrasts (parametric modulation across distortion levels; untrained > trained) using whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with FDR correction and provides coordinate tables and figures. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and task details are reported. The paradigm engages executive processes (conflict monitoring, response selection, working memory/attention demands and training-related cognitive control changes), fitting the meta-analysis focus on executive function activations. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or unhealthy/out-of-range samples) are met.

The study contains an fMRI experiment in healthy adults that directly contrasts single (discrete) and repetitive (sequential) tapping within participants, targeting motor programming/initiation processes. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM (thresholds reported) with Talairach coordinates and figures, and provides participant age range, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms. The sequencing/initiation measure maps onto the ‘initiation’ executive function domain. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-subject contrasts, not patient-only, uses active task contrasts, participants aged 22–45). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the paper meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study examines executive processes (relational reasoning/working memory) in healthy adults (n=8, ages 19–32). It reports within-subject contrasts including parametric complexity vs distractor conditions and a direct subtraction of high-complexity minus high-distractor (an active control), fulfilling an executive-task vs active-control contrast. Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps (SPM99) reported in figures/tables with coordinates and thresholds. The paper reports participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of object naming/semantic context and visual feature effects, not an executive function or cognitive control task in established EF domains (e.g., working memory, inhibition, set-shifting). Although it reports within-participant contrasts (homogeneous vs. heterogeneous naming) and whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates and participant details, the task does not target executive function per inclusion criteria. Thus I5 (study assessing executive function) and I9 (task within established executive function domains) are not met; I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs active control) is therefore not satisfied. Full text is complete. Exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are not triggered.

This PET study reports task-based, within-subject contrasts that isolate cognitive components of motor sequence learning (explicit spatial sequence learning) that rely on spatial working memory and attention (executive processes). It used voxelwise, group-level SPM analyses and reports peak coordinates and cluster results for contrasts (e.g., M_SEQ − M_PRED and M_ROT − M_PRED) against an active sensory control (S). Participant information (N=12; mean age 35.6, range 22–59) confirms a healthy adult sample. Imaging modality (H2 15O PET), detailed task paradigms, and whole-brain statistical maps are described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical sample) apply. Thus the study meets all required inclusion criteria and is appropriate for a meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This fMRI study is excluded because it uses resting/baseline contrasts rather than an active-control within-subject executive contrast (Exclusion E6). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported, e.g., targets>baseline), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described/figured), I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigms reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function condition relative to an active control is reported — key contrasts are targets>baseline or cues>baseline rather than e.g., no-go>go or invalid>valid at whole-brain level), I9 (task is primarily spatial attention/orienting; although it contains go/no-go elements, the paper does not present a clear whole-brain executive-control (e.g., inhibition) contrast). Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only metadata/redirect text provided). Title indicates study population is patients with schizophrenia, therefore study does not include a healthy adult sample and violates exclusion criterion E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals). Based on available information, no inclusion criteria (I5–I10) can be confirmed. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function) — not confirmed; I6 (within-participant contrast in healthy participants) — not met; I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps) — not confirmed; I8 (reporting of whole-brain results) — not confirmed; I9 (task within established executive domains) — not confirmed; I10 (reporting of participant age/healthy status/modality/task) — healthy status not satisfied. Given the clear indication in the title that participants have schizophrenia, the study is excluded. Full text incomplete: true.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (abstract reasoning/sequencing with a working-memory match control). It reports within-subject contrasts of reasoning versus an active control (R > M, R > Rc, M > Mc), group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (FDR-corrected), and tables/figures describing results. Participants are healthy adults (n=19; age 21±2.4), imaging modality (fMRI) and task details are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-groups-only, not non-empirical, and participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive-function activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (executive function) in healthy adult participants that reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., ORG > HIGH, HIGH > LOW) using group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with thresholded maps and tables of activations. Participants (n=15 per experiment) are healthy young adults with reported ages; imaging modality, acquisition parameters, and task paradigms are fully described. The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references).

This fMRI study meets several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing working memory, an executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures and described in text), I9 (task falls within executive function domain: working memory), and I10 (participant age, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). However, it does NOT meet I6: there is no within-participant contrast of the executive task versus an active control condition — primary contrasts are subsequent-memory (Hits vs Misses) within the same task rather than task>active-control. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. fulltext_incomplete=false.

This fMRI study reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts in healthy adults (ages 24–56) investigating maintenance/recall of temporal information with an imposed delay—engaging a classic prefrontal–parietal–temporal working memory network. The design includes within-subject contrasts (Continuation vs Pacing; Pattern effects) that isolate mnemonic/working-memory-related activity, and results are reported as voxelwise analyses with coordinates and statistical maps. Participant sampling, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described in sufficient detail. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, resting baseline-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; thus full text is complete.

This fMRI study uses an executive initiation task (Hayling sentence completion) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinates and full methods; however it does not meet the review’s required within-participant contrast against an active control condition (uses rest/fixation baseline only), and the sample is not restricted to healthy adults within 18–60 years (participants were aged 16–25 at recruitment, including <18, and the sample includes high-risk individuals with transient psychotic symptoms). Therefore exclusion criteria E6 and E8 are met. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (results reported with coordinates/figures), I9 (task falls within executive domains—initiation), I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition). Full text appears complete and contains methods, results, and discussion.

Exclusion E8 applies: the sample includes participants outside the specified age range (reported age range 33–61 years; includes age 61 > 60). Study meets all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing working memory), I6 (within-participant contrasts including task/stimulus-type contrasts), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrast maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/text), I9 (working memory is an executive function domain), and I10 (participant age, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). No other exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Because E8 is violated, the study must be excluded despite satisfying inclusion criteria.

The article reports an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15 analyzed, ages 18–31, females) using a working memory (executive function) delayed-response task with emotional, neutral, and scrambled distracters. It includes within-subject contrasts (emotional vs neutral vs scrambled) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported coordinates and activation maps (voxel-wise thresholds and ROIs described). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (4T fMRI), and task paradigm are fully reported. Core article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups only, includes active control conditions and whole-brain task activations, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory/proactive interference (an executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 23.5). It reports within-participant contrasts (PI vs. nPI; retrieval-phase contrasts relative to a nonmnemonic active control), conducts group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses, and provides whole-brain voxel coordinates and activation maps. Imaging modality, participant health/age, and task paradigm are clearly reported. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study of reversal learning (cognitive flexibility/inhibition) in healthy adults (n=21, age 20–32) with clear reporting of participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., error-feedback vs correct-feedback within IR/OA/RR conditions; choice-interval contrasts) and between-condition contrasts, and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with multiple-comparison correction (AlphaSim) and conjunctions; results are reported in tables/figures. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state-only, empirical human neuroimaging within 18–60 healthy adults). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This fMRI study used an auditory one-back working memory task (executive function: working memory) with manipulated perceptual load (low vs high), providing within-subject contrasts (high vs low load and visibility interactions). Group-level random-effects analyses were conducted and voxelwise whole-brain exploratory analyses are reported (PFDR whole-brain checks), with coordinates reported for significant effects; results are presented as statistical maps/coordinates and figures. Participants were healthy adults (ages 21–31/22–30), imaging modality is fMRI, and the task paradigm is described in detail. All required reporting (methods, results, participant info) is present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, includes active task conditions beyond rest, healthy adult sample). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Exclusion E8 met: the study includes adolescent participants (mid-adolescence; Tanner stage reported) in addition to adults, so participants fall outside the target 18–60 healthy adult range and cannot be included in a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing cognitive control/emotional Stroop), I6 (within-subject contrasts: rejection>neutral and rejection>acceptance using active control conditions), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures), I9 (task taps an executive function domain—inhibition/cognitive control), I10 (reporting of participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded solely because of E8 (participants outside target adult age range).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n=10, ages 25–43) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM) with tables/coordinates and figures. It contains within-participant contrasts that map onto executive processes: Selection vs No-Selection (controlled lexical selection/cognitive control) and Go vs No-Go (response execution/inhibition). Imaging modality, participant characteristics, and task paradigms are fully reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Although this is an event-related fMRI study of executive function (attentional set shifting/cognitive flexibility) with within-subject task contrasts and reported group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses, the manuscript as provided does not report participant age information nor explicitly state confirmation that the sample were healthy adults. Inclusion criterion I10 requires reporting of participant age and confirmation of healthy sample status; this criterion is not met in the provided full text. Therefore not all inclusion criteria are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered based on the provided content.

Although this PET study clearly assesses executive function (working memory) with task-based within-subject contrasts and reports group-level, voxelwise SPM results, it includes clinical participants (hypertensive patients) and is not restricted to healthy adults. The inclusion of patient groups (and at least some participants reportedly above age 60) violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals and/or outside the 18–60 age range). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none of the I-criteria themselves fail, but exclusion E8 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis limited to healthy adults aged 18–60.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 23–37) that tests response inhibition/proactive control within a task-based paradigm (cueing/Go–NoGo adaptation). The paper reports within-participant, group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise contrasts (e.g., mixed-block no-cue vs. pure-block no-cue) and lists identified clusters/regions (Table 1, Fig. 5) implicating inhibitory/executive-control networks. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are provided. The task falls within an established executive domain (inhibition). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group contrasts; active task baselines; empirical human neuroimaging data; participants within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control during episodic retrieval (retrieval-induced forgetting), addressing executive function (interference resolution/inhibition). It includes a within-subject contrast of selective retrieval (selection) versus nonselective re-exposure (active control), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise SPM analyses reported with peak coordinates and figures, and reports participant demographics (22 healthy adults, ages 20–29), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, empirical healthy adult sample).

This is an event-related fMRI study of visual-spatial attention (endogenous/exogenous orienting and inhibition of return) in healthy adults. While it meets several methodological criteria (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with coordinates and figures, and provides participant/sample, modality, and task details), the experimental task does not fall within the meta-analysis’ specified executive function domains (e.g., working memory, response inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) and I9 (task within established executive function domains). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps), I8 (coordinates/figures reported), I10 (participant age/health and imaging modality described). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–36) that includes a working memory (visual short-term memory, VSTM) task—a recognized executive function domain. Analyses include within-participant, parametric regressors (K-weighted and linear set-size) and group-level, whole-brain (random-effects) voxelwise statistical maps (FDR-corrected), with coordinates and figures reported. Participant health status, age range, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

Although this is a whole-brain fMRI study that reports within-subject contrasts and detailed coordinates for healthy control participants, it includes a clinical PTSD sample alongside controls and is not restricted to healthy individuals (Exclusion E8). The paper does report whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses and within-group contrasts for controls (meeting I5, I7, I8, I9, I10), but it does not present a clear within-participant contrast of an executive function task versus an active control condition as defined by the inclusion criteria (I6 not met). Therefore it must be excluded for violating E8 (and lacking the specific active-control within-subject contrast required by I6). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly investigates working memory (an executive function) during a delayed-recognition kinesthetic task. The study reports within-participant parametric contrasts of task difficulty (set size 3>2>1>0) and delay-period memory-load effects, uses group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects SPM analyses with reported coordinates and cluster thresholds, and provides participant demographics (ages, health status), imaging modality, and task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group activations, uses active task baselines, empirical data, participants within 18–60). Full text is complete.

This is an fMRI, task-based study of working memory/anticipation (executive function) that reports analyses in healthy adult controls. The paper includes within-participant contrasts between two active task conditions (anticipatory vs mnemonic WM) as well as activation-vs-rest contrasts; group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) are reported with tables/coordinates and conjunction/random-effects results. Participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are described. Although block contrasts vs rest are present, the critical within-group task-vs-task (active control) contrast in controls satisfies the requirement and avoids exclusion for using rest-only baselines. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Although this is an fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reporting coordinates/tables and with healthy adult participants (meets I7, I8, I10), it does not meet core eligibility for an executive-function meta-analysis. The experimental tasks are phonological (final consonant discrimination and rhyming) aimed at language/phonological processing; they are not established executive-function paradigms (e.g., n-back, inhibition, task switching) and thus fail I5 and I9. While the authors discuss working-memory demands, the tasks are not defined or administered as canonical executive-control tasks and contrasts are linguistic vs nonlinguistic controls rather than explicit EF manipulations, so I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs active control) is not satisfied for an EF domain. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded from the executive-function meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults investigating hypothesis generation/set-shift problems (executive/cognitive flexibility). It reports within-subject contrasts (Match Problems vs active baseline) and additional within-condition contrasts (successful vs unsuccessful; parametric modulation). Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM2) with corrected thresholds and MNI coordinates in tables/figures. Participant demographics and health status (healthy, mean age 26.3) and imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly described. Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete.

Excluded because the study includes non-healthy participants (schizophrenia patients) and is not restricted to a healthy adult sample (E8). Although the paper reports within-subject task contrasts in healthy controls and provides coordinate tables, the fMRI analyses were constrained to a dorsomedial prefrontal search volume (small-volume correction) rather than reporting a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map (I7 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts such as error vs correct and high vs low error-likelihood), I8 (results reported as coordinates/tables), I9 (tasks map to executive domains: working memory, inhibition), I10 (participant and modality information reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no whole-brain group-level maps reported; analyses confined to an MPFC search volume). Exclusion criteria met: E8 (participants not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis and is excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory during language processing in healthy adults (mean age 22.2), using task-based paradigms comparing spatial vs nonspatial (age) recall. It reports within-subject contrasts (Space > Nonspace and parametric RT modulations), group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables/figures, and sufficient participant and imaging details. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical work, nor out-of-range/unhealthy participants). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study of top-down attentional/cognitive-control processes (anticipatory allocation of spatial attention), examining within-subject contrasts (V+ vs ND, V+ vs V−, V+ vs invalid) and reporting group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with peak coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults (mean age 26, n=15), modality is fMRI, and task falls within executive domains related to vigilance/attentional control (a form of cognitive control). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, rest-only, or non-empirical study; participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study investigating conflict during bimanual reaching, specifically goal-selection and movement-related conflict (i.e., response-selection/cognitive control). It reports within-subject contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; symbolic vs spatial) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM, thresholding, cluster correction) with tables of coordinates. Participants are healthy adults (N=19 recruited; ages 18–31; right-handed), imaging modality is fMRI (1.5T), and the task paradigm and results are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group contrasts, uses active task contrasts, empirical study in healthy adults within age range). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, refs). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive function/task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of response inhibition/selective movement prevention (an executive control domain). It reports within-participant contrasts (e.g., stop > go; stop selective > stop all), performed group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with cluster correction, and provides coordinates/figures and detailed methods. Participants are healthy adults (ages 22–40), modality is fMRI, and the paradigm is described. The full-text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (12 college students, ages 18–21) that directly tests language switching using within-subject task contrasts. The primary contrasts (language switching vs non-switching; forward vs backward switching relative to non-switching) are within-participant and target executive control processes (inhibition/task switching/cognitive flexibility). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (thresholds and clusters provided) with coordinates and activation maps described in the text and figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-groups-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full article text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of mood induction (happy/sad) using emotional face stimuli, not an executive-function task. Although (a) it reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and coordinates (satisfies I7 and I8) and (b) provides participant age/healthy sample and imaging/task details (satisfies I10), it does not assess tasks within established executive-function domains (working memory, inhibition, flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). The active control (gender discrimination) is a perceptual/cognitive non-emotional control, not an executive function contrast; thus I5 and I9 are not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8, E5, E6, E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded for failing to satisfy the required executive-function/task-domain inclusion criteria.

Full text is complete. This is an fMRI study in healthy adults with within-subject contrasts (self > other) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with coordinates and cluster tables; participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported. However, the experimental tasks (conceptual self-reference and agentic self-reference/item selection) probe self-referential processing and mnemonic/agency effects rather than established executive function domains (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Therefore key inclusion criteria are not met: I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) and I9 (task falls within established executive function domains) are not satisfied. I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs active control) is also not applicable because the contrasts do not target executive function. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Conclusion: exclude because the study does not investigate executive function tasks as defined by the review objective; meets I7, I8, and I10 but fails I5, I6, and I9.

This is an event-related fMRI study of a Go/No-go response inhibition task (Error Awareness Task) in healthy adults (n=13, ages 21–41). It examines executive function (response inhibition) with within-subject contrasts (commission errors, Aware vs Unaware errors, Stops, Oddball) relative to an active baseline (Go trials). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (one-sample t-tests with voxelwise threshold and cluster correction) and coordinates/tables of significant clusters are reported. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and task paradigm are all described. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so it appears complete.

This empirical BOLD-fMRI study (healthy adult men, ages 18–40, n=24) used a Go/NoGo response-inhibition task (executive function domain) and reports within-subject contrasts (Go/NoGo vs Go). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (SPM99) are described with statistical maps, coordinate tables, figures, and between-group comparisons; coordinates and voxelwise results are reported. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only; not connectivity- or resting-state-only; includes within-group task activation; uses an active control condition; is empirical; participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete.

(a) Exclusion met: E8 — the study includes healthy participants outside the target age range (elderly group age 62–77), which violates the review's age restriction.
