(b) Inclusion met: I5 (fMRI study of executive function: GO/NOGO inhibition), I6 (within-participant contrast: high vs low conflict condition), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task is inhibition, an executive function), I10 (participant ages, healthy status, modality, and paradigm reported). (c) Inclusion not met: none — all required inclusion criteria present. Therefore the study is excluded due to E8.

This is an fMRI study of working memory and control during sentence comprehension in healthy adults (ages 18–25). It includes within-participant task contrasts (syntactically complex vs. simple sentences and varying extrinsic WM load) that index executive function/working memory demands, reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with corrected statistics and coordinate tables/figures, and provides participant, imaging modality, and paradigm details. The tasks fall within the executive function domain (working memory/control). The full text contains methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I5–I10 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only, not rest-only baseline, empirical human fMRI data, healthy adult sample).

Full text is complete. Excluded because participants include ages 21–73 (mean 40.8), i.e., includes individuals >60 years, violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (within-participant contrasts R vs NR and A vs NA), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I9 — the primary task targets semantic memory/object-recall rather than a canonical executive function domain, so it does not clearly fall within established executive function tasks (working memory/inhibition/cognitive flexibility/etc.). Therefore excluded due to E8.

Excluded because the study uses block-design task vs rest baseline without an active control condition, meeting exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI including cognitive tasks, including a four-choice reaction task interpreted as involving planning/cognitive load), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps and coordinate tables), I8 (results reported in figures/tables with coordinates), I9 (at least one task—4CRT—falls within an executive domain, e.g., planning/response selection), and I10 (healthy adult sample, ages reported, imaging modality and task paradigm described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task relative to an active control condition; the contrasts are task versus rest). Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDED due to E6.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults explicitly examining working memory (an established executive function domain) for face identity vs emotion. It reports within-participant contrasts between task conditions (identity vs emotion) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with thresholding and cluster results. Participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, do not use rest/fixation as the only baseline, and participants are healthy adults within the 18–60 range. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are satisfied and the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function) in healthy adults (mean age 27.4) that reports group-level, whole-brain task analyses and coordinates. The experiment includes within-participant contrasts of experimental (working memory) tasks versus active control tasks, and task PLS produced whole-brain activation patterns (with local maxima/coordinates) suitable for meta-analysis. Connectivity analyses are also present but do not replace the whole-brain task activation results. All required participant, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups only, includes active control, empirical, and participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory/selective attention (executive function) in healthy adults (ages 19–30). It includes within-participant contrasts (Remember/Ignore vs Passive View), reports group-level whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with thresholded statistical maps and coordinate tables/figures, and provides participant, imaging modality, and task paradigm details. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=38 females, age range 21.1–40.6). The task recruits executive processes (working memory, uncertainty management, cognitive control/conflict monitoring) and reports within-subject contrasts of task conditions (feedback types; learning phases) using group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM2 analyses. Results are reported as whole-brain voxelwise maps and coordinate tables; task paradigm and imaging modality are clearly described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not resting-only baseline, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study tests memory-guided saccadic sequences with within-subject contrasts (New vs Rest, Familiar vs Rest, New vs Familiar) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM results with thresholding and coordinates/figures). The task explicitly engages spatial working memory, sequence planning and selection—domains of executive function. Participant details (ten healthy right-handed females, age 22–30), imaging modality (3T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are reported. The resting control retained the same audio/visual stimulation while subjects maintained central fixation, serving as an appropriate active baseline controlling for sensory/auditory input; thus the within-participant contrasts are suitable for isolating executive components. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is present. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10 and does not violate exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study reports fMRI group-level, whole-brain activation for a sustained attention/working memory task (PVSAT) in both MS patients and matched healthy controls, and provides participant demographics and task details. However, the task baseline/contrast used in the reported within-group analyses is rest/fixation (AB blocks of activation vs rest) rather than an active control condition. This violates inclusion criterion I6 and falls under exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This fMRI task study includes an executive task (Go–NoGo) and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group results (tables/figures), and provides age, sample, modality, and task details (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10). However, the executive inhibition contrast (Go trials) is reported relative to fixation/rest (no active control), so it does not provide the required within-participant executive-task versus active-control contrast (violates I6). Moreover, the sample includes clinical participants (treatment-naive OSA patients) and healthy controls rather than being restricted to healthy adults, which violates E8. The reported analyses focus on between-group (combined age × OSA) contrasts rather than providing within-group task-activation maps for healthy participants, consistent with E5. Because E8 (and also E6 and E5) are met and I6 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The study is an fMRI, whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analysis in healthy adult participants and reports coordinates. It includes a within-subject contrast (semantic categorization > passive listening). However, the task is a semantic language categorization task, not an established executive function domain (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore it does not meet inclusion criteria I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control) and I9 (task within established executive function domains), and consequently I6 (contrast of an executive function task vs active control) is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion).

The study used event-related fMRI with within-subject cue vs neutral contrasts and reported group-level whole-brain results in healthy adults (mean age 22.9). It therefore satisfies I6 (within-participant contrasts), I7 (group-level whole-brain analyses), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures), and I10 (participant demographics, healthy sample, imaging modality, and task described). However, the task is a Posner spatial orienting paradigm targeting endogenous/exogenous attention shifts (orienting/attentional processes), not an established executive-function domain as defined in the inclusion list (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Thus it does not meet I5 and I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study using a task-based cognitive control paradigm (face-gender Simon task) in healthy adults (N=21, mean age 27.9, range 23–34). It contains within-subject contrasts (e.g., error > correct; post-error > correct; INCO vs COMP) and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction. Results are reported as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables/figures. The manuscript provides participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task methods. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting-only baseline, empirical human imaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is appropriate for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This study uses task-based fMRI with a verbal fluency (silent word generation) vs active control (number listing) contrast and reports group-level whole-brain activations; however, the sample includes a postmenopausal/aged group with ages up to 68 years. The review exclusion criterion E8 disallows studies that include participants outside 18–60 years or are not restricted to healthy individuals. Because this study includes participants aged 60–68 (mean age 63 in the aged group) and is not restricted to the 18–60 range, it must be excluded despite meeting the analytic and reporting inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI, task-based study comparing motor imagery (MI) and visual imagery (VI) in CFS patients and matched healthy controls. It reports within-subject contrasts (MI vs VI), whole-brain random-effects analyses with corrected clusters and stereotactic coordinates, and provides participant ages and other sample information. These features satisfy inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I10. However, the study includes both patients (CFS) and healthy controls rather than being restricted to healthy individuals. This violates exclusion criterion E8 (not restricted to healthy individuals). Because any exclusion criterion met requires exclusion, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite meeting the other inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based PET study in healthy adults (ages reported 18–29 and 20–27) that investigates cognitive control/executive processes (recognition, response reversal, set-shifting, concurrent discrimination) and contrasts non-stereotyped versus stereotyped retrieval. It reports within-participant, group-level voxelwise analyses using SPM (voxelwise contrasts, cluster thresholds, corrected inference) and provides coordinates and figures. Active control conditions (visuomotor controls, fixation/passive viewing) and multiple within-subject contrasts are used. Participant health status, imaging modality (PET), and detailed task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (this is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-state-only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a structural MRI volumetric ROI study of prefrontal cortex degeneration in aging and Alzheimer disease. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (reports only ROI analyses with no whole-brain task-evoked results) and E8 (participants are outside 18–60 years and sample includes clinical AD patients, not restricted to healthy adults). No inclusion criteria are satisfied: it is not a task-based fMRI or PET study (I5 not met), contains no within-participant task vs active-control contrasts (I6 not met), provides no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps or coordinate activation tables for executive tasks (I7/I8 not met), does not report any executive function task activations (I9 not met), and although participant age and health information are reported, the imaging modality is structural MRI rather than fMRI/PET and no task paradigm is provided (I10 not met). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory/executive control (delayed face-recognition with distraction) in healthy adults (mean age 22.4). It reports within-subject contrasts (memory-present vs memory-absent; distraction-present vs distraction-absent) with active control trials (memory-absent trials requiring a matched response), and group-level voxelwise analyses of task-evoked activity (whole-brain acquisition and voxelwise t-maps/ANOVAs reported and illustrated). Results and methods fully reported (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus it satisfies all inclusion criteria for task, contrasts, whole-brain reporting, executive function domain, and participant/imaging details; no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is an fMRI study of inhibitory control (antisaccade task) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses and adequate reporting of participants, task and imaging parameters, the sample includes participants aged 8–27 (children, adolescents, and adults). This violates exclusion criterion E8 (includes participants outside the 18–60 year healthy adult range / not restricted to adults). Additionally, the paper's primary analyses compare correct vs. error trials relative to a non-task baseline rather than presenting a within-participant contrast of the executive task versus an active control condition (I6 not clearly met). Therefore, the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults (18–60) and requiring an active task-vs-control within-subject contrast.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation maps (random-effects one-sample t-tests) with coordinates and tables. The task includes an executive-control/inhibition contrast during the decision phase (bad vs good opponents) implicating right DLPFC and is a within-participant task contrast against an active control condition (good/unknown opponents). Participants are healthy adults (mean age 21.35), imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm (prisoner’s dilemma decision-making) are fully described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting baseline only, empirical with healthy adult sample within 18–60).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly examines domain-general executive control contributions (inhibition/monitoring) to performance (lexical decision). It includes within-participant contrasts that isolate executive demands (lexicality × orthographic neighborhood size interaction; parametric contrasts of neighborhood size, and comparisons of large vs. small neighborhood within words/nonwords), and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and cluster statistics. Participant ages (23–28), healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. The results localize effects to mid-dorsolateral and medial prefrontal cortex—regions of interest for executive function meta-analyses. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study (n=16 healthy adults, ages 21–28) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with coordinate tables and figures) contrasting serial prediction tasks (when/what/where) against an active control. The SPT requires subjects to encode and predict stimulus patterns and detect violations, engaging attention/pattern maintenance and sustained monitoring — processes that fall within established executive domains (working memory/vigilance). The study includes within-participant contrasts versus an active control, reports whole-brain group results (maps and coordinate tables), uses fMRI, and provides participant and task details. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, uses an active control rather than rest, empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults aged 18–60). Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied.

Full text is incomplete (HTML header only). Cannot verify whether this is an fMRI/PET study of executive function or includes within-participant whole-brain contrasts. Based on available information, no inclusion criteria can be confirmed. Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria not met/uncertain: I5 (no evidence of task-based fMRI/PET assessing executive function), I6 (no within-participant contrast reported), I7/I8 (no whole-brain results or coordinate tables available), I9 (task domain not described as an executive function), I10 (participant age/health/imaging details not reported). No exclusion criteria from the list can be definitively applied with the available information (exclusion IDs met: none). Set fulltext_incomplete=true. Further assessment requires complete article content (methods/results).

Full text is complete and reports an fMRI longitudinal study with within-participant contrasts (Spanish naming vs. distorted images) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates; participant demographics and healthy status are reported. These satisfy I6, I7, I8, and I10. However, the study’s experimental paradigm is overt picture naming within a second-language lexical learning framework (language/lexical learning), not an established executive function task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Thus it does not meet I5 (study assessing executive function/cognitive control using a task-based executive function paradigm) nor I9 (task within established executive function domains). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I5 and I9 are not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that directly probes short-term/working memory (an executive function domain) using a pitch memory task. The study reports within-participant contrasts (pitch memory > active motor control) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with coordinates, thresholds, and cluster results. Participant age (18–40), healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activations, uses an active control). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria listed below.

Although this study uses fMRI of working memory (an executive function) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results for both control and patient groups, it must be excluded. Exclusion reasons: (E6) the reported within-group activation contrasts are activation versus rest/fixation only (no active control task), and (E8) the sample is not restricted to healthy individuals (includes a patient group of chronic schizophrenic subjects). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results described/tables/figures), I9 (working memory is an executive domain), I10 (participant ages, healthy control info, imaging modality and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition).

The study uses an affective face-processing fMRI task (matching fearful/angry faces) and investigates COMT genotype effects on limbic/prefrontal reactivity and connectivity. While it provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task activation maps and adequate participant/imaging details (satisfying I7, I8, I10), the paradigm is not an executive function or cognitive control task (does not fall into working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Therefore it fails I5 and I9, and does not meet I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs active control). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (tables and figures) and provides full methods/results. The number bisection task engages executive processes (monitoring, inhibition, cognitive set changes) as discussed in the paper, fitting established executive-function domains (inhibition/cognitive flexibility). The study uses within-participant contrasts comparing task conditions (e.g., impossible vs possible, multiplicative vs non-multiplicative, decade crossing vs no crossing), which serve as active condition contrasts. Participant age (21–30), healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

Although this is an fMRI task of verbal short-term memory (working memory) with within-subject STM vs active REF contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported, the participant sample is not within the target age range for the meta-analysis (participants aged 62–85) and includes clinical Alzheimer's disease patients (not restricted to healthy adults). This violates exclusion criterion E8 (participants outside age range 18–60 and not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study is excluded.

Although this is an fMRI study of executive function using a within-subject active contrast (‘search’ vs ‘maintain’) and reports participant and task details, the group analyses are based on voxel counts in manually defined volumes-of-interest (VOIs) and GLM on these ROI counts rather than providing group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps or coordinate tables. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain voxelwise group results (I7) and effectively reports ROI-only analyses, triggering exclusion criterion E3. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. Exclusion criteria met: E3.

Exclusion E3: The report focuses on anatomically defined ROIs and mean time courses within these ROIs; no evidence is provided in the available text of a group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI) and I9 (working memory task). Inclusion not met: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast reported against an active control condition), I7 (no whole-brain voxelwise group map reported), I10 (participant age and explicit confirmation of a healthy sample are not reported in the provided text). The provided content appears to be an abstract/summary rather than a complete full text, so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=12, ages 20–25) examining executive functions (response inhibition via an anti-saccade task and feedback processing via a modified WCST). It reports within-subject contrasts (anti-saccade vs control saccade; shift with negative feedback vs shift without feedback). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are presented (random-effects group t-maps, thresholding) with coordinates and surface maps reported. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigms are described. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used PET but as resting (FDG) scanning with subjects resting; cognitive testing was behavioral and performed after PET. No task-based PET/fMRI activation contrasts or within-participant task vs active control contrasts are reported, and no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps are provided. Participants include PTSD patients and healthy controls (not restricted to healthy adults). Therefore it fails inclusion criteria requiring task-based imaging, within-participant contrasts, and whole-brain activation maps and violates exclusions E5, E6, and E8.

This is an fMRI study of an executive function task (2-back working memory) that reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses and provides demographic/healthy-control information. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI executive function task), I7 (group-level whole-brain statistical maps reported), I8 (results reported in text/figures/tables), I9 (task = working memory, an EF domain), and I10 (participant age and healthy-control information reported). However, the critical within-participant contrast required by I6 (an executive-task vs an active control condition) is not presented—analyses focus on error vs correct trials and network/connectivity differences rather than a task>active-control contrast. More importantly, the study sample is not restricted to healthy adults (it includes 37 individuals with schizophrenia and 32 healthy controls), violating exclusion criterion E8. Because E8 is met and I6 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of overt and covert spatial attention shifts and maintenance in healthy adults. It reports group-level whole-brain surface/voxel statistics and peak coordinates and provides participant age and health info. However, the experimental task probes spatial attention (shift and sustained attention/counting of near-threshold dimming), not established executive function domains (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning). Therefore it does not meet the review's requirement that the study assess an executive function task (I5/I9). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered by the full text. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (whole-brain group maps), I8 (coordinates/figures clearly reported), I10 (participant and imaging details reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task assesses executive function/cognitive control) and I9 (task falls within established executive function domains); I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs active control) is not applicable because the task is not an executive function task. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is excluded because it does not meet several required inclusion criteria. Although it is an fMRI group-level, whole-brain voxelwise study that reports thresholded activation maps and coordinates (satisfying I7 and I8), the task is a motor timing/continuation tapping paradigm rather than a clearly defined executive-function paradigm (fails I5 and I9). The within-subject contrast reported (CSHIFT vs CNO-SHIFT) is of sensorimotor conditions and not explicitly an executive-function task vs an active control (fails I6). Additionally, participant ages are not reported, so the requirement to report age for a healthy adult sample is unmet (fails I10). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Because all inclusion criteria must be met and multiple required criteria are not satisfied, the study must be excluded.

Although this is an empirical, whole-brain fMRI study in healthy adults (reported ages and sample health) and provides voxelwise results/coordinates, the experimental paradigm does not target established executive-function domains for this meta-analysis. The task manipulates emotional prosody and selective auditory attention during a gender-decision task; primary contrasts are emotion (angry vs neutral) and attention (to-be-attended vs to-be-ignored). There is no within-participant contrast that isolates an executive function or cognitive-control task (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance) relative to an active control condition. Therefore I6 and I9 are not met, and the study does not address the meta-analysis objective despite meeting other reporting criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive/cognitive-control processes (semantic classification, decision selection, response selection) in healthy adults (ages 18–35). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., novel vs. within-task; AT-RR vs. AT-RS) and group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses with coordinates and ROI/SVC corrections. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, it is empirical, and participants are within the 18–60 healthy range. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the study used rest/fixation (a black screen) as the baseline/control rather than an active control task, which violates exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive/inhibitory control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures), I9 (task falls within inhibition executive function domain), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task described). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition; only rest baseline was used). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore EXCLUDED due to E6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–26) that explicitly examines executive-function components (response selection and inhibitory control) using task-based paradigms. It includes within-participant contrasts (Incompatible vs Compatible response mapping) and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak activations and figures/tables of coordinates. Tasks fall within established executive function domains (response selection/inhibition). Participant characteristics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group activations, uses active control conditions, empirical dataset, healthy adult sample within 18–60). Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion; therefore fulltext_incomplete is false.

Exclusion based on E8: study includes participants outside the 18–60 age range (control range 20–64 y; TBI range 21–65 y), violating the meta-analysis age restriction. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive processes via auditory oddball), I7 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text), I9 (task probes executive domains: attention/working-memory updating), I10 (participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion I6 is not clearly met: while the study modeled targets, novels, and standards, the paper reports main effects (target and novel detection) relative to implicit baseline and does not explicitly present a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition (e.g., target > standard) in the healthy sample. Full text appears complete. Therefore EXCLUDE due to E8.

This fMRI study investigates random number generation as an executive function task in healthy adults, uses an active control (counting), reports within-participant contrasts (RNG minus counting) using group-level voxelwise SPM analyses with whole-brain results presented in figures/tables, and provides participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task details. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (includes methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study of executive function (attentional/task switching) in healthy adults (N=16, age 18–45). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (object-switch, rule-switch, object–rule-switch vs nonswitch) using second-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with reported coordinates and figures. Participant characteristics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. The nonswitch baseline is an active control condition. All inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not rest-only baseline, empirical human imaging data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears to include introduction, methods, results, and discussion, enabling complete assessment.

This is an fMRI, whole-brain, group-level study with healthy adult participants and clearly described tasks and methods. However, the experimental paradigms are language tasks (reading aloud and lexical decision) aimed at contrasting vowel vs. consonant processing, not established executive function tasks. Although the authors interpret a right middle frontal activation as related to inhibitory/no-go processing in the lexical decision condition, the study does not manipulate or target an executive function domain (e.g., dedicated inhibition, working memory, cognitive flexibility) as the primary task, nor does it present a within-participant contrast of an explicit executive-control task versus an active control designed to isolate executive processes. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I9. No exclusion criteria are directly met. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of inference/coherence-judgment that explicitly probes cognitive control/executive processes (search for coherence, decision under uncertainty, strategy updating). It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., distantly related vs. unrelated; closely vs. distantly related) reflecting executive demand and inference success. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (Z-maps, cluster thresholds) with coordinates and figures. Participants are healthy adults (n=14 analyzed, mean age 25), imaging modality is fMRI, and the task paradigm and results (frontal/parietal IFJ, pre-SMA/BA8 activations) fall within executive function domains. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-group only, resting baseline only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical sample) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (overt letter verbal fluency) in healthy adult volunteers; it reports within-participant contrasts of the executive task versus an active control condition (word repetition); group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps and cluster/coordinate results are reported and illustrated; reporting of whole-brain results appears in tables/figures and is described in the text; verbal fluency is an established executive domain (initiation/lexical retrieval); and participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly provided. None of the exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group task activations, uses an active control, is empirical human neuroimaging, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

The study is excluded because it includes older adults (beyond the 18–60 range), violating E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive process), I6 (within-participant contrasts: refresh vs read), I7 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked results reported as regional activations), I8 (whole-brain results reported in text/figures), I9 (task maps onto executive function—selection/refreshing), I10 (reports participant age groups, healthy samples, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Note: the provided full text appears to be abstract-level and is likely incomplete (core methods/results/discussion not fully present), so fulltext_incomplete=true.

This study is an fMRI, whole-brain, task-based investigation that reports within-subject contrasts (learning vs distraction active baseline) and provides group-level voxelwise maps and adequate reporting of participants, imaging modality, and task. However, the task is primarily an associative episodic memory/learning paradigm (face–name/face–number) rather than a canonical executive-function task (e.g., n-back, inhibition, set-shifting). Crucially, the sample includes chronic cannabis users (a non-healthy/substance-using group) alongside controls, so the study is not restricted to healthy adults as required (Exclusion E8). Because the review objective targets executive-function activations in healthy adults, and the study fails to meet the domain requirement (I5/I9) and violates E8, it must be excluded.

This is an fMRI task study with within-subject contrasts (Age vs Colour) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported; however the sample is not restricted to healthy adults and participants are older adults (age-matched controls and Alzheimer’s patients), thus violating the review’s requirement of healthy adults aged 18–60. Therefore it must be excluded under E8. Although inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I10 are met (fMRI task paradigm, within-participant contrast, whole-brain maps/coordinates reported, and participant/task/modality details provided), criterion I9 (task falls within established executive function domains) is borderline for visuo-attentional/shallow vs deep perceptual judgments and may not clearly map to the specified executive domains. Primary exclusion reason: E8 (includes non-healthy, older participants outside the 18–60 healthy adult restriction). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of phonemic verbal fluency in young adults and meets multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing an executive function), I6 (within-participant contrasts of task vs active control condition), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (coordinates and figures reported), I9 (verbal fluency is an established executive-domain task), and I10 (participant ages, group health status, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). However, exclusion criterion E8 is met: the sample includes participants younger than 18 years (range starts at 17.8 years), which violates the review’s age/healthy-sample restriction. Because any single exclusion criterion mandates exclusion, the study must be excluded. No other exclusion criteria were triggered. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study reports PET activation (RNG vs COUNT) with whole-brain voxelwise analyses in elderly controls and PD patients and provides ages, healthy-control status, imaging modality, and task details. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task-based executive function), I6 (within-participant RNG vs active counting contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM results), I8 (coordinates and figures reported), I9 (RNG is an executive function task), I10 (participant age, health status, imaging modality, and paradigm reported). Exclusion criteria met: E8 — participants fall outside the review age range (controls mean age 61.3 years, and sample includes older adults) and study includes non-healthy participants (PD patients), violating the meta-analysis restriction to healthy adults aged 18–60. Inclusion criteria not met: none of the I5–I10 criteria are missing; exclusion is due to E8 (age/sample). Full text appears complete.

This empirical fMRI study uses a task-based auditory oddball paradigm assessing selective attention/vigilance (an executive domain). It reports within-participant contrasts (target vs non-target) and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2, p<0.0001) with coordinates and figures. Participant age and healthy status are reported and imaging modality/task paradigm are described. Full text includes methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

Excluded because the sample violates age restriction criterion (E8): participants are elderly (mean age 62.33 years), outside the 18–60 range. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive-related decision processes), I6 (within-participant contrast of activation vs high-level active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis reported), I8 (results reported with coordinates/figures), I9 (task engages executive functions—information integration, working memory, conflict detection), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Full text appears complete.

This study is not a task-based fMRI or PET investigation of executive function. Exclusion IDs met: E8 (sample includes psychiatric/offender patients and controls; not restricted to healthy individuals) and E5 (reports group comparisons without any within-participant task activation contrasts in healthy participants). Inclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs not met: I5 (not an fMRI or PET task study), I6 (no within-participant task vs active control contrasts), I7 (no group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps), I8 (no whole-brain coordinate/figure results of task activations), I9 (no task-based imaging within established executive-function domains), I10 (does not report required info for fMRI/PET task paradigms in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (background, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study does not meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (verbal fluency) that reports within-subject contrasts (generation > repetition, active control) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM5) with voxelwise FDR correction and coordinates/figures. It includes a healthy adult sample (n=48) with demographic information and describes the imaging modality and paradigm. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes older adults aged 60–85 (i.e., participants outside the 18–60 age range). The study otherwise meets all inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive control/task-switching), I6 (within-participant contrasts such as switch > repeat and cue+target > cue-only), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses and reported omnibus maps/tables), I8 (results reported with coordinates and tables), I9 (task-switching falls under cognitive flexibility/executive function), and I10 (participant ages, health screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite satisfying the other inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive verbal working memory (Sternberg paradigm) in healthy adults (ages 19–28). It reports within-subject contrasts comparing an executive manipulation condition versus an active match control, uses group-level random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2), and reports peak coordinates and figures. Participant demographics, imaging modality, and task details are provided. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

The study is a PET task-based investigation in healthy adults and includes a within-subject contrast of an executive function task (MCST) vs an active control (I5, I6). The task assesses planning/set-shifting (executive domain) and participant info (healthy, age 20–33) and modality are reported (I9, I10). However, the imaging results were analyzed/reported only within the striatum (small-volume/ROI approach); authors state that "Only those peaks falling within the striatum were considered" and used a search volume equal to the striatum. No group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map is reported, so the study does not meet I7. This violates exclusion E3 (ROI/small-volume-only reporting with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of perceptual decision-making (dot-motion task) in healthy adults with whole-brain analyses, but it does not assess an executive function task within the review's defined domains. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses present), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described/tabled/figured), and I10 (participant age and healthy status and imaging modality reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (study does not target an executive function or cognitive-control task as specified), I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control condition), I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are directly triggered by the manuscript. Therefore the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is a task-based PET investigation of executive function (Montreal Card Sorting Task) in healthy adults and includes within-subject contrasts (active MCST vs active control). Group-level voxelwise analyses were performed and reported (statistical parametric maps with peak coordinates and corrected thresholds), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Participant demographics (ages 20–33) and healthy status, imaging modality (PET), and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, uses an active control, empirical human neuroimaging, participants within 18–60 and healthy).

This is an fMRI study of overt verbal fluency in healthy adults that manipulates executive demands (letter vs category retrieval; switching vs single-cue) and includes within-subject contrasts versus an active control (automatic speech). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (AFNI, cluster-corrected maps; tables/figures described). Participants are healthy adults (mean age 32, range 22–48). The tasks map onto executive function domains (cognitive flexibility/switching, initiation, controlled retrieval). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Thus the study meets I5–I10 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study of a verbal Trail Making Test (vTMT) probing cognitive flexibility (executive function) in healthy adults (ages 19–43). It reports a within-participant contrast of vTMTB (set-shifting) versus vTMTA (active control), with group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM analyses, corrected p-values and cluster thresholds, and results described in text/tables/figures. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (Go/No-Go inhibition) in healthy adults (age range 19–40) using a within-subject design. The analysis models event types (hits, correct rejections, false alarms) and reports group-level, whole-brain SPM results (FDR-corrected) with coordinates and tables describing task-evoked activation. Participant health status, ages, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (n-back) in healthy adults (ages 21–53). The paper reports within-subject, group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (1-back vs 0-back, 2-back vs 0-back, 2-back vs 1-back) using random-effects SPM analyses and corrected SPM{Z} maps; results are presented in figures and tables of coordinates. An active baseline (0-back) was used. Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality (4T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion criterion E8 met: study includes clinical (Parkinson's disease) patients (not restricted to healthy individuals) and control participants whose ages range up to 68 years (outside the 18–60 inclusion window). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function - WCST), I6 (within-participant contrasts vs active control conditions reported), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with correction and reported peaks/tables), I8 (whole-brain results described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within cognitive flexibility/executive function), I10 (participant age, healthy sample status for controls, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 present). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The full text is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (mean age 23.9) investigating conflict, task-switching, and errors—established executive functions. It uses within-subject contrasts (e.g., correct incongruent vs correct congruent; task-switch vs correct incongruent; error vs correct), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholds, cluster correction) with coordinates and figures. Imaging modality, task paradigms, and participant details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of executive-function (set-shifting/planning) using the Montreal Card-Sorting Task and provides within-subject contrasts against an active control condition (e.g., retrieval without shift vs control; continuous shift vs control). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (statistical maps thresholding described; peaks/tables and figures provided). The healthy control group activations are presented separately (within-group results and inter-group comparisons), and participant age, healthy-status screening, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. Although the study also includes Parkinson’s patients, the presence of clearly reported healthy control within-group whole-brain activations makes it eligible for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (fMRI verbal working memory task — executive function), I6 (within-participant contrast: memory vs control), I7 (group-level whole-brain GLM reported and thresholded), I8 (ROIs and coordinates reported), I9 (task is working memory). Inclusion IDs not met: I10 (participant age information not reported in the full text; although healthy status, imaging modality, and paradigm are described, ages or age range/mean are not provided). Therefore the study fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (I10 missing) and must be excluded.

Although this study used task-based fMRI of an executive function (3-back working memory) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps with coordinates, it does not include a within-participant contrast against an active control condition. The primary contrast reported is task > fixation (rest), i.e., fixation/rest was the baseline. Because the review requires an active control contrast (I6) and excludes studies that use only rest/fixation as the baseline (E6), this study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an executive function domain, with healthy adult participants (ages within 18–37). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (voxelwise correlations between BOLD amplitude and RT) and an explicit within-participant contrast/manipulation of cognitive load (3-back vs 1-back) in Experiment 2, satisfying the requirement for an active control condition. Imaging modality, participant demographics, and task paradigm are clearly described. Results are not ROI-only (whole-brain maps reported), and no exclusion criteria are met. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

The study is an fMRI task-based investigation of cognitive control/conflict monitoring in healthy adult college students and includes within-participant contrasts (preview vs no-preview; high vs low conflict), satisfying I5, I6, I9, and I10. However, all reported imaging analyses focus on two a priori ROIs (ACC and lPFC) with ROI-based statistics and no group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or tables/coordinates of whole-brain results are reported. Therefore it does not meet I7 and meets exclusion criterion E3 (ROI-only analyses). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Consequently the study must be excluded because it lacks whole-brain activation results required by the review.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that reports within-subject contrasts of the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT) relative to an active control task and presents group-level whole-brain activation maps and ROI and regression analyses. Participant age (mean 23.1), healthy sample status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. Although the IGT is primarily a decision-making task, the methods and analyses explicitly probe executive components (e.g., working memory, risk evaluation, and cognitive control) and the paper frames IGT-related activity in terms of dorsolateral PFC and other executive systems; therefore it falls within the review’s executive-function domain inclusion. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided.

Although this fMRI study reports whole-brain, within-participant contrasts (decision > no-decision) with voxelwise group-level maps and provides participant/sample details, it does not meet key inclusion regarding the review focus on executive function tasks. The task (modified Iowa Gambling Task) targets decision-making/risk/reward processing rather than established executive function domains listed (working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Therefore I5 and I9 are not satisfied. Additionally, the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (includes substance-dependent and pathological gambling groups), violating exclusion E8 for studies not restricted to healthy individuals. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an fMRI study of working-memory manipulation (executive function) in healthy adults, using within-subject 2×2 factorial contrasts (e.g., ACROSS vs WITHIN; 2ST-ACROSS vs SUP-ACROSS) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; FDR/FWE correction). Participant demographics (age 21–30), healthy sample status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are fully reported. Results include whole-brain statistical maps and tables of activations and coordinates; connectivity (PPI) is secondary to task activation analyses. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults that reports group-level voxelwise activation analyses and provides participant demographics and task details. However, the task contrasts reported compare task-evoked BOLD to an overall session baseline (rest), and no active control condition is described. Therefore it fails the requirement for a within-participant contrast against an active control condition. Exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline without an active control) is met. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (fMRI executive-function task), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described), I9 (working memory task falls within executive functions), and I10 (healthy adult sample, imaging modality, and task reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of task switching (cognitive flexibility/executive control) in healthy adults (n=24, mean age 25). It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., Stage 3 vs Stage 1, Switch vs Pure blocks) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with Talairach coordinates and figures (Tables II–III, figures). Imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), participant health/age, and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, uses active task contrasts, empirical data, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore it meets I5–I10 and is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of executive function (WCST variant) in healthy adults (mean age 24.8). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing a WCST-like (rule-generation/cognitive flexibility) condition to instructed working-memory control conditions, and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FDR-corrected) with coordinates/tables and figures. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied; no exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Conclusion, so appears complete for screening.

This fMRI study examines divided attention/working memory and cognitive control in healthy adults using a within-subject task contrast (memorize+serial subtraction vs. memorize+counting). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholding, Talairach normalization, cluster correction) with activation tables and figures, and provides participant demographics (age, healthy sample), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), and detailed task paradigm. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study used fMRI to assess a verbal working memory task (an executive function) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with coordinates; participant ages and healthy control group, imaging modality, and paradigm are described. However, the paper does not present a within-participant (within-group) contrast of the executive function task relative to an active control for the healthy participants (the only reported significant result is a group-by-time interaction and no significant within-group WM>control or WM>baseline activation maps for controls are reported). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only between-group/interaction results without an accompanying within-group task activation contrast in healthy participants). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of a visual working memory task (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (ages 18–25). The paper reports within-subject contrasts of task difficulty (6-dot vs 2-dot) serving as an active control condition, and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with corrected clusters and Talairach coordinates (Table 3 and figures). Participant demographics, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, includes within-group task activation contrasts, uses active baseline beyond fixation, and participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be INCLUDED.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I9: the imaging task (numerical calculations/arithmetic) is not clearly an established executive function domain (e.g., working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning). Although the paper reports correlations between baseline prefrontal metabolism and neuropsychological executive tests, the PET activation paradigm used (arithmetic) is not described or justified as a canonical executive-function task for a within-participant executive vs active-control contrast. Full text is complete. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (PET task-based study), I6 (within-participant contrast of task vs baseline active condition), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported via SPM), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), I10 (participant age/health, modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) were triggered.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive function (verbal working memory manipulation vs maintenance) in healthy adults. It uses within-subject contrasts (manipulation vs maintenance; high vs low load), reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with thresholded SPM images and tables of coordinates, and provides participant demographics, health screening, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. All inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the article appears complete for screening purposes.

Exclusion criterion E8 is met: participants age range is 16–23 (includes minors <18), so the sample is not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60. The study otherwise meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive processes like working memory/interference), I6 (within-subject contrasts vs. an active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), I9 (task taps executive domains: working memory/interference resolution), and I10 (reports participant ages, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm). Because E8 is violated, the study must be excluded despite fulfilling the other inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 19–36) using a task-based AX-CPT variant that probes cognitive control/set shifting and vigilance. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., targets vs. nontargets, parametric modulators of bias and reward expectancy) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM results (FDR-corrected maps and coordinates). Methods, participant demographics, imaging modality (3T BOLD fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. Although the paper also reports DCM connectivity analyses, it additionally provides whole-brain activation maps and coordinate tables. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of cognitive inhibition (an executive function) in healthy young adults that reports within-subject contrasts (INT vs COV) and provides participant demographics, task details, and imaging modality. However, the fMRI analysis is ROI-based (AROI parcellation) with average BOLD signals per anatomical ROI; no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or voxelwise coordinate tables are reported. Therefore it fails the requirement for whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical maps.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of working memory (mental arithmetic) in healthy adults, with within-subject contrasts against an active control (zero trials). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level SPM analyses with coordinates and figures, and provides full participant demographics (N=20, ages 20.3–39.6, healthy) and task details. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are met. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Exclusion rationale: (a) Exclusion criteria met: E3 (the primary analyses are restricted to a priori ROI/small-volume tests rather than reporting a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map) and E8 (the sample includes adolescents below 18 years; participants are a mixed-age sample including ages 9–17 and adults, so the study includes participants outside the required 18–60 age range). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI examining cognitive control/decision-making), I6 (within-subject contrasts of task conditions, e.g., risky vs safe selections and inclusion of an active control wheel), I8 (results reported with coordinates and described in text), I9 (task engages cognitive control/conflict monitoring processes relevant to executive function), and I10 (participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task details are reported). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map is reported; analyses were confined to ROIs/SV-corrected spheres). Given violation of E3 and E8, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of planning (autobiographical and visuospatial), which falls within executive function domains (planning). It reports within-subject contrasts of planning tasks relative to an active control (counting) and/or fixation, includes group-level whole-brain task-evoked results (PLS maps, tables of activation peaks, figures), and provides participant demographics confirming a healthy adult sample (ages 18–29). Imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigms, and behavioral results are reported. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only report, not only connectivity/resting analyses, not between-group only, not non-empirical, and participants are within the 18–60 healthy range). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study is an fMRI investigation of creative idea generation (alternative uses, name invention, object characteristics, word endings) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses reported (FWE-corrected) and detailed participant information. However, the meta-analysis requires studies to assess executive function/cognitive control tasks within established EF domains. The present tasks are creativity-focused and, although the authors discuss working memory and selection/inhibition processes, the paradigms are not standard executive function tasks (e.g., n-back, go/no-go, task-switching) and the contrasts are not explicitly framed as EF vs active control. Therefore I5 (study assesses executive function) and I9 (tasks fall within established EF domains) are not met; I6 (within-participant contrast of an executive task vs active control) is not met for the same reason. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I7 (group-level whole-brain maps), I8 (whole-brain results clearly reported), I10 (participant age/health/imaging/task described). No exclusion criteria from E3–E8 apply. Conclusion: exclude because key inclusion criteria I5, I6, and I9 are not satisfied.

This fMRI study examines preparatory brain states and cognitive control mechanisms (ACC) during problem solving and reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise contrasts (insight vs noninsight), but the provided full text does not report participant age information required by inclusion criterion I10. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study of cognitive control/executive processes), I6 (within-participant contrasts of task conditions), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in tables/figures/text), I9 (task involves cognitive control/cognitive flexibility relevant to executive function). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (participant age not reported in the provided full text). No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered by the available information. Full text appears complete for methods/results/discussion, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is an event-related fMRI study using a target-detection oddball task that explicitly assesses cognitive control/executive function (target vs novel contrasts isolate task-dependent control). Analyses include within-participant contrasts (shape targets vs novels; face targets vs novels; direct comparison) at the group level using whole-brain voxelwise mixed-effects (FLAME) with reported cluster thresholds and MNI coordinates. Participants are healthy adults with reported ages (19.3–47.5), and the paper reports imaging modality and task details. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly investigates executive functions (monitoring, planning, response selection) during cooperation and competition. It uses within-subject contrasts (cooperation vs independent; competition vs independent) against an active control (independent play). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM2; voxelwise threshold, tables/figures with coordinates). Participants are healthy adults (ages 21–28), modality is fMRI, and the task paradigm is described in detail. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group only, healthy adult sample). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so is complete.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (ages 18–26) using a line-judgment paradigm with congruent vs incongruent and relative vs absolute conditions that engage attentional control/working memory. The paper includes within-participant contrasts (incongruent vs congruent; relative vs absolute), whole-brain voxelwise analyses (whole-brain corrected thresholds reported and coordinates/ROIs described), and sufficient details on participants, imaging modality, and task paradigm. Although the sample is small (N=20) and the focus includes a temperament moderator (SPS), the primary imaging analyses include task-evoked, group-level, whole-brain activation contrasts relevant to executive control/attention, meeting the meta-analysis inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI task study of executive function (overt verbal fluency) with within-subject contrasts (generation > repetition using an active control), reported at the group level with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected) and coordinates. Healthy adult volunteers are explicitly included and characterized alongside patients; imaging modality and task paradigm are described. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for meta-analysis of executive-function task activations in healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met.
